title: soilSIM Performance Improvement Plan
text: Benchmarked : 150.34s synthetic 50,000-cell raster (direct fuse_texture_group() call, bypassing network fetch). title: AWS / Van Genuchten Modeling
text: functional area covers available water storage (AWS) modeling: evaluating closed-form van Genuchten (1980) water-retention curve, Monte Carlo-simulating available water holding capacity (AWHC) ROSETTA-derived pedotransfer parameters, depth-slicing/summarizing AWHC per soil component. implemented entirely R/aws-simulation.R self-contained - unlike R/depth-simulation.R’s functions, none three functions depend -yet-ported helper (e.g. sim_component_comp()). can read, tested, used isolation rest soilSIM migration.

title: AWS / Van Genuchten Modeling
text: Purpose: Evaluates closed-form van Genuchten (1980) equation volumetric water content given matric potential. Parameters: h - Matric potential (cmH2O, typically negative). alpha, n - Van Genuchten shape parameters. theta_r, theta_s - Residual saturated volumetric water content. Returns: numeric vector volumetric water content, theta(h). Algorithm/behavior: function computes m <- 1 - (1 / n) evaluates standard closed-form van Genuchten retention equation: wrapped .numeric() strip attributes carried vectorized inputs. pure, vectorized, side-effect-free function dependence external packages - just base R arithmetic - reused directly inside simulate_vg_aws()’s row-wise Monte Carlo loop.
code: van_genuchten(h, alpha, n, theta_r, theta_s) theta(h) = theta_r + (theta_s - theta_r) / (1 + |alpha * h|^n)^m

title: AWS / Van Genuchten Modeling
text: Purpose: Monte Carlo-simulates field capacity (FC) permanent wilting point (PWP) volumetric water content - difference, available water holding capacity (AWHC) - row (soil layer/component) van Genuchten parameters. Parameters: data - data frame one row per soil layer/component, columns alpha, sd_alpha, npar, sd_npar, theta_r, sd_theta_r, theta_s, sd_theta_s, layerID - exactly shape produced soilDB::ROSETTA(..., include.sd = TRUE) plus caller-added layerID (see calculate_aws_df()). n_simulations - Number Monte Carlo draws per row (default 100). Returns: named list (one element per row, keyed paste(layerID, , sep = "_")), element data frame n_simulations draws columns alpha, n, theta_r, theta_s, sim_num, theta_fc, theta_pwp, AWHC. Rows missing van Genuchten parameter skipped entirely (absent result list, present NA rows). Algorithm/behavior: row data, function extracts mean/SD pair alpha, npar, theta_r, theta_s. four means NA, row skipped via next. Otherwise calls set.seed(123) draws n_simulations samples stats::rnorm(mean, sd) four parameters. sampled alpha n values back-transformed 10^(...) (treating sampled values log10-space draws), theta_r/theta_s samples used -. Fixed matric potentials field capacity permanent wilting point converted kPa cmH2O (1 kPa = 10.19716 cmH2O): h_fc = -33 * 10.19716 h_pwp = -1500 * 10.19716. per-draw data frame built sampled/back-transformed parameters plus sim_num, dplyr::rowwise() + dplyr::mutate() calls van_genuchten() h_fc h_pwp get theta_fc theta_pwp draw; AWHC <- theta_fc - theta_pwp computed plain vectorized column ungrouping. resulting per-row data frame stored output list key paste(data$layerID[], , sep = "_"). Ported--behavioral quirks (documented source intentional, bugs): - set.seed(123) called inside per-row loop, every row re-seeds draws identically-seeded random stream rather evolving stream across rows. means n_simulations draws row 1 row 2 (back-transformation) numerically identical underlying rnorm() output, differing row’s mean/SD. - Sampled alpha/n values back-transformed via 10^(...), .e. input data$alpha/data$npar (SDs) treated already log10 space. standard technique keeping van Genuchten shape parameters positive adding Gaussian noise, whether soilDB::ROSETTA()’s actual reported values meant interpreted way independently verified port - preserved exactly existed legacy source.

title: AWS / Van Genuchten Modeling
text: Purpose: Runs soilDB::ROSETTA() soil texture/bulk-density/water-retention inputs derive van Genuchten pedotransfer parameters, Monte Carlo-simulates AWHC per horizon via simulate_vg_aws(), depth-slices summarizes mean AWHC per component standard depth intervals via aqp::slab(). Parameters: sim_data_df - data frame one row per horizon, columns sand_total, silt_total, clay_total, bulk_density_third_bar, water_retention_third_bar, water_retention_15_bar (ROSETTA’s expected input variable names - note differ rest soilSIM’s sandtotal_r/claytotal_r/etc. SSURGO-derived naming convention, since ’re ROSETTA’s API contract), plus compname, hzdept_r, hzdepb_r, cokey. Returns: long-format data frame one row per cokey per depth slab actually spanned component’s horizons (slab boundaries per slab.structure = c(0, 5, 15, 30, 60, 100)), columns cokey, top, bottom, AWHC (mean available water holding capacity slab). tidyr::pivot_wider() step widens variable (always "AWHC" , since one property slabbed), collapse depth slabs columns - exists match aqp::slab()’s long output shape plain value-column contract. Algorithm/behavior: function first guards httr installed (requireNamespace("httr", quietly = TRUE)), since soilDB::ROSETTA() uses internally make live API call; missing, stops explicit message. calls soilDB::ROSETTA(sim_data_df, vars = variables, v = "3", include.sd = TRUE) variables fixed vector six ROSETTA input names, requesting ROSETTA model version "3" standard deviations included. layerID column constructed paste(compname, hzdept_r, sep = "_") sim_data_df copied onto rosetta_data simulate_vg_aws() can key result list. simulate_vg_aws(rosetta_data) called Monte Carlo-simulate AWHC per horizon. resulting list per-horizon simulation data frames passed Map() alongside sim_data_df’s hzdept_r, hzdepb_r, compname, cokey vectors, attaching top, bottom, compname, cokey columns element; list flattened dplyr::bind_rows() sim_aws_df. aqp::depths(sim_aws_df) <- cokey ~ top + bottom promotes data frame aqp SoilProfileCollection keyed cokey depths taken newly-attached top/bottom columns (original hzdept_r/hzdepb_r names, longer exist object). aqp::slab(sim_aws_df, fm = cokey ~ AWHC, slab.structure = c(0, 5, 15, 30, 60, 100), slab.fun = .aws_slab_mean) computes mean AWHC within fixed depth slabs (0-5, 5-15, 15-30, 30-60, 60-100 cm) per cokey, using local .aws_slab_mean() place removed aqp::mean_na(). Finally, slab output contributing_fraction column dropped pivoted wider via tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = value), remaining NA values reassigned NA (-op cleanup line preserved original source) data frame returned.

previous_headings: Core Functions > Tier 1: Exact closed-form Normal-Normal fusion
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Exact, closed-form Bayesian fusion two Normal distributions (prior likelihood) posterior Normal, via precision-weighted averaging. Parameters: prior_mu, prior_sigma - Prior mean/sd (numeric scalar vector). lik_mu, lik_sigma - Likelihood mean/sd (numeric scalar vector, length prior args). Returns: list(mu = posterior mean, sigma = posterior sd). Algorithm/behavior: Converts side’s sd precision (1 / sigma^2), sums two precisions get posterior precision (post_prec <- prior_prec + lik_prec), takes posterior sd sqrt(1 / post_prec), computes posterior mean precision-weighted average (prior_mu * prior_prec + lik_mu * lik_prec) / post_prec. standard conjugate-Normal update rule: precisions (variances) add. Documented invariants, enforced tests/testthat/test-bayesian-updating.R: posterior sigma <= min(prior_sigma, lik_sigma) (fusing two beliefs can sharpen, never widen, estimate); posterior mu bounded prior_mu lik_mu; function symmetric swapping (prior_mu, prior_sigma) (lik_mu, lik_sigma) (prior/likelihood just labels - math doesn’t care side ). fully vectorized, prior_mu/prior_sigma/lik_mu/lik_sigma can equal-length vectors elementwise fusion many quantities/cells - property R/raster-fusion.R relies apply function unchanged SpatRaster cell values.
code: bayes_update_normal_normal(prior_mu, prior_sigma, lik_mu, lik_sigma)

what: 2. normal_to_lognormal_params() - Raw-Space to Log-Space Moment Conversion
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Moment-matches raw-space Lognormal distribution’s mean/sd onto mu/sigma underlying (log-space) Normal, bayes_update_normal_normal() can reused log-space strictly-positive, right-skewed properties (e.g. SOC, CEC) fusing raw mean/sd Normal let posterior place probability mass zero. Parameters: mu, sigma - Raw-space mean/sd. Returns: list(mu = log-space mu, sigma = log-space sigma). Algorithm/behavior: Computes sigma_log <- sqrt(log(1 + (sigma / mu)^2)) mu_log <- log(mu) - sigma_log^2 / 2 - standard closed-form moment-matching formulas relating Lognormal’s raw-space mean/sd underlying Normal’s mu/sigma. caller expected fuse log-space via bayes_update_normal_normal(mu_log_prior, sigma_log_prior, mu_log_lik, sigma_log_lik) convert result back lognormal_to_normal_params().
code: normal_to_lognormal_params(mu, sigma)

what: 3. lognormal_to_normal_params() - Log-Space to Raw-Space Moment Conversion
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Inverse normal_to_lognormal_params() - converts log-space Normal(mu, sigma) parameters (e.g. posterior produced fusing log-space) back raw-space Lognormal’s mean/sd. Parameters: mu_log, sigma_log - Log-space mean/sd. Returns: list(mu = raw-space mean, sigma = raw-space sd). Algorithm/behavior: Computes mu <- exp(mu_log + sigma_log^2 / 2) sigma <- sqrt((exp(sigma_log^2) - 1) * exp(2 * mu_log + sigma_log^2)) - standard closed-form Lognormal moment formulas, exact algebraic inverse normal_to_lognormal_params().
code: lognormal_to_normal_params(mu_log, sigma_log)

what: 4. fuse_beta() - Beta-Beta Conjugate Fusion via Density Multiplication
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Exact, closed-form fusion two independent Beta belief distributions family, derived multiplying kernels: Beta(a1,b1) x Beta(a2,b2) -> Beta(a1+a2-1, b1+b2-1). Parameters: prior_alpha, prior_beta - Prior Beta shape parameters (numeric scalar vector). lik_alpha, lik_beta - Likelihood Beta shape parameters (numeric scalar vector). Returns: list(alpha = , beta = , feasible = ). Algorithm/behavior: Computes alpha <- prior_alpha + lik_alpha - 1 beta <- prior_beta + lik_beta - 1, following directly multiplying two Beta kernels x^(-1)(1-x)^(b-1) recognizing product another (unnormalized) Beta kernel. addition--shape-parameters-minus-one Beta-family analogue Tier 1’s addition Normal precisions. resulting alpha/beta must stay positive remain valid distribution, function also returns feasible flag: (prior_alpha + lik_alpha > 1) & (prior_beta + lik_beta > 1). feasible FALSE, documented fallback route re-express input Betas Normal moments via beta_to_moments(), fuse moments bayes_update_normal_normal(), convert result back moments_to_beta().
code: fuse_beta(prior_alpha, prior_beta, lik_alpha, lik_beta)

what: 5. fuse_gamma() - Gamma-Gamma Conjugate Fusion via Density Multiplication
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Exact, closed-form fusion two independent Gamma (shape/rate) belief distributions family: Gamma(k1,r1) x Gamma(k2,r2) -> Gamma(k1+k2-1, r1+r2). Parameters: prior_shape, prior_rate - Prior Gamma shape/rate parameters (numeric scalar vector). lik_shape, lik_rate - Likelihood Gamma shape/rate parameters (numeric scalar vector). Returns: list(shape = , rate = , feasible = ). Algorithm/behavior: Computes shape <- prior_shape + lik_shape - 1 rate <- prior_rate + lik_rate, derived multiplying two Gamma kernels x^(k-1)exp(-r*x) - rates add outright (like Normal precisions), shapes add minus one (like Beta’s alpha/beta). Validity requires fused shape stay positive, feasible <- (prior_shape + lik_shape > 1) returned alongside. fuse_beta(), documented infeasible-cell fallback re-express sides Normal moments via gamma_to_moments(), fuse bayes_update_normal_normal(), convert back moments_to_gamma().

Finally, n samples drawn value_grid sample(..., prob = posterior_prob, replace = TRUE). fully general (shape, family, even mismatched sides prior likelihood) considerably expensive closed-form tiers, needs raw samples rather distributional parameters sides.

title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar)
text: Purpose: Fuses two independent bivariate Normal beliefs 2D quantity (used ILR-transformed clay/sand/silt texture coordinates), direct multivariate generalization bayes_update_normal_normal()’s scalar-precision addition: precision MATRICES add instead scalar precisions. Parameters: mu1, mu2 - Length-2 mean vectors. Sigma1, Sigma2 - 2x2 covariance matrices. Returns: list(mu = fused mean vector, Sigma = fused covariance matrix). title: Data Acquisition & Processing
text: Inputs required caller: - AOI WKT string EPSG:4326 (geographic WGS84) coordinates, valid per validate_wkt_geometry() (bounded [-180,180] x [-90,90], default max area 100 deg^2, max 1000 vertices / 100 parts). - property name list drawn (resolvable via synonym ) SSURGO base names: sandtotal, claytotal, silttotal, dbovendry, ph1to1h2o, cec7, om, wthirdbar, wfifteenbar (default set), plus rfv rock fragments, handled specially throughout. - Optionally, cache_dir download caching, max_depth (cm) governing deep profile processing/infilling extends (default 250 cm throughout). Outputs produced: - download_ssurgo_tabular() → raw ssurgo_data (one row per horizon per component, _l/_r/_h columns per requested property, restriction/unsuitable-horizon flags requested) + spatial mu + metadata. - process_ssurgo_data() → processed_data (infill-ready combined data frame - cleaned, standardized column names, essential columns guaranteed, depth-filtered, sorted cokey/depth), plus separate horizon_data/component_data views quality report. - infill_soil_property() / process_soil_properties_comprehensive() → data frame shape remaining NAs suitable, -depth _r cells processed properties (extent recoverable), complete _l/_h ranges satisfying _l <= _r <= _h, unsuitable_horizon logical flag, infill_method audit-trail string per row documenting strategy filled cell. caller wiring group larger pipeline expect supply WKT + property list, treat unsuitable_horizon == TRUE rows excluded simulation inputs convention (never used infilling sources, callers may choose filter entirely via remove_unsuitable = TRUE process_soil_properties_comprehensive()).

code: # 1. Download raw SSURGO tabular data for an AOI dl <- download_ssurgo_tabular(   aoi_wkt = "POLYGON((-120.5 46.5, -120.4 46.5, -120.4 46.6, -120.5 46.6, -120.5 46.5))",   properties = c("sandtotal", "claytotal", "silttotal", "dbovendry", "om", "wthirdbar", "wfifteenbar"),   include_restrictions = TRUE,   cache_dir = "cache/ssurgo",   verbose = TRUE )  # 2. what: 1. fit_normal_triplet() / quantile_normal() - Exact closed-form Normal fit
title: Distribution Fitting & Correlation Matrices - Function Summary and Connections
text: Purpose: Fit/evaluate Normal distribution low/median/high percentile triplet. Signatures: Parameters: p_lo_val/p50_val/p_hi_val - values probabilities p_lo/0.5/p_hi; p_lo/p_hi - probabilities low/high values represent (e.g. 0.05/0.95); fit - fit_normal_triplet() result; q - vector probabilities evaluate quantile function . Returns: fit_normal_triplet() returns list(mean=, sd=); quantile_normal() returns numeric vector. Algorithm: mean simply median value; sd solved exactly two-point spread (p_hi_val - p_lo_val) / (qnorm(p_hi) - qnorm(p_lo)) - direct algebraic consequence Normal’s linear quantile function, requiring iteration.
code: fit_normal_triplet(p_lo_val, p50_val, p_hi_val, p_lo, p_hi) quantile_normal(fit, q)

what: 2. Beta fitting: fit_beta_mom() / fit_beta_mle_newton() / fit_beta_mle_newton_vec() / quantile_beta()
title: Distribution Fitting & Correlation Matrices - Function Summary and Connections
text: Purpose: Fit Beta(shape1, shape2) distribution percentile values rescaled onto [0,1] physical bounds. Signatures: Parameters: mean/var - mean variance [0,1]; values - numeric vector k percentile values raw units (one horizon); value_matrix - one row per horizon, one column per percentile (e.g. 3 columns l/r/h triplet), vectorized variant; bounds - c(lower, upper) physical bounds used rescale; n_iter - fixed Newton-Raphson iteration count (convergence check, always runs exactly n_iter steps); eps - clamp distance exact 0/1 rescaled boundary (avoids -Inf log-likelihood score percentile lands exactly bound); fit/q quantile_beta() - fit shape1/shape2, probabilities evaluate. Returns: fit_beta_mom() fit_beta_mle_newton() return list(shape1=, shape2=); fit_beta_mle_newton_vec() returns data frame columns shape1/shape2 (one row per horizon); quantile_beta() returns numeric vector via qbeta(). Algorithm: fit_beta_mom() closed-form method--moments solution, used Newton-Raphson seed. fit_beta_mle_newton() rescales values (eps, 1-eps), seeds shape parameters fit_beta_mom() (floored 0.1), runs fixed n_iter-step vectorized Newton-Raphson Beta MLE score/Hessian (closed-form digamma()/trigamma(), standard Beta MLE theory), floor-clamping updated shape 0.01. fit_beta_mle_newton_vec() identical update applied row-wise across value_matrix one pass (digamma()/trigamma() already vectorized), intended called per property across horizons rather looping scalar version. validated upstream fitdistrplus::fitdist() ~1e-3-1e-5 15 iterations.
code: fit_beta_mom(mean, var) fit_beta_mle_newton(values, bounds, n_iter = 15, eps = 1e-6) fit_beta_mle_newton_vec(value_matrix, bounds, n_iter = 15, eps = 1e-6) quantile_beta(fit, q)

what: 5. Metalog fitting: fit_metalog_linear() / quantile_metalog_linear() / check_metalog_feasible() / quantile_metalog_with_fallback()
title: Distribution Fitting & Correlation Matrices - Function Summary and Connections
text: Purpose: dependency-free (rmetalog) closed-form metalog distribution fitter, used number interior percentiles equals number desired metalog terms. Signatures: Parameters: interior_values/interior_probs - percentile values/probabilities strictly interior (0,1); bounds - c(lower, upper), required unless boundedness = "u"; boundedness - one "u" (unbounded), "sl" (semi-bounded ), "su" (semi-bounded ), "b" (bounded); fit - output fit_metalog_linear(); q - probabilities evaluate; y_grid - probability grid used probe monotonicity; infeasible - check_metalog_feasible() result fit; full_probs/full_values - FULL percentile set (including p=0/p=1 available) used fallback. Returns: fit_metalog_linear() returns list(=, term=, bounds=, boundedness=); quantile_metalog_linear() quantile_metalog_with_fallback() return numeric vectors; check_metalog_feasible() returns TRUE infeasible (non-monotonic quantile function), else FALSE. Algorithm: interior-percentile count equals metalog term count, fit exactly-determined linear system: build metalog basis matrix Y (internal metalog_basis_matrix()) interior_probs, transform interior_values unconstrained z-space per boundedness (internal metalog_to_z()), solve <- solve(Y, z) directly - optimization. validated upstream ~1e-12 rmetalog::metalog(), fast path rmetalog takes solution already feasible. quantile_metalog_linear() evaluates basis matrix q, multiplies coefficient vector, maps back z-space (metalog_from_z()). check_metalog_feasible() probes quantile function across y_grid flags non-monotonicity (equivalent implied density going negative) - cheap probe, proof. quantile_metalog_with_fallback() safety net fit_percentile_triplet()/quantile_from_fit() rely : infeasible TRUE, evaluates quantile_linear_cdf() full percentile set instead (invalid) metalog fit. Internal-helpers: metalog_basis_matrix(), metalog_to_z(), metalog_from_z() (@keywords internal) implement basis-function construction boundedness transforms meant called directly.
code: fit_metalog_linear(interior_values, interior_probs, bounds = NULL, boundedness = "u") quantile_metalog_linear(fit, q) check_metalog_feasible(fit, y_grid = seq(0.02, 0.98, by = 0.02)) quantile_metalog_with_fallback(fit, infeasible, full_probs, full_values, q)

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlation Matrices - Function Summary and Connections

text: Signatures: Parameters: clay/sand/silt - numeric vectors, units (e.g. percent), length, positions 1/2/3 partition; z1/z2 - numeric vectors ILR coordinates; total - composition’s target sum (default 100). Returns: ilr_forward() returns 2-column matrix (z1, z2); ilr_inverse() returns 3-column matrix (clay, sand, silt) summing total every row. Algorithm: ilr_forward() computes z1 = sqrt(2/3) * log(clay / sqrt(sand*silt)) z2 = sqrt(1/2) * log(sand/silt) - standard sequential-binary-partition ILR coordinates. ilr_inverse() reconstructs CLR (centered log-ratio) coordinates z1/z2, exponentiates, closes (renormalizes) total, guaranteeing every output row sums exactly total stays within [0, total] construction (softmax-like normalization can never produce negative --range share).

text: Purpose: Estimate correlation matrix real data grouped global fallbacks, porting code_ref/brdf/property_simulation.R’s simulate_soil_properties() correlation pattern. Signature: Parameters: data - data frame numeric property columns (one row per horizon), optionally grouping column named group_var; group_var - optional column name stratify (e.g. "genhz"); min_group_n - minimum complete-observation count required trust group’s (pooled data’s) empirical correlation fallback; global_fallback - optional fallback correlation matrix, defaults identity matrix data’s numeric columns; group_fallback_matrices - optional named list correlation matrices keyed group_var value, substituted group fails min_group_n instead dropping outright (contributes weighted combination nominal weight n_obs = min_group_n); global_fallback_method - label final-tier method string neither group pooled fit succeeds (defaults "global_fallback"; callers supplying non-identity global_fallback, e.g. KSSL-derived prior, override method honestly distinguishes “genuinely uninformative” “real borrowed prior”). Returns: list(matrix=, method=, n_obs=). method one "empirical_grouped", "kssl_fallback_grouped", "empirical_grouped_kssl_blended", "empirical_pooled", global_fallback_method’s value. Algorithm: internal repair_and_symmetrize() closure forces symmetry ((m + t(m))/2) , chol() fails (PD), repairs via Matrix::nearPD(m, corr = TRUE)$mat. internal compute_one() closure computes Hmisc::rcorr(..., type = "pearson")$r complete-observation rows min_group_n , discarding result NA/non-finite value rcorr() failure. group_var supplied: group, tries compute_one(); failure, falls back matching entry group_fallback_matrices (repaired/reordered data’s columns) present; groups neither dropped. surviving groups (empirical /substituted) combined one matrix via n_obs-weighted average, repaired , method set "empirical_grouped" (empirical), "kssl_fallback_grouped" (substituted), "empirical_grouped_kssl_blended" (mixed). groups qualify (group_var wasn’t supplied), falls back compute_one() pooled data (method = "empirical_pooled"). also fails, returns global_fallback method = global_fallback_method.
code: estimate_correlation_matrix_robust(data, group_var = NULL, min_group_n = 5,                                     global_fallback = NULL,                                     group_fallback_matrices = NULL,                                     global_fallback_method = "global_fallback")

text: file consolidates several “simulate distribution summary percentiles” approaches behind one dispatcher, generalizing distributions.R’s fixed 3-point (fit_percentile_triplet()) machinery arbitrary number known percentiles (e.g. P0/P5/P50/P95/P100, set). method = "metalog" deliberately offered (require rmetalog package, project avoids per validated hang/segfault history) - distributions.R’s dependency-free fit_metalog_linear() covers need instead.

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlation Matrices - Function Summary and Connections
text: Signature: Parameters: quantile_df - data frame least one row percentile-named columns (e.g. "P0", "P5", "P50"); method - one "linear_cdf" (default), "spline", "kde", "beta", "normal"; percentile_cols - candidate percentile column names look ; n - number samples draw; bounds - optional c(lower, upper), required "beta", used padding bounds "spline" given; ... - method-specific extra arguments (e.g. sample_size "kde"), filtered per-method target function’s formal argument names unrelated extras don’t cause error. Returns: numeric vector n simulated values. Algorithm/methods (implemented internal, non-exported helper shape): - extract_percentile_pairs() (internal): shared front end - parses columns named "P<num>", drops NA sentinel -1, requires >= 2 valid columns, returns sorted probs/values. - linear_cdf (sim_linear_cdf(), internal): piecewise-linear inverse-CDF via approxfun(..., rule = 2), exact knots, tails clamped. - spline (sim_spline(), internal): monotonic-spline inverse-CDF (splinefun(..., method = "monoH.FC")) smoother reconstruction still exact knots; pads 0/1 endpoints bounds (+/-5% observed range bounds NULL) P0/P100 column wasn’t already supplied. - kde (sim_kde(), internal; requires truncnorm): seeds truncated-normal draws around percentile (bandwidth neighbor spacing) build large pseudo-sample, estimates kernel density resamples density - smoothed nonparametric reconstruction. - beta (sim_beta(), internal; requires fitdistrplus; needs bounds >= 3 percentiles): rescales values [0,1] via bounds, fits Beta via fitdistrplus::fitdist(), draws rbeta() samples, rescales back. - normal (sim_normal(), internal; needs >= 3 percentiles including P50): uses P50 mean estimates SD widest available non-0/1 percentile pair (generalizing hardcoded P5/P95 assumption whatever percentiles actually present).
code: simulate_from_percentiles(quantile_df,                            method = c("linear_cdf", "spline", "kde", "beta", "normal"),                            percentile_cols = c("P0", "P5", "P50", "P95", "P100"),                            n = 1000,                            bounds = NULL,                            ...)

Returns: data frame, one row per method, mean Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic mean absolute relative mean/SD error across replicates. Algorithm: Per replicate, draws n_true ground-truth samples, computes “known” percentiles , reconstructs n_sim samples per method via simulate_from_percentiles(), scores reconstruction true draws (stats::ks.test(), relative mean/SD error); scores averaged across n_reps replicates sorted KS statistic. Used empirically justify method prefer given data shape.

text: Signature: build_kssl_fallback_matrix(properties, genhz = NULL) Parameters: properties - character vector property names build matrix , order returned matrix dimnamed; genhz - optional single genhz value (O//E/B/C/Cr; R property-matrix entry); NULL (default) pools unweighted average across every available genhz key. Returns: length(properties) x length(properties) correlation matrix dimnamed properties, NULL fewer 2 properties KSSL mapping, genhz supplied among available keys. Algorithm: Selects requested genhz’s property matrix, (genhz NULL) averages genhz matrices (valid since positive-definite matrices form convex cone - average stays positive-definite). Maps properties KSSL column names via internal .kssl_property_name_map() lookup (see ), keeping mappable, present names. fewer 2 properties map, returns NULL. Otherwise starts identity matrix dimnamed properties overlays matched KSSL principal submatrix mapped positions - properties without mapping stay identity values (deliberate partial degrade, --nothing failure). result positive-definite construction (principal submatrices PD matrix PD; block-diagonal combination PD blocks zero cross-terms PD), still passed ensure_positive_definite_matrix() defensively. Supporting internals (exported): .kssl_property_matrices() / .kssl_texture_matrices() internal accessors bundled sysdata (9x9 per-genhz property matrices; 3x3 texture-matrices, currently unused build_kssl_fallback_matrix() 9x9 property matrix’s bundled ilr1/ilr2 columns already solid eigenvalues, unlike standalone texture matrix exactly singular E/Cr/R). .kssl_property_name_map fixed lookup vector mapping soilSIM property names (dbovendry, wthirdbar, wfifteenbar, ph1to1h2o, cec7, om, rfv, ilr1, ilr2) KSSL matrix column names (db, wr_3b, wr_15b, ph, cec, soc, rfv, ilr1, ilr2) - confirmed exact lookup table built source data. Notably, om -> soc caveat: KSSL matrix’s soc column actually populated om_r (organic matter %), true lab-measured soil organic carbon, treated organic-matter proxy.

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: functional area covers two tightly coupled files. gp-modeling.R prepares NRCS/SSURGO component-horizon data fits Gaussian Process (GP) models soil property trends depth, stratified soil group (series, taxonomic class, particle-size class, etc., hierarchical fallback coarser groupings stratum sparse). multivariate-adjustment.R takes output Monte Carlo simulation (see Monte Carlo Simulation engine module) across entire dataset integrates fitted GP depth trends: every simulated cokey nudges realization depth toward GP-predicted trend using reference-quantile (“rank-preserving”) transform, depth trend becomes realistic within-depth correlation structure properties (e.g. clay vs. bulk density vs. pH) preserved rather scrambled adjusting property independently. result GP-depth-adjusted, correlation-preserving set property realizations per component (cokey), ready downstream statistical summarization validation.

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Turn raw combined NRCS component/horizon data cleaned, grouped training set ready build_stratified_gp_models(). Parameters: - nrcs_combined_data - combined NRCS data horizon component information (must contain cokey, hzdept_r). - grouping_strategy - "auto" triggers select_optimal_grouping(); otherwise one "soil_series", "taxonomic_class", "particle_size", "soil_grtgroup", "soil_suborder", "soil_order", "none". - min_profiles_per_group / min_observations_per_group - minimum distinct cokeys / total rows group must considered adequate. - target_min_groups - minimum number adequate groups auto-selector wants find accepting strategy. - max_depth - horizons hzdepb_r beyond (cm) dropped. - validation_config - quality-threshold config; defaults get_default_configuration("validation"). Returns: data frame standardized property columns (clay_pct, sand_pct, silt_pct, pH, organic_matter, bulk_density, cec, awc), soil_group column, depth_midpoint, rows belonging groups meeting min_observations_per_group. Algorithm: Runs validate_data_quality(), standardizes property names via standardize_property_names(), computes unsuitable_horizon is_unsuitable(processed_data, strict_mode = TRUE) filters horizons (|>-pipe-safe rewrite original %>% mutate(is_unsuitable(.)) pattern - see inline code comment flag must precomputed rather referenced via bare . inside mutate()), auto-selects grouping strategy requested, reconciles hzdept_r/hzdepb_r whichever depth columns populated, coalesces synonym columns eight standard property names via safe_coalesce(), assigns soil_group via create_soil_groups(), drops inadequate groups, logs processing summary.

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: original (pre-refactor) multivariate correlation-preserving adjustment routine, operating directly matrices rather long-format simulation data frames. Parameters: simulated_list - named list [depths x simulations] matrices, one per property; gp_models - named list fitted GP models (nested list(gp_model = ...) structures) per property; depths - depth vector matching matrix rows; primary_property - reference property whose surface-depth quantile ordering applied every property (defaults first property simulated_list). Returns: named list adjusted matrices, shape simulated_list. Algorithm: Validates matrices share dimensions every property corresponding GP model, predicts GP means depth (via predict_gp_depth_trends() nested models GPfit::predict.GP() directly, falling back rowMeans() prediction failure), computes ECDF primary property’s surface-depth values fix per-simulation reference quantile, depth--depth (depth 2 onward) computes GP ratio consecutive depth means, nudges simulation toward previous_value * gp_ratio reference quantile current property’s distribution, re-maps nudged values back onto current property’s original ECDF keep marginal distribution shape intact. Logs post-hoc check maximum correlation-matrix difference (original vs. adjusted) first five depths, warning exceeds 0.1. array-based sibling multivariate-adjustment.R’s preserve_correlation_structure(), operates algorithm invoked long-format integration pipeline.
code: adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP(simulated_list, gp_models, depths, primary_property = NULL)

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Quantify much depth-wise correlation matrix properties changed original_list adjusted_list (matrix-format counterparts used adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP()). Returns: data frame one row per depth (depth_idx, depth_value, max_cor_difference, mean_cor_difference, latter averaged upper triangle correlation-difference matrix). Algorithm: depth, extracts [simulations x properties] slice lists, computes cor(..., use = "complete.obs") , records max/mean absolute difference; wrapped per-depth tryCatch one bad depth abort whole validation.
code: validate_correlation_preservation(original_list, adjusted_list, depths)

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: End--end single-cokey convenience wrapper: generate Monte Carlo realizations one component, apply either NRCS GP local GP depth-trend adjustment correlation preservation, one call. Parameters: target_cokey - cokey simulate; nrcs_gp_models/cokey_mapping - fitted NRCS GP models cokey--group mapping (optional; enables NRCS-GP mode); sim_data - processed per-horizon simulation input cokey (others - filtered internally); correlation_matrices/txt_correlation_matrices - genhz-keyed (flat) correlation matrices; n_simulations - number Monte Carlo realizations; use_nrcs_gp - use NRCS GP models (defaults TRUE iff nrcs_gp_models supplied) vs. locally-fit GP models; preserve_correlations - whether run correlation-preserving adjustment path. Returns: long-format data frame enhanced simulations target_cokey, validation, n_simulations, use_nrcs_gp, preserve_correlations attached attributes (empty data frame cokey data). Algorithm: Filters sim_data target_cokey; picks single flat correlation matrix via select_simulation_correlation_matrix() (using cokey’s modal genhz group, falling back txt_correlation_matrices empirically-estimated correlations); calls generate_monte_carlo_realizations() flattens [horizon, property, realization] array long format via flatten_simulation_array_to_long(); , NRCS GP models cokey mapping supplied, looks cokey’s gp_model_group (falling back "fallback_general") calls apply_nrcs_gp_adjustments_with_correlations(), otherwise calls apply_local_gp_adjustments_with_correlations(); finally runs validate_enhanced_simulations() attaches result attribute.
code: simulate_soil_properties(   target_cokey,   nrcs_gp_models = NULL,   cokey_mapping = NULL,   sim_data,   correlation_matrices,   txt_correlation_matrices,   n_simulations = 100,   use_nrcs_gp = !is.null(nrcs_gp_models),   preserve_correlations = TRUE )

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Map every simulated cokey GP model group (build_stratified_gp_models()) used adjust depth trend. Parameters: simulated_cokeys - cokeys needing mapping; nrcs_combined_data - source NRCS data carrying taxonomic columns; gp_models - fitted models keyed property; property - property’s model groups match ; matching_strategy - currently "exact_cokey" implemented (hierarchical taxonomic matching). Returns: two-column data frame, sim_cokey gp_model_group ("pooled_model" short-circuit gp_models[[property]]$type "stratified_grouped"). Algorithm: Builds distinct lookup taxonomic columns (compname, taxclname, taxpartsize, taxgrtgroup, taxsuborder, taxorder) nrcs_combined_data, left-joins onto target cokeys, calls apply_matching_hierarchy() fill gp_model_group priority order (compname exact match -> taxclname exact match -> fallback-prefixed particle size/great group/suborder/order matches -> "fallback_general" -> "general_pool" -> first available group last resort). Logs per-group match-count summary warns still-unmatched cokeys.
code: match_soils_to_gp_models(   simulated_cokeys,   nrcs_combined_data,   gp_models,   property = "clay_pct",   matching_strategy = "exact_cokey" )

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Predict fitted GP model’s property values arbitrary new depths. Parameters: gp_model_info - model element produced fit_individual_gp_model() (contains gp_model depth_scaling); new_depths - numeric vector depths predict . Returns: Numeric vector predictions (Y_hat), length new_depths; NA-filled model info invalid prediction errors. Algorithm: Rescales new_depths [0,1] range model trained using stored depth_scaling$min/range, clamps [0,1], calls GPfit::predict.GP().
code: predict_gp_depth_trends(gp_model_info, new_depths)

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Diagnostic pass entire fitted GP model set, checking predictability, trend monotonicity, realistic value ranges. Parameters: gp_models - output build_stratified_gp_models(); nrcs_data - original training data (currently unused beyond passed ); validation_depths - depths test predictions. Returns: list model_validation (per-property, per-group prediction/diagnostic results), prediction_validation (unused/reserved), overall_assessment (total_models, valid_models, success_rate, validation_passed = success rate >= 0.8), recommendations. Algorithm: every property/group model, predicts validation_depths via predict_gp_depth_trends(), checks assess_trend_monotonicity() (>=70% depth--depth diffs share sign) assess_realistic_values() (predictions inside property-specific realistic range table, e.g. clay/sand/silt [0,100], pH [2.5,11], bulk density [0.3,3.0]), logging recommendations models fail produce unrealistic values. Minor exported/internal helpers (separately detailed ): create_soil_groups() (assigns soil_group chosen taxonomy column, "unknown" missing), create_test_grouping()/apply_hierarchical_grouping()/apply_matching_hierarchy() (grouping matching mechanics used functions ), generate_gp_processing_summary() (logging ), create_model_summary() (builds model_summary metadata block), k_fold_gp_cv() optimize_gp_hyperparameters() (k-fold CV across three GPfit correlation families - exponential power 1.95, Matern nu=3/2, Matern nu=5/2 - picking lowest mean held-RMSE; CV results attached winning model cv_results attribute), calculate_model_diagnostics() (training RMSE log-likelihood), assess_trend_monotonicity()/assess_realistic_values() (used validate_gp_models()), infer_simulation_properties() (numeric, non-structural columns long-format simulation data frame), apply_nrcs_gp_adjustments_with_correlations() / apply_local_gp_adjustments_with_correlations() (thin wrappers infer properties argument delegate multivariate-adjustment.R’s apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments() / apply_local_gp_adjustments()), validate_enhanced_simulations() (row-count-match check used simulate_soil_properties()), select_simulation_correlation_matrix() flatten_simulation_array_to_long() (Monte Carlo input-shaping helpers simulate_soil_properties()), export_gp_models()/load_gp_models() (RDS-based persistence fitted GP model set, optionally stripping training data shrink file size).
code: validate_gp_models(gp_models, nrcs_data, validation_depths = seq(0, 200, by = 10))

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Whole-dataset entry point applies GP depth-trend adjustment (NRCS-model-based /locally-fit) every cokey Monte Carlo simulation result, validation rich metadata. Parameters: simulation_results - output generate_monte_carlo_realizations() (must simulation_data element); gp_models - fitted NRCS GP models build_stratified_gp_models() (optional); cokey_mapping - output match_soils_to_gp_models() (optional); integration_method - "nrcs_gp" (NRCS models ), "local_gp" (per-cokey local GP ), "hybrid" (NRCS adjustment followed local GP adjustment); preserve_correlations - whether run correlation-preserving quantile transform; properties - properties adjust, NULL auto-detect via detect_simulation_properties(); parallel/n_cores - parallel dispatch across cokeys; config - Module 8-style config, defaults get_default_configuration("full"). Returns: list: integrated_data (final adjusted long-format data frame), original_simulation_data, integration_metadata (method, properties processed, success rate, processing time, package versions, etc.), validation_results (validate_integration_results()), original_metadata; also carries success_rate, processing_time, validation_passed attributes. Algorithm: Validates parameters simulation-data quality, auto-detects/validates properties, decides use_nrcs_gp/use_local_gp integration_method whether GP models/mapping supplied, dispatches per-cokey work process_cokeys_parallel() process_cokeys_sequential() (calling process_single_cokey(), applies apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments() /apply_local_gp_adjustments() per cokey inside tryCatch), combines successful per-cokey results combine_and_validate_results(), runs validate_integration_results(), packages everything via create_integration_results().
code: integrate_monte_carlo_with_gp(   simulation_results,   gp_models = NULL,   cokey_mapping = NULL,   integration_method = "hybrid",   preserve_correlations = TRUE,   properties = NULL,   parallel = FALSE,   n_cores = NULL,   config = NULL )

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: Core single-cokey routine reshapes long-format simulation rows matrices, applies GP-trend adjustment (correlation-preserving independent), reshapes back. Parameters: cokey_data - long-format rows one cokey; gp_predictions - named list depth-indexed GP mean predictions per property; properties - properties adjust; preserve_correlations - use preserve_correlation_structure() (>=2 properties) vs. apply_individual_adjustments(); primary_property - reference property quantile ordering (defaults first available property). Returns: cokey_data adjusted property columns merged back (unchanged fewer 2 rows, fewer 2 valid depths, properties overlap gp_predictions). Algorithm: Filters valid depths, builds [depth x simulation] matrices via convert_to_property_matrices(), adjusts via preserve_correlation_structure() apply_individual_adjustments(), converts result back long format via convert_to_long_format(), merges adjusted values cokey_data via merge_adjusted_data() (matched hzdept_r + simulation_number). Every stage wrapped tryCatch/handle_workflow_error() failure step degrades returning unmodified/partially-modified data rather aborting.
code: apply_gp_depth_trends(   cokey_data,   gp_predictions,   properties,   preserve_correlations = TRUE,   primary_property = NULL )

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment
text: Purpose: production correlation-preserving depth-adjustment algorithm (long-format pipeline’s counterpart gp-modeling.R’s adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP()). Parameters: property_matrices - named list [depth x simulation] matrices; gp_predictions - named list per-depth GP mean vectors; depths - depth vector; primary_property - reference property (falls back first property missing property_matrices). Returns: Named list adjusted matrices, shape property_matrices. Algorithm: Computes ECDF primary property’s surface-depth (depths[1]) values fix per-simulation reference_quantiles; property matching, depth-length GP prediction vector, walks depths 2..n computing safety-clamped GP ratio (calculate_safe_gp_ratio(), clamped [0.1, 10]), nudges simulation toward previous_adjusted_value * gp_ratio reference quantile within current property’s current-depth distribution (apply_quantile_adjustment()), remaps nudged values back onto current property’s original ECDF (correct_distribution_shape()) preserve marginal shape. Properties lacking usable GP prediction passed unchanged.
code: preserve_correlation_structure(property_matrices, gp_predictions, depths, primary_property)

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment

code: # 1. Prepare NRCS training data and fit stratified GP depth-trend models nrcs_training <- prepare_nrcs_training_data(   nrcs_combined_data,   grouping_strategy = "auto",   max_depth = 200 )  gp_models <- build_stratified_gp_models(   nrcs_training,   properties = c("clay_pct", "sand_pct", "pH", "organic_matter"),   optimize_hyperparameters = TRUE )  # 2. Map the Monte Carlo simulation's cokeys onto GP model groups cokey_mapping <- match_soils_to_gp_models(   simulated_cokeys = unique(mc_results$simulation_data$cokey),   nrcs_combined_data = nrcs_combined_data,   gp_models = gp_models,   property = "clay_pct" )  # 3. Integrate the Monte Carlo output with the fitted GP models, preserving correlations integrated <- integrate_monte_carlo_with_gp(   simulation_results = mc_results,   gp_models = gp_models,   cokey_mapping = cokey_mapping,   integration_method = "hybrid",   preserve_correlations = TRUE,   parallel = TRUE )  final_realizations <- integrated$integrated_data

what: 9. fuse_observed_data_into_priors() - Bayesian Fusion of Observed Data (optional)
title: Monte Carlo Simulation
text: Purpose: Orchestrates Bayesian updating property’s per-horizon prior (prepare_simulation_parameters()) caller-supplied observed-data likelihood, using bayesian-updating.R’s pure fusion primitives. Signature: Parameters: - simulation_params - Per-horizon parameter list prepare_simulation_parameters(). - simulation_data - filtered per-horizon data frame (row order simulation_params). - sim_properties - Property vector simulation_params keyed (may include ILR pseudo-properties). - properties - Caller-facing original property vector (kept interface symmetry; used directly). - observed_data - Named list keyed property name; texture entries supplied jointly claytotal/sandtotal/silttotal. - composition_plan - Result resolve_composition_groups(). - config - Simulation configuration. Returns: simulation_params fused entries replaced place (unfused entries pass unchanged). Behavior: Two parts. (1) Texture (composition group) fusion: three texture members present observed_data, reduced c(low, rep, high) triplet (via internal as_lrh_triplet() - accepting named low/rep/high l/r/h triplets, unnamed length-3 vector, raw sample vector reduced via empirical quantiles lh_percentile), fuse_texture_group_from_triplets() called per horizon (horizon’s clay/sand/silt _l/_r/_h prior side, shared observed triplet likelihood side), replacing simulation_params[[]][["ilr1"]]/[["ilr2"]]. Partial texture entries (1-2 3) skip texture fusion logged WARN. (2) Ordinary property fusion: every non-texture property present observed_data sim_properties, horizon’s prior fused via internal fuse_one_property_prior() helper shared observed likelihood (every horizon keeps prior shares one likelihood, since field/lab measurements aren’t usually tied individual simulated horizons). Two supported likelihood shapes: raw numeric sample vector routes fully general fuse_property() grid-KDE path (prior first sampled via quantile_from_fit(), posterior stored exact empirical quantile function family = "linear_cdf"); family-native parameter list (list(mean=, sd=) list(shape1=, shape2=)/list(mean=, var=)) routes closed-form bayes_fuse()-based path, supported prior families normal/lognormal/beta (families conjugate route) - prior family skips fusion (horizon, property) logged WARN. Note: narrows property’s marginal prior spread; touch cross-property correlation/dependency structure, estimate_property_correlations() estimates separately raw representative values. Minor related internal helpers (exported, @keywords internal): - as_lrh_triplet(x, lh_probs) - reduces observed_data entry unnamed c(low, rep, high) triplet. - fuse_one_property_prior(prior, likelihood, is_vector_likelihood, n_samples, supported_closed_form, prop, horizon_index) - implements per-property closed-form/general dispatch described , handling normal, lognormal (converts raw-space likelihood log-space via normal_to_lognormal_params() fusing, since lognormal prior fit already stored log-space), beta (rescales raw-scale likelihood mean/var onto prior’s [lower, upper] support fitting moments, since fuse_beta()’s alpha/beta addition requires shared support; falls back Normal-moments round-trip via bayes_update_normal_normal() direct beta fusion infeasible).

title: Monte Carlo Simulation
text: Purpose: actual correlated-random-number-generation engine: every horizon, generates n_realizations correlated draws across properties using Gaussian (Cholesky) copula property’s fitted quantile function. Signature: Parameters: - simulation_params - List containing simulation parameters horizon. - correlation_matrix - Correlation matrix properties (identity used NULL). - n_realizations - Number realizations generate. - properties - Character vector property names. - config - Configuration settings (used incidentally ; property’s family travels fitted params). Returns: [horizon, property, realization] numeric array (dimnamed accordingly). Behavior: Initializes result array; defaults/repairs correlation matrix (ensure_positive_definite_matrix(), validate_correlation_matrix() check falls back identity failure); Cholesky-decomposes (chol()). Per horizon: draws independent uniform matrix (n_properties x n_realizations), transforms standard normal (qnorm), applies correlation structure (chol_matrix %*% normal_matrix), transforms back correlated uniforms (pnorm), property calls distributions.R’s quantile_from_fit() property’s resolved family/fit (family travels params - config$monte_carlo$distribution_type ever consulted upstream fallback, never ) get final simulated values. Missing per-property parameters yield NA property/horizon. Reports progress via track_progress() finishes validate_simulated_array() finite-rate check.

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: pipeline soilSIM’s core-vs-adapter architecture made concrete. generic fusion core (R/distribution-fitting-raster.R, R/raster-fusion.R, R/raster-cache.R) implements distribution fitting, Bayesian prior/likelihood fusion, disk caching purely terms terra::SpatRaster percentile-value inputs — knowledge SSURGO, SOLUS, specific data source, fuse prior/likelihood SpatRaster pair sharing common probability grid. Two adapters currently plug core shared area interest (AOI): R/ssurgo-simulation.R supplies prior side (SSURGO map units, Monte Carlo-simulated per-cell percentiles), R/solus-simulation.R supplies likelihood side (SOLUS100’s published low/prediction/high percentiles, fetched directly). Neither adapter special-cased core: simply produce list(values = <named list percentile-value SpatRasters>, probs = <matching probabilities>) structure, fuse_property_adaptive() requires either side. deliberate: future data source (e.g. HWSD, SoilGrids) plug new adapter supplying either prior likelihood side — , fusing two entirely new sources — without change fitting/fusion/caching core .

text: Purpose: Fit Normal distribution’s mu/sigma rasters three percentile-value rasters (low/median/high), evaluate fitted distribution target quantile — pure raster arithmetic, EXACT relative closed-form Normal quantile formula. Parameters: Returns: fit_normal_raster() returns list(mu = SpatRaster, sigma = SpatRaster); quantile_normal_raster() returns single SpatRaster quantile values. Behavior: mu simply median raster; sigma (p_hi_r - p_lo_r) / (qnorm(p_hi) - qnorm(p_lo)), .e. value-per-z-unit spacing implied two tail percentiles. Evaluation mu + sigma * qnorm(q). single arithmetic expressions across whole raster, cost independent q many times fitted fit re-queried.
code: fit_normal_raster(p_lo_r, p50_r, p_hi_r, p_lo, p_hi) # p_lo_r, p50_r, p_hi_r - SpatRasters for the low/median/high percentile values # p_lo, p_hi            - the probabilities p_lo_r/p_hi_r represent (e.g. 0.025/0.975)  quantile_normal_raster(fit, q) # fit - output of fit_normal_raster() # q   - target quantile probability

text: Purpose: Method--moments Beta fit — APPROXIMATE relative MLE, used Newton-Raphson seed fit_beta_mle_newton_raster() (intended standalone fit). Parameters: Returns: fit_beta_mom_raster() returns list(alpha = SpatRaster, beta = SpatRaster); quantile_beta_mom_raster() returns SpatRaster (via terra::lapp() calling stats::qbeta() per cell, since qbeta() raster-native form). Behavior: common <- mean*(1-mean)/var - 1; alpha = mean*common, beta = (1-mean)*common — standard closed-form Beta method--moments identity, applied elementwise.

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Fit Beta distribution’s (alpha, beta) via vectorized Newton-Raphson MLE across entire raster — fitdistrplus::fitdist()‘s generic optim()-based MLE vectorized form, exploits Beta log-likelihood’s known closed-form score/Hessian terms digamma()/trigamma() (vectorized base-R functions) update cells’ estimates simultaneously per iteration. Validated upstream fitdistrplus::fitdist() ~1e-3–1e-5. Parameters: Returns: list(alpha = SpatRaster, beta = SpatRaster); quantile function returns SpatRaster (via terra::lapp() + qbeta()). Behavior: Values rescaled [eps, 1-eps] within bounds (clamping cells land exactly 0/1, log(x)/log(1-x) -Inf). Beta method--moments fit seeds (alpha, beta), clamped 0.1 floor. n_iter iterations computes digamma/trigamma rasters alpha, beta, alpha+beta, forms 2x2 score vector (S1, S2) Hessian (H11, H12, H21, H22), solves 2x2 linear system closed form (det, d_alpha, d_beta), updates alpha_r/beta_r 0.01 floor. Two internal (non-exported) helpers, raster_digamma()/raster_trigamma(), wrap terra::app() around base R’s digamma/trigamma.
code: fit_beta_mle_newton_raster(value_rasters, bounds, n_iter = 15, eps = 1e-6) # value_rasters - list of percentile-value SpatRasters (any count >= 3) # bounds        - c(lower, upper) physical bounds # n_iter        - fixed Newton-Raphson iteration count (validated sufficient at 15 upstream) # eps           - clamp epsilon away from the exact 0/1 rescaled boundary  quantile_beta_mle_newton_raster(fit, q) # fit - output of fit_beta_mle_newton_raster() # q   - target quantile probability

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Run complete prior-fetch → likelihood-fetch → align → fuse pipeline one property/depth window AOI, disk caching every fetch step. Parameters: Returns: list(prior=, likelihood=, posterior=, dist=, dist_source=, skew_proxy=, route=, route_detail=, n_fallback_cells=), NULL SSURGO SOLUS side failed. posterior’s shape depends dist — see fuse_property_adaptive(). Behavior: property_config$composition_group set, delegates entirely run_stage1_fusion_group() slices property’s result. Otherwise: builds cache key via build_cache_key(..., "ssurgo"), checks cache_get()/unwrap_percentile_list(), miss calls fetch_ssurgo_percentiles() caches result (wrap_percentile_list() first, per raster-cache.R’s known limitation); repeats cache--fetch pattern SOLUS side via fetch_solus_percentiles() kind "solus". SSURGO prior (~30 m, mukey.wcs()) SOLUS likelihood (100 m) sit different grids, prior terra::resample(..., method = "bilinear")’d onto SOLUS grid fusion, since every fusion route requires cell-aligned rasters. Finally calls fuse_property_adaptive() aligned prior SOLUS likelihood, returns raw sides plus fused posterior.
code: run_stage1_fusion(aoi_vect, property_config, top_depth, bottom_depth,                    composition_groups = NULL, property_configs = NULL) # aoi_vect            - a terra::SpatVector AOI (projected, e.g. EPSG:5070) # property_config     - list with id (used as fetch_ssurgo_percentiles()'s property id and as #                        the cache key), solus_variable (a soilDB::fetchSOLUS()-recognized #                        variable name), and dist/bounds/boundedness/auto_skew_threshold/ #                        composition_group as needed by fuse_property_adaptive() # top_depth, bottom_depth - numeric depth bounds in cm # composition_groups, property_configs - only needed when property_config$composition_group #                        is set; passed through to run_stage1_fusion_group()

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Run fetch → align → fuse pipeline run_stage1_fusion(), whole compositional group (currently "texture": clay/sand/silt) jointly, since independent fusion per member measurably breaks sum--100. Parameters: Returns: named list keyed member id, element list(posterior = list(value=, ilr_mu=, ilr_Sigma=), dist = "texture_ilr", route = "closed_form_ilr_group", route_detail = NULL, n_fallback_cells = 0) — uniform (mu,sigma)/(alpha,beta) contract non-compositional properties get — NULL member’s SSURGO/SOLUS fetch failed. Behavior: Resolves member ids via group_members(). Checks group-level cache entry (kind "texture_group") first; miss, fetches member’s SSURGO prior SOLUS likelihood (cache--fetch, exactly run_stage1_fusion(), one "ssurgo"/"solus" cache entry per member later single-property request still hits cache), resamples member’s prior onto SOLUS grid, — every member’s fetch succeeded — calls fuse_texture_group() whole group. joint result cached group key, member’s posterior also seeded per-property "posterior" cache kind, three sequential run_stage1_fusion() calls clay, sand, silt trigger joint fetch+fusion exactly , three times.
code: run_stage1_fusion_group(aoi_vect, group, composition_groups, property_configs,                          top_depth, bottom_depth) # aoi_vect                 - a terra::SpatVector AOI # group                    - a composition group name (e.g. "texture") # composition_groups       - a config$monte_carlo$composition_groups-shaped list (see #                             group_members()) giving this group's member ids in order # property_configs         - a named list, keyed by each member id composition_groups lists, #                             of per-member config lists (each needs at least id/solus_variable) # top_depth, bottom_depth  - numeric depth bounds in cm

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Build deterministic, filename-safe cache key one AOI/property/depth-window/kind combination, default cache max-age (30 days) used throughout pipeline. Parameters: Returns: character string, safe use filename. Behavior: Extracts AOI’s WKT geometry (terra::geom(aoi_vect, wkt = TRUE)[1]), hashes via digest::digest(), concatenates "raster_" prefix, first 12 hash characters, id, top_depth, bottom_depth, kind, sanitizes character outside [-Za-z0-9_-] underscore.
code: build_cache_key(aoi_vect, id, top_depth, bottom_depth, kind) # aoi_vect               - a terra::SpatVector (single-feature AOI) # id                     - a property id or composition-group name (e.g. "ph", "texture") # top_depth, bottom_depth - numeric depth bounds in cm # kind                   - a short string distinguishing what's cached for this key #                          (e.g. "ssurgo", "solus", "texture_group", "posterior")  CACHE_TTL_SECONDS  # = 30 * 24 * 3600 (30 days)

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Retrieve/store cached value key, tools::R_user_dir("soilSIM", "cache") (standard R >= 4.0 per-package cache location) — general disk-cache mechanism every adapter orchestrator uses. Parameters: Returns: cache_get() returns cached value, NULL cache miss/stale entry/read failure. cache_set() returns TRUE success, FALSE write failure (never errors). Behavior: cache_get() checks file existence, computes age file.mtime(), returns NULL stale missing, otherwise readRDS()s (wrapped tryCatch). cache_set() creates cache directory needed saveRDS()s value (wrapped tryCatch) — see Known Limitations SpatRaster wrap/unwrap caveat function callers must handle manually.
code: cache_get(key, ttl_seconds = CACHE_TTL_SECONDS) # key         - a cache key from build_cache_key() # ttl_seconds - maximum cache age in seconds before a hit is treated as stale  cache_set(key, kind, value) # key   - a cache key from build_cache_key() # kind  - unused beyond documenting intent at call sites (matches the original bundle's #         3-argument calling convention) - the value is stored keyed only by key, since #         build_cache_key() already encodes kind # value - the R object to cache (anything saveRDS() can serialize)

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Orchestrate full SSURGO Monte Carlo pipeline one AOI/depth window — fetch tabular SSURGO data, infill, simulate, adjust, aggregate — producing replicate-level draws fetch_ssurgo_percentiles() summarizes percentile rasters. Parameters: Returns: data frame, one row per mukey/cokey/simulation_number replicate, simulated property columns aggregated depth window — NULL tabular fetch fails. Behavior: Reprojects aoi_vect EPSG:4326 first (download_ssurgo_tabular()’s aoi_wkt argument hardcoded assume lon/lat, regardless aoi_vect’s actual CRS — extracting WKT directly already-projected AOI, e.g. EPSG:5070, silently mislabel meter coordinates degrees). Checks "ssurgo_tabular"-kind disk cache first; miss, calls R/ssurgo-acquisition.R’s download_ssurgo_tabular() unwraps $ssurgo_data, caching data frame directly (wrap() needed — ’s tabular, raster). : infill_soil_data(); removes organic horizons (remove_organic_layer()) hzname contains "O"; derives genhz via classify_genhz(); simulates component composition via sim_component_comp() left-joins sim_comppct back onto horizon data cokey; loads KSSL reference correlation matrices via .kssl_property_matrices()/.kssl_texture_matrices() (already built R/sysdata.rda, re-read raw files runtime); per unique cokey, calls simulate_cokey_generalized() (wrapped tryCatch, skipping messaging per-cokey failure) row-binds results; applies maybe_adjust_soil_data_depth_trend() property columns SSURGO_SIM_PROPERTY_COLUMNS; finally aggregates requested depth window via aggregate_depth_window_by_replicate().

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: Merge per-mukey percentile-value table onto mukey raster, producing one SpatRaster per percentile column. Parameters: Returns: named list single-layer terra::SpatRasters, one per percentile column. Behavior: Reads raster’s factor category table (terra::cats()), whose first column internal numeric factor ID (must stay first, since levels<- requires ) whose second column holds mukey codes character. Left-joins (dplyr::left_join(), deliberately base merge(), reorders join column front break “ID must stay first” requirement) percentile columns onto category table mukey column, reassigns levels(mukey_raster) <- merged, calls terra::catalyze() expand categorical raster one continuous layer per joined percentile column, returned named list.
code: rasterize_mukey_percentiles(mukey_raster, percentile_by_mukey) # mukey_raster        - a categorical (factor) mukey terra::SpatRaster from #                       fetch_ssurgo_mukey_raster() # percentile_by_mukey - a data frame with a mukey column and one column per percentile #                       (e.g. P05, P25, P50, P75, P95)

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: Purpose: top-level SSURGO “prior” entry point fuse_property_adaptive(): rasterizes map units, Monte Carlo-simulates requested property, returns per-cell percentile-value rasters list(values=, probs=) shape fusion core expects. Parameters: Returns: list(values = <named list percentile-value SpatRasters>, probs = probs), NULL mukey raster Monte Carlo draws unavailable AOI. Behavior: Calls fetch_ssurgo_mukey_raster() (returning NULL early fails), simulate_ssurgo_mapunit_draws() replicate-level Monte Carlo draws. Maps property_id simulated column via property_to_sim_column(), computes stats::quantile(..., probs = probs) per mukey group, reshapes mukey + one-column-per-percentile data frame, rasterizes via rasterize_mukey_percentiles().
code: fetch_ssurgo_percentiles(aoi_vect, property_id, top_depth, bottom_depth,                           probs = c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95), n_mc = 1000) # aoi_vect                 - a terra::SpatVector AOI # property_id              - one of property_to_sim_column()'s recognized ids # top_depth, bottom_depth  - numeric depth window bounds in cm # probs                    - percentile probabilities to compute # n_mc                     - number of triangular draws per component (default 1000)

text: Purpose: Snap [top_depth, bottom_depth] depth window nearest native SOLUS depth slice, since soilDB::fetchSOLUS()’s depth_slices single depth points, ranges. New design port (referenced never defined source ported ) — simplest representative-point choice otherwise point-based data source. Parameters: Returns: single numeric value available_slices. text: Purpose: Fetch SOLUS100’s low/prediction/high rasters one variable depth window — raw three-way fetch underlying fetch_solus_percentiles(). text: Purpose: top-level SOLUS “likelihood” entry point fuse_property_adaptive(). Parameters: Returns: list(values = list(P025 = <low raster>, P50 = <pred raster>, P975 = <high raster>), probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)), NULL low/pred/high unavailable. title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: External packages: - terra — used throughout every file pipeline (SpatRaster/SpatVector arithmetic, terra::app()/terra::lapp()/terra::ifel()/terra::rasterize()/terra::resample()/ terra::catalyze()/terra::wrap()/terra::unwrap()). - soilDB::fetchSOLUS() — live network API solus-simulation.R’s fetch_solus_low_pred_high() calls SOLUS100 low/prediction/high rasters. - soilDB::mukey.wcs() / soilDB::SDA_spatialQuery() — live network APIs ssurgo-simulation.R’s fetch_ssurgo_mukey_raster() calls SSURGO map unit grids/polygons. - digest — raster-cache.R’s build_cache_key() hashes AOI’s WKT via digest::digest(). - dplyr — used throughout SSURGO adapter grouping/joining/summarizing (dplyr::group_by()/left_join()/summarise()/group_modify()). - GPfit (optional) — guarded requireNamespace() maybe_adjust_soil_data_depth_trend(); skipped warning unavailable. soilSIM dependencies: - R/distributions.R — distribution-fitting-raster.R directly reuses metalog_basis_matrix()/metalog_to_z()/metalog_from_z() unchanged, since ’re pure elementwise arithmetic already works SpatRaster inputs (confirmed dedicated smoke test file written, merely assumed); raster-fusion.R’s fuse_texture_group() similarly reuses estimate_ilr_moments_mc()/ilr_inverse() directly, resolve_composition_groups()’s composition-group config convention reused rather duplicated. - R/bayesian-updating.R — raster-fusion.R reuses bayes_update_normal_normal(), fuse_beta(), fuse_gamma(), moments_to_gamma()/moments_to_beta()/beta_to_moments()/gamma_to_moments(), normal_to_lognormal_params()/lognormal_to_normal_params(), bayesian_update(), fuse_bivariate_normal() directly, unmodified — pure elementwise arithmetic, already work unchanged SpatRaster inputs exactly plain numerics. - R/property-simulation.R — feeds SSURGO adapter’s Monte Carlo step: sim_component_comp() simulate_cokey_generalized() called directly simulate_ssurgo_mapunit_draws(). - R/ssurgo-acquisition.R — download_ssurgo_tabular() called simulate_ssurgo_mapunit_draws() underlying tabular SSURGO fetch (cached separately raster-fusion cache’s "ssurgo"/"solus" kinds, "ssurgo_tabular" kind). - R/data-infilling.R — infill_soil_property() called infill_soil_data(). - R/kssl-reference-correlations.R — .kssl_property_matrices()/.kssl_texture_matrices() (already built R/sysdata.rda) classify_genhz() called simulate_ssurgo_mapunit_draws(). - R/multivariate-adjustment.R — apply_local_gp_adjustments() called maybe_adjust_soil_data_depth_trend(). - R/monte-carlo.R — simulate_from_percentiles() called (per cell, inside terra::app()) fuse_general_kde(). run_stage1_fusion()/run_stage1_fusion_group() (R/raster-fusion.R) top-level AOI orchestrators tying together — single entry points caller (e.g. Shiny app batch script) needs, hiding fetch/cache/align/fuse sequence behind one call per property (per compositional group) per AOI/depth window.

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: : - AOI, terra::SpatVector (projected, e.g. EPSG:5070). - property config (property_config): id, solus_variable, dist ("normal"/"beta"/ "gamma"/"lognormal"/"metalog"/"auto"), optionally bounds/boundedness/ auto_skew_threshold/composition_group. - Depth window bounds (top_depth/bottom_depth, cm). - compositional properties: composition-group config (composition_groups, config$monte_carlo$composition_groups shape) per-member property_configs list. : - single, non-compositional property: fused posterior SpatRaster set (family-native parameter rasters — mu/sigma, alpha/beta, shape/rate — per resolved dist), plus raw prior/likelihood rasters, routing diagnostics (route, route_detail, n_fallback_cells), distribution-resolution diagnostics (dist, dist_source, skew_proxy) — run_stage1_fusion(). - compositional group: member’s fused texture posterior (value point-estimate raster plus shared ilr_mu/ilr_Sigma rasters posterior sampling) — run_stage1_fusion_group(). - Intermediate cached artifacts disk (tools::R_user_dir("soilSIM", "cache")): raw SSURGO tabular data, SSURGO/SOLUS percentile rasters (terra::wrap()ped), texture-group fusion results, per-property posterior results, keyed AOI + id + depth window + kind via build_cache_key().

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
text: metalog_moments_raster() new, less-validated glue code (R/raster-fusion.R). Unlike rest pipeline’s math — validated upstream fitdistrplus/closed-form references — mean/variance-via-quadrature computation metalog_moments_raster() prior validated version. Per original source bundle’s caveat, spot-checked real data trusted production. SpatRaster/SpatVector objects survive plain saveRDS()/readRDS() round-trip (R/raster-cache.R). objects hold external pointer -memory/-disk GDAL state. cache_get()/cache_set() wrap/unwrap automatically, since every cached value raster (e.g. Monte Carlo draw data frames aren’t). Callers caching raster values must call terra::wrap() cache_set() terra::unwrap() cache_get() — exactly wrap_percentile_list()/unwrap_percentile_list() list(values=<SpatRasters>, probs=) percentile shape, run_stage1_fusion()/ run_stage1_fusion_group() call around every SSURGO/SOLUS cache read write.

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion Pipeline
code: library(terra)  # AOI, already projected (e.g. EPSG:5070) aoi_vect <- vect("aoi_polygon.gpkg")  # --- Using the top-level orchestrator (fetches + caches both sides internally) --- result <- run_stage1_fusion(   aoi_vect = aoi_vect,   property_config = list(id = "clay", solus_variable = "claytotal", dist = "auto"),   top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 30 ) if (!is.null(result)) {   posterior_mu    <- result$posterior$mu     # or $alpha/$beta, or $shape/$rate, per result$dist   posterior_sigma <- result$posterior$sigma   writeRaster(posterior_mu, "clay_posterior_mean_0_30cm.tif", overwrite = TRUE) }  # --- Using fuse_property_adaptive() directly with pre-fetched percentile rasters --- ssurgo_prior <- fetch_ssurgo_percentiles(aoi_vect, "clay", top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 30) solus_lik    <- fetch_solus_percentiles(aoi_vect, "claytotal", top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 30)  # Align the SSURGO (~30m) prior onto the SOLUS (100m) grid before fusing. prior_aligned <- lapply(ssurgo_prior$values, resample, y = solus_lik$values[[1]], method = "bilinear")  fused <- fuse_property_adaptive(   prior_value_rasters = prior_aligned, prior_probs = ssurgo_prior$probs,   lik_value_rasters   = solus_lik$values, lik_probs = solus_lik$probs,   property_config     = list(dist = "beta", bounds = c(0, 100)) )  cat("route:", fused$route, "\n") plot(fused$posterior$alpha)

title: soilSIM: Architecture Overview
text: soilSIM simulates soil properties fuses estimates multiple soil data products uncertainty. core statistical machinery - percentile-triplet arbitrary-percentile distribution fitting, correlated Monte Carlo simulation, Gaussian-process depth-trend modeling, Bayesian updating/fusion (scalar raster-native) - data-source-agnostic design: operates low/representative/high triplet prior/likelihood pair, regardless numbers came . SSURGO SOLUS100 two concrete data-source adapters wired today, supplying prior likelihood sides (respectively) raster fusion pipeline. architecture deliberately split way future data sources (e.g. HWSD, SoilGrids) can plug new adapters alongside SSURGO/SOLUS, reusing simulation/fusion core rather duplicating . See soilSIM/R/soilSIM-package.R (rendered ?soilSIM) package-level roxygen summary framing. directory’s 10 documents go one level deeper package doc per-function .Rd/roxygen reference: covers functional group’s full function signatures, internal call graphs, cross-file dependencies, data flow, known limitations - depth legacy modules/mod0-8_summary.md docs provided pre-package prototype, adapted soilSIM’s current (larger, restructured) R/ layout.

title: Profile, Component & Depth Simulation
text: functional group covers two source files together simulate compositional morphological variability SSURGO soil components profiles. R/property-simulation.R simulates component-composition percentages (sim_component_comp()) per-cokey correlated soil properties - including compositional sand/silt/clay texture via package’s ILR core - low/representative/high (_l/_r/_h) triplets (simulate_cokey_generalized(), built simulate_correlated_triangular()). R/depth-simulation.R simulates horizon depths, horizon-thickness variability, boundary distinctness whole aqp::SoilProfileCollection profiles, using OSD (Official Series Description) data inform boundary perturbation, sequential, parallel (future/future.apply), -mukey orchestration entry points. files ported code_ref/brdf/property_simulation.R code_ref/brdf/depth_simulation.R respectively; also two smaller, standalone-horizon-data helpers remove_organic_layer() slice_and_aggregate_soil_data() (property-simulation.R), tied compositional-simulation machinery shipped legacy file.

title: Profile, Component & Depth Simulation
text: Parameters: df - data frame horizon rows cokey, hzname, hzdept_r, hzdepb_r, optionally hzdept_l, hzdepb_l, hzdept_h, hzdepb_h. Returns: data frame organic horizons removed remaining depths re-anchored 0 within cokey group. Behavior: Groups cokey; within group, drops rows whose hzname contains capital “O”, shifts low/high depth columns (hzdep*_l/hzdep*_h) first remaining horizon’s original hzdept_r stay consistent, zeroes low/high top-depth value lands exactly new top horizon, recomputes hzdept_r/ hzdepb_r (low/high pairs, present entirely NA) cumulative sums original horizon thicknesses - preserving horizon’s thickness removing organic layer’s contribution depth.

title: Profile, Component & Depth Simulation
text: n - integer, number samples generate. params - list c(, b, c) triples, one per distribution, (lower, mode, upper) order - note differs tri_dist()’s (= lower, b = upper, c = mode) argument convention; preserved exactly legacy source defines . correlation_matrix - square, positive-semi-definite correlation matrix, length(params) x length(params). random_seed - optional integer seed reproducibility. Returns: n-row x length(params)-column matrix correlated samples. Behavior: Draws n * k independent standard normal values (mathematically equivalent MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = rep(0, k), Sigma = diag(k)), MASS dependency used), correlates via chol(correlation_matrix), converts correlated-normal column uniform via stats::pnorm(), inverts standard triangular- distribution CDF analytically (branching whether u falls mode’s CDF value) map column onto (, b, c) triangular distribution. c == given parameter, column filled constant (degenerate triangular).

Groups stacked results hzname computes sd(Thickness) (rounded 2 decimals) per horizon, merges back onto horizon’s representative hzdept_r/hzdepb_r (renamed top/bottom) original input. variability-estimation pass, distinct perturbation applied downstream simulate_and_perturb_soil_profiles().

text: Parameters: soil_profile - single-profile aqp::SoilProfileCollection. Returns: SoilProfileCollection n_simulations perturbed realizations input profile (n_simulations derived unique sim_comppct value profile’s horizons - see Known Limitations). calls simulate_soil_profile_thickness() get per-horizon thickness_sd; (2) calls query_osd_distinctness() averages bound_sd id/genhz lookup table; (3) merges thickness distinctness data together back onto profile’s horizons; (4) runs aqp::perturb(n = n_simulations, thickness.attr = "thickness_sd") generate n_simulations thickness-perturbed copies whole profile ; (5) runs second, per-copy aqp::perturb(n = 1, boundary.attr = "bound_sd") pass copies individually additionally perturb horizon boundary depths using OSD-derived distinctness offsets, recombines via aqp::combine(); (6) final guard, clamps simulated horizon’s top/bottom back within original horizon’s hzdept_l/hzdepb_h bounds (via internal adjust_out_of_range_profiles() helper) perturbation push horizon boundary outside originally observed low/high range.

Reverts future::sequential parallel step, combines results via aqp::combine(), wraps whole parallel block tryCatch() logs returns NULL error rather propagating.
