title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: functional group covers two files — R/statistics.R R/validation-diagnostics.R — together provide package’s analytical quality-assurance layer. statistics.R performs statistical characterization processed SSURGO soil property data: correlation analysis (including compositional/ILR-aware texture correlations), distribution fitting via fitdistrplus, outlier detection (univariate IQR/Z-score multivariate Mahalanobis), descriptive property statistics confidence intervals. validation-diagnostics.R performs end--end quality assurance across entire simulation workflow, just group’s output: checks Monte Carlo convergence coverage, correlation-structure preservation simulation pipeline, Gaussian-process (GP) depth-trend model performance, soil-science plausibility final simulated values, rolls single weighted quality score, grade, optional diagnostic report/plots. overall soilSIM pipeline group sits downstream data acquisition processing: consumes cleaned/infilled SSURGO data statistical analysis, separately consumes outputs Monte Carlo, GP-modeling, multivariate-adjustment (correlation) groups validate workflow whole.

what: 1. analyze_soil_statistics() — Master Statistical Analysis Entry Point
title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Purpose: Top-level driver runs full statistics pipeline (validation → correlation → distribution fitting → outlier detection → property statistics → results validation → quality report) processed SSURGO data frame. Signature: Parameters: - processed_data — processed SSURGO data frame (data-processing group), expected carry cokey, hzdept_r, numeric _r property columns. - analysis_config — list overrides merged (via merge_configurations()) top get_statistical_analysis_defaults(). - correlation_methods — character vector correlation methods compute ("pearson", "spearman", /"kendall"). - distribution_fitting — whether run Step 5 (distribution analysis). - outlier_detection — whether run Step 6 (outlier analysis). - validate_results — whether run Step 8 (statistical-results validation). - verbose — enables DEBUG-level logging initializes logging already configured. Returns: list correlation_matrices, distribution_analysis, outlier_analysis, property_statistics, validation_results, analysis_metadata (timing, config, counts), quality_report, data_validation, processed_data (populated config$return_processed_data TRUE). Behavior: Runs fixed 10-step pipeline: (1) validates input data quality via validate_data_quality(), warning rather stopping quality min_quality_score; (2) identifies validates numeric soil properties via identify_numeric_soil_properties() + filter_valid_numeric_properties() (drops -NA/non-finite columns) + validate_properties_with_synonyms(); (3) handles missing values via handle_missing_values(), optionally grouped genhz; (4) runs correlation analysis via internal run_comprehensive_correlation_analysis_safe(); (5) optionally fits distributions via analyze_property_distributions_safe() (lightweight version computes descriptive summary statistics per property, actual distribution fits); (6) optionally detects outliers via detect_comprehensive_outliers_safe() (IQR method ); (7) computes full property statistics via compute_property_statistics(); (8) optionally validates accumulated results via validate_statistical_results_safe(); (9) builds quality report via generate_statistical_quality_report_safe(); (10) assembles timing/count metadata. Every analytical step individually tryCatch-wrapped handle_workflow_error(..., "warn"), failure one step degrades gracefully rather aborting whole analysis.

Returns character vector candidate distribution names.

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: detect_comprehensive_outliers(data, properties, config) Purpose/Behavior: property sufficient observations, runs every method config$outlier_methods (e.g. "iqr", "zscore", "modified_zscore") via detect_outliers(), using matching threshold config$outlier_thresholds. length(properties) >= 2 config$detect_multivariate_outliers TRUE, also runs detect_multivariate_outliers() (real Mahalanobis-distance detection, guarding non-positive-definite covariance matrix Matrix::nearPD(); flags outer 1 - config$mahalanobis_alpha fraction, default 2.5%, via chi-squared cutoff). Returns list(property_outliers=, multivariate_outliers=, summary=) (summary via generate_outlier_summary()).

Aggregates overall validity flag validation_score via calculate_overall_validation_score() (1.0 minus per-error/per-warning penalties). Returns list(overall_valid=, errors=, warnings=, validation_score=, component_validations=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: compute_property_statistics(data, properties, config) Purpose/Behavior: property, computes n/missing-rate/mean/sd/min/max/range/CV/median/quartiles/IQR finite values, adds 95% t-based confidence interval via calculate_confidence_intervals(), adds skewness/kurtosis (calculate_skewness()/calculate_kurtosis(), hand-rolled moment-based implementations) plus Shapiro-Wilk normality p-value (computed n ≤ 5000, since shapiro.test() defined larger samples). Properties zero finite values silently skipped. Returns named list keyed property.

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: analyze_texture_correlations(data, texture_properties, methods, config) Purpose/Behavior: Computes raw Pearson/Spearman correlations among available texture properties (raw_correlations), known spuriously negative compositional (simplex-constrained, sum--100) data. three claytotal_r/sandtotal_r/silttotal_r present >4 complete rows, additionally computes correlations isometric-log-ratio (ILR) space via distributions.R’s dependency-free ilr_forward(), exposed ilr_correlations — statistically defensible view compositional data. Returns list(raw_correlations=, ilr_correlations=, n_observations=, note=). Minor exported helpers statistics.R (documented brief, separately elaborated): filter_valid_numeric_properties() (drops properties finite values, non-exported), internal _safe counterparts run_comprehensive_correlation_analysis_safe(), analyze_property_distributions_safe(), detect_comprehensive_outliers_safe(), validate_statistical_results_safe(), generate_statistical_quality_report_safe() (non-exported; lighter-weight versions actually wired analyze_soil_statistics()). Small numeric utilities calculate_condition_number(), calculate_skewness(), calculate_kurtosis() also non-exported.

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Purpose: Top-level driver assesses entire soil-simulation workflow’s output (Monte Carlo, correlation, GP models, soil-science realism) rolls one overall quality assessment. Signature: Parameters: - workflow_results — complete workflow output, expected optionally contain simulation_data, integrated_data, gp_models, correlation_matrices, training_data keys. - original_data — original SSURGO/NRCS data, used comparison baseline coverage depth-trend checks. - validation_config — validation configuration; defaults get_default_configuration("validation"). - generate_plots — whether generate diagnostic plots (Step 7 pipeline). - output_dir — directory save diagnostic plot files (plots still returned objects/paths even NULL, just written disk). Returns: list workflow_summary, monte_carlo_validation, correlation_validation, gp_model_validation, soil_science_validation, performance_metrics, overall_assessment (score/grade/status), diagnostic_plots, recommendations, validation_metadata (timestamp, config, R/package versions, duration). Behavior: (1) initializes result structure via initialize_validation_structure(); (2) extracts shallow-validates whichever simulation_data/gp_models/correlation_matrices/training_data present via extract_and_validate_components(); (3) runs execute_validation_pipeline(), turn conditionally calls validate_monte_carlo_quality(), validate_correlation_structures(), validate_gp_model_workflow(), validate_soil_science_realism() — skipped (failed) required component wasn’t found — computes calculate_workflow_performance(), assess_workflow_quality(), optionally generate_comprehensive_diagnostics(), generate_workflow_recommendations(); (4) finalizes timing via finalize_validation_results(). Every pipeline step individually tryCatch-wrapped, missing malformed component degrades step validation_skipped/validation_failed entry rather aborting whole call.

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: assess_workflow_quality(validation_results, validation_config) Purpose/Behavior: Computes per-component quality score (Monte Carlo, correlation, GP models, soil science) via calculate_component_quality_scores(), combines single weighted score via calculate_weighted_quality_score() (weights validation_config$quality_weights get_default_quality_weights(), equal 0.25/0.25/0.25/0.25 split default), assigns letter-style grade via determine_quality_grade() ("Excellent" ≥0.9 "Poor" <0.6), flags identify_critical_issues() (validation failures, sub-0.6 overall score, data-quality failures). Returns create_quality_assessment() list: quality_score, quality_grade, component_scores, critical_issues, workflow_status ("PASSED" quality_score >= validation_config$minimum_acceptable_score — default 0.7 — else "FAILED"), confidence_level (via calculate_confidence_level(), rewards high mean score low cross-component variance), assessment_metadata.

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_monte_carlo_quality(monte_carlo_results, original_data = NULL, config = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Validates monte_carlo_results$simulation_data via validate_data_quality() (requires cokey, simulation_number), runs four assessments sequence progress tracking (track_progress()): assess_simulation_convergence() (splits simulation_number config$convergence_criteria$n_batches sequential batches — default 5 — checks whether numeric property’s batch mean stabilized within tolerance, default 0.05 relative change), assess_simulation_coverage(), validate_distribution_fidelity(), "diagnostics" step calls generate_simulation_diagnostics(). Fixed (previously bug): last call used pass 2 positional arguments generate_simulation_diagnostics() (defined monte-carlo.R) takes 5 (original_data, simulation_results, properties, correlation_config, config), always raised argument-mismatch error, silently caught surrounding tryCatch list(validation_failed = TRUE, error = ...) placeholder instead real diagnostics. call now passes 5 args name, sourced function’s original_data parameter, already-fetched simulation_data local (constrained [horizon, property, realization] array), monte_carlo_results$metadata$properties/monte_carlo_results$correlation_structure. Returns list(convergence_assessment=, coverage_assessment=, distribution_fidelity=, simulation_diagnostics=, data_quality=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: assess_simulation_coverage(simulation_data, original_data, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(min_coverage_percentile = 0.95, max_extrapolation_factor = 1.2, min_samples_per_group = 10). Identifies numeric properties (excluding simulation_number/hzdept_r/hzdepb_r) via validate_properties(), : original_data supplied, computes assess_property_coverage() (overlap simulated original ranges, plus extrapolation-beyond-range detection); always computes assess_distributional_coverage() (IQR-based outlier percentage 5th–95th percentile spread relative full range). cokey present, also computes assess_group_representation() (fraction cokey groups meeting min_samples_per_group). Returns list(parameter_space_coverage=, distributional_coverage=, group_representation=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_distribution_fidelity(simulation_data, simulation_metadata, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(ks_test_alpha = 0.05, moment_tolerance = 0.1, quantile_tolerance = 0.05). property named simulation_metadata$distribution_parameters, draws reference sample fitted distribution via distributions.R’s quantile_from_fit() compares simulated values three ways: test_distribution_fidelity() (two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test), compare_distribution_moments() (relative mean/variance difference), compare_distribution_quantiles() (relative difference 10th/50th/90th percentiles). Also runs IQR-based detect_outliers() per property. Returns list(distribution_tests=, moment_comparisons=, quantile_comparisons=, outlier_assessment=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_correlation_structures(correlation_matrices, simulation_data, config = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Validates simulation_data via validate_data_quality(), runs four steps progress tracking: validate_correlation_matrix_quality() (positive-definiteness + condition number per matrix, via assess_correlation_matrix_properties()), validate_correlation_preservation_diagnostics(), validate_within_depth_correlations(), assess_cholesky_decomposition(). Returns list(matrix_quality=, preservation_assessment=, depth_specific_validation=, cholesky_validation=, data_quality=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_correlation_preservation_diagnostics(original_correlations, simulation_data, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(max_correlation_difference = 0.1, correlation_rmse_threshold = 0.05, min_samples_for_validation = 30). Computes overall simulated correlation matrix via safe_correlation() compares original_correlations$global_correlation_matrix shared properties via assess_correlation_differences() (real element-wise max/mean/RMSE difference). Also recomputes correlations within 5 distinct hzdept_r depth values (requiring ≥ min_samples_for_validation rows) compares via assess_depth_correlation_preservation(). Returns list(overall_preservation=, depth_specific_preservation=, property_specific_preservation=) (last currently never populated).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_within_depth_correlations(simulation_data, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria includes depth_bins = c(0, 15, 30, 60, 100, 200) min_samples_per_bin = 20. Bins hzdept_r via cut(), computes correlation matrix per bin (via safe_correlation()) meets minimum sample size, records mean absolute correlation plus assess_correlation_matrix_properties() per bin. Also computes assess_correlation_stability_across_depths() (much pairwise correlation’s value varies across bins). Returns list(depth_bin_correlations=, correlation_stability=, depth_trend_correlations=) (last currently never populated).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: assess_cholesky_decomposition(correlation_matrices, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(reconstruction_tolerance = 1e-10, condition_number_threshold = 1e12, eigenvalue_threshold = 1e-8). every matrix entry correlation_matrices, runs assess_single_cholesky_decomposition() — actual chol() attempt Frobenius-norm reconstruction-error measurement (||L'L - matrix||), graded "excellent"/"good"/"poor" tolerance. Returns list(decomposition_quality=, numerical_stability=, reconstruction_accuracy=) (latter two sub-lists populated beyond decomposition_quality).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_gp_model_workflow(gp_models, training_data, config = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Validates training_data (supplied) via validate_data_quality(), runs four GP-focused steps progress tracking: validate_gp_model_performance(), validate_gp_predictions(), assess_depth_trend_realism(), perform_gp_cross_validation(). Returns list(model_performance=, prediction_quality=, depth_trend_realism=, cross_validation=, training_data_quality=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_gp_model_performance(gp_models, training_data, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(max_training_rmse = 0.5, min_r_squared = 0.6, max_condition_number = 1e12). every property/group combination gp_models whose type "stratified_grouped", calls assess_single_gp_performance(), delegates training RMSE gp-modeling.R’s calculate_model_diagnostics() derives R² RMSE training data’s variance. Aggregates via calculate_overall_gp_performance() (mean R²/RMSE across models). Returns list(individual_model_performance=, overall_performance=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: assess_depth_trend_realism(gp_models, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria includes test_depths = seq(0, 200, = 5), realistic_ranges = get_realistic_property_ranges(), monotonicity_tolerance = 0.3, gradient_limits = get_realistic_gradients(). stratified-grouped GP model, predicts depth trend via gp-modeling.R’s predict_gp_depth_trends(), judges realism via assess_trend_realism() — reuses gp-modeling.R’s assess_trend_monotonicity() assess_realistic_values(), additionally counts values outside criteria$realistic_ranges[[prop]] (non-finite predictions range configured property). Violations aggregated via summarize_constraint_violations(). Returns list(trend_predictions=, realism_assessment=, constraint_violations=) (realism_assessment currently never separately populated beyond ’s nested trend_predictions/constraint_violations).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_gp_predictions(gp_models, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Default criteria list(test_depths = seq(0, 150, = 10), uncertainty_threshold = 0.5, smoothness_criteria = 0.1). stratified-grouped GP model, calls validate_single_gp_predictions(), predicts depth trend measures smoothness one minus normalized mean absolute second difference predicted curve (discrete-roughness measure). Returns list(prediction_smoothness=, uncertainty_assessment=, extrapolation_behavior=) (prediction_smoothness currently populated).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: validate_soil_science_realism(simulation_data, original_data = NULL, config = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Validates simulation_data via validate_data_quality(), runs four steps progress tracking: assess_property_constraints(), validate_horizon_characteristics() (surface vs. subsurface range compliance plus depth-transition smoothness), assess_pedological_relationships() (checks clay–CEC organic-matter–depth correlation direction/strength columns present), validate_simulation_depth_trends() (correlation simulated original per-depth-bin means, original_data supplied). Returns list(property_constraints=, horizon_characteristics=, pedological_relationships=, depth_trend_realism=, data_quality=).

title: Statistics & Diagnostics
text: Signature: assess_property_constraints(simulation_data, criteria = NULL) Purpose/Behavior: Defaults get_default_property_constraints(), builds property_ranges get_realistic_property_ranges() (hardcoded min/max clay/sand/silt/pH/bulk density/water retention/OM/CEC/RFV). configured property present data, checks range violations (directly via utils.R’s validate_numeric_ranges()), calls assess_cross_property_constraints() (texture sum--100 check plus explicit cross_property_rules) detect_distribution_anomalies() (IQR-outlier counts per numeric column, via detect_outliers()). what: is_unsuitable(data, hzname_col = "hzname", strict_mode = TRUE, custom_exclusions = NULL)
title: Utilities
text: Purpose: Flags soil horizons excluded property modeling/imputation aren’t representative soil material (bedrock, cemented pans, organic horizons, restrictive layers, etc.). Parameters: - data - Soil horizon data frame horizon designation information. - hzname_col - Column name containing horizon designations (default "hzname"). column absent, function logs WARN returns -FALSE (nothing flagged) rather erroring. - strict_mode - Whether apply additional strict-mode criteria (default TRUE, note differs legacy mod00 default FALSE). - custom_exclusions - Optional additional regex patterns (matched raw hzname values) flag unsuitable. Returns: logical vector, one element per row data, TRUE horizon considered unsuitable. Algorithm/behavior: Horizon names coerced character NA-filled "". row, hzname (desgnmaster present) upper-cased/trimmed checked, priority order, : (1) desgnmaster c("R","O"); (2) regex bedrock/cemented-pan codes (R, Cr, Cd, Cx, optional leading numeric prefix); (3) restrictive-layer descriptor words (fragipan, duripan, petrocalcic, petrogypsic, cemented, indurated); (4) trailing cemented-suffix "m"; (5) O organic-horizon pattern. richer columns is_potentially_restrictive, missing_required_properties, hzdept_r, restriction_top present, horizons restrictive contact (hzdept_r >= restriction_top) also flagged potentially-restrictive missing required properties ’d result. organic_horizon column present, ’d directly. strict_mode, horizons deeper 250 cm flagged, second pass applies generic transitional-horizon patterns (^C$, ^C[0-9], BC, CB, 2C, 3C, 4C) case-sensitively raw (non-uppercased) hznames. custom_exclusions regexes applied last, also case-sensitively raw hznames. Final counts (<= 10 distinct) actual unsuitable horizon-name values logged via log_message(). Note default strict_mode = TRUE differs legacy mod00_soil_utils.R prototype’s default FALSE, strict-mode pattern pass custom-exclusion pass match raw, non-uppercased hznames vector rather upper-cased hz used earlier loop - mixed-case horizon name (e.g. "bc") match strict-mode "BC" pattern.

what: validate_data_quality(data, required_columns = character(0), numeric_columns = character(0), quality_thresholds = NULL)
title: Utilities
text: Purpose: Composite data-quality assessment - missing-data percentage, outlier prevalence (informational ), consistency checks - rolled overall quality score letter grade. Parameters: - data - Input data frame assess. - required_columns - Columns whose presence required; missing ones lower consistency score. - numeric_columns - Columns expected numeric; drives numeric-completeness outlier sub-assessments. - quality_thresholds - Optional list overriding max_missing_percentage (default 0.2), min_completeness (default 0.8), max_outlier_percentage (default 0.05), min_numeric_columns (default 1); thresholds omitted supplied list backfilled defaults via %||%. Returns: list overall_quality (score, grade, validation_passed, component_scores), column_assessments (unused/always empty current implementation), missing_data_summary, numeric_data_summary, outlier_summary, consistency_summary. Algorithm/behavior: four assessment steps (missing data, numeric validation, outliers, consistency) wrapped tryCatch() safe fallback one failing step abort whole assessment. Step 1 computes per-column mean(.na(col)) (treating zero-length column 100% missing) flags columns exceeding max_missing_percentage. Step 2, numeric_columns non-empty, computes per-column total/finite/missing/infinite counts completeness (finite/total) existing numeric column. Step 3 runs simple 1.5x-IQR outlier count inlined directly function (call detect_outliers()) across existing numeric columns, requiring 4 finite values per column. Step 4 checks missing required_columns counts exact duplicate rows via duplicated(data). overall score weighted blend: missing_score * 0.4 + numeric_score * 0.4 + consistency_score * 0.2, missing_score = 1 - avg_missing_percentage numeric_score defaults 0.8 numeric summary computed. blended score maps grade: >= 0.9 Excellent, >= 0.8 Good, >= 0.7 Acceptable, >= 0.6 Needs Improvement, else Poor; validation_passed score >= quality_thresholds$min_completeness (default 0.7… note default constant used 0.7, min_completeness default 0.8 shown - inline fallback literal pass/fail check differs value written quality_thresholds$min_completeness thresholds auto-generated).

title: Utilities
text: Purpose: Throttled progress logging plus rough time-remaining estimate long-running loops (downloads, Monte Carlo simulations). Algorithm/behavior: Skips logging entirely unless current multiple update_frequency equals total (first calls, current == 1 timer setup, typically logged unless update_frequency 1). Computes percentage <- round(current/total * 100, 1). current > 0, reads progress_start_time option (defaulting Sys.time() - .e. effectively zero elapsed time - never set), computes rate <- current/elapsed remaining <- (total - current)/rate, appends "X min remaining"/"X sec remaining" string (minutes remaining exceeds 60 seconds). current == 1, sets options(progress_start_time = Sys.time()) subsequent calls read - reset happens current call’s elapsed-time calculation , current == 1 passes update_frequency gate top function (e.g. skipped entirely update_frequency isn’t 1 divisor happens allow row 1 , unless total == 1 ). Logs via log_message("INFO", ..., category = "Progress").

title: Utilities
text: Purpose: Confidence interval computation mean, median, proportion, normal-approximation, t-distribution, bootstrap. Parameters: statistic - "mean", "median", "proportion" (proportion treated identically mean - mean(x) - throughout; dedicated binomial/Wilson-type interval logic). method - "normal" (z-based), "t" (t-based, uses df = n-1), "bootstrap" (percentile bootstrap n_bootstrap resamples). Algorithm/behavior: Drops NAs data front (logging count removed - note logged count computed removal, now-NA-free vector, always log 0 removed regardless many actually stripped). Returns -NA result immediately nothing left. "bootstrap", draws n_bootstrap resamples sample(data, length(data), replace = TRUE), computes requested statistic resample via replicate(), takes alpha/2/1-alpha/2 sample quantiles bootstrap distribution CI bounds (unrecognized statistic inside bootstrap loop hard stop()). "normal"/"t", computes se <- sd(data)/sqrt(n) margin error either qnorm(1 - alpha/2) qt(1 - alpha/2, df = n-1), applied symmetrically around sample mean (note: "t"/"normal", estimate always mean regardless requested statistic - "median"/"proportion" actually honored "bootstrap" branch). method value hard stop(). code: # Validate a set of user-supplied property names against SSURGO synonyms, # then run a composite data-quality check before doing anything expensive with it.  property_check <- validate_properties_with_synonyms(   properties = c("clay", "sandtotal_r", "pH", "bogus_property"),   property_lookup = "ssurgo",   strict_mode = TRUE )  if (!property_check$valid) {   stop("Property validation failed: ", paste(property_check$errors, collapse = "; ")) }  # ssurgo_data is a horizon-level data frame with an `hzname` column ssurgo_data$unsuitable_horizon <- is_unsuitable(ssurgo_data, hzname_col = "hzname")  quality <- validate_data_quality(   data = ssurgo_data[!ssurgo_data$unsuitable_horizon, ],   required_columns = c("cokey", "hzdept_r", "hzdepb_r"),   numeric_columns = c("claytotal_r", "sandtotal_r", "silttotal_r") )  log_message("INFO", paste("Data quality grade:", quality$overall_quality$grade), category = "Example")

title: Available Water Storage via Van Genuchten / ROSETTA
text: Available water storage (AWS) - much plant-available water soil can hold - derived van Genuchten (1980) water-retention curve, whose shape parameters soilSIM estimates via soilDB::ROSETTA(), live pedotransfer-function API. vignette derives real AWS estimates real soil components Amador-area AOI used “Getting Started” vignette. See soilSIM/docs/07_aws_van_genuchten_modeling.md full function-level reference, including two intentional, ported--quirks simulate_vg_aws() vignette doesn’t need touch.
code: library(soilSIM) library(ggplot2)

title: Available Water Storage via Van Genuchten / ROSETTA

what: Step 2: Run ROSETTA and simulate available water storage
title: Available Water Storage via Van Genuchten / ROSETTA
text: calculate_aws_df() (1) calls soilDB::ROSETTA() - live POST handbook60.org - derive van Genuchten shape parameters texture/bulk-density inputs, (2) Monte Carlo-simulates field capacity permanent wilting point water content via simulate_vg_aws(), (3) depth-slices result standard intervals via aqp::slab(): available water holding capacity (AWHC, cm water per cm soil) real component, standard 0-5, 5-15, 15-30, 30-60, 60-100 cm depth slabs actually spanned component’s horizons (slab beyond component’s real horizon depths comes back NA, last row ).  Averaging across depth slabs like , though, throws away real structure data: component’s AWHC actually varies slab slab. Plotting AWHC depth real component shows depth-resolved pattern instead flattening away:
code: # The real call this vignette's cached data came from (requires live network access): aws_result <- calculate_aws_df(rosetta_input) aws_result <- aws_example$result aws_result #> # A tibble: 15 × 4 #>    cokey      top bottom   AWHC #>    <chr>    <int>  <int>  <dbl> #>  1 26397650     0      5  0.146 #>  2 26397650     5     15  0.146 #>  3 26397650    15     30  0.123 #>  4 26397650    30     60  0.111 #>  5 26397650    60    100  0.111 #>  6 26397656     0      5  0.146 #>  7 26397656     5     15  0.146 #>  8 26397656    15     30  0.123 #>  9 26397656    30     60  0.111 #> 10 26397656    60    100  0.111 #> 11 26397666     0      5  0.160 #> 12 26397666     5     15  0.160 #> 13 26397666    15     30  0.160 #> 14 26397666    30     60  0.160 #> 15 26397666    60    100 NA plot_data <- aws_result[!is.na(aws_result$AWHC), ] agg <- aggregate(AWHC ~ cokey, data = plot_data, FUN = mean) agg$cokey <- factor(agg$cokey)  ggplot(agg, aes(x = cokey, y = AWHC, fill = cokey)) +   geom_col() +   scale_fill_viridis_d() +   guides(fill = "none") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Mean simulated AWHC by real component (cokey)",        x = "cokey", y = "AWHC (cm water / cm soil)") +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) plot_data$mid_depth <- (plot_data$top + plot_data$bottom) / 2 plot_data$cokey <- factor(plot_data$cokey)  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = mid_depth, y = AWHC, color = cokey)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "cokey") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Simulated AWHC vs. depth, by real component (cokey)",        x = "Depth (cm, slab midpoint)", y = "AWHC (cm water / cm soil)")

title: Available Water Storage via Van Genuchten / ROSETTA
text: van_genuchten() closed-form curve calculate_aws_df() evaluates internally field capacity (-33 kPa) permanent wilting point (-1500 kPa) matric potentials. three curves use illustrative shape parameters - representative ranges ROSETTA typically returns sandy, loamy, clayey texture respectively - values derived vignette’s real data:
code: h <- -10^seq(0, 5, length.out = 200)  # matric potential, cmH2O (log-spaced) vg_params <- data.frame(   texture = c("Sandy (illustrative)", "Loamy (illustrative)", "Clayey (illustrative)"),   alpha   = c(0.075, 0.02, 0.008),   n       = c(1.89, 1.3, 1.09),   theta_r = c(0.045, 0.05, 0.098),   theta_s = c(0.43, 0.45, 0.459) )  vg_curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(vg_params)), function(i) {   p <- vg_params[i, ]   data.frame(     texture = p$texture,     h = h,     theta = van_genuchten(h, alpha = p$alpha, n = p$n, theta_r = p$theta_r, theta_s = p$theta_s)   ) })) vg_curves$texture <- factor(vg_curves$texture, levels = vg_params$texture)  fc_x <- 33 * 10.19716    # field capacity, -33 kPa in cmH2O wp_x <- 1500 * 10.19716  # wilting point, -1500 kPa in cmH2O  ggplot(vg_curves, aes(x = -h, y = theta, color = texture)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_x_log10() +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Texture") +   geom_vline(xintercept = fc_x, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +   geom_vline(xintercept = wp_x, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey20") +   annotate("text", x = fc_x, y = 0.46, label = "Field capacity\n(-33 kPa)",            hjust = -0.05, size = 3, color = "grey40") +   annotate("text", x = wp_x, y = 0.46, label = "Wilting point\n(-1500 kPa)",            hjust = 1.05, size = 3, color = "grey20") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Van Genuchten water-retention curves (illustrative parameter sets)",        x = "Matric potential (-cmH2O, log scale)",        y = "Volumetric water content")

title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: vignettes package (getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd, raster-fusion-ssurgo-solus.Rmd) walk top-level pipeline functions end end. vignette instead zooms single thematic group low-level, pure-math functions - R/bayesian-updating.R - works one individually: computes, parameter controls, varying parameter changes result. finer-grained, “read primitives” companion raster-fusion-ssurgo-solus.Rmd, exercises exact math implicitly (raster-native, cell cell) inside fusion pipeline never isolates . See soilSIM/docs/08_bayesian_updating.md full function-level reference vignette based . bayesian-updating.R fuses prior belief soil property (e.g. SSURGO-derived estimate) likelihood - newly observed data (e.g. lab field measurements) - posterior belief combines , weighted confident (precise) side . examples use small, clearly-labeled synthetic prior/likelihood values - network access real SSURGO/SOLUS data needed vignette. Steps: bayes_update_normal_normal() - exact closed-form Normal-Normal fusion, worked example plus sensitivity sweep relative precision. normal_to_lognormal_params() / lognormal_to_normal_params() - fusing right-skewed, strictly positive property (organic matter) safely, log-space. fuse_beta() / fuse_gamma() - closed-form -family fusion bounded (Beta) positive-skewed (Gamma) properties, plus moment-conversion helpers. fuse_bivariate_normal() - 2D generalization, illustrated joint clay/sand/silt (ILR) example. dispatchers bayes_fuse(), bayesian_update(), fuse_property() - route right method.
code: library(soilSIM) library(ggplot2)

title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: Purpose: fuse Normal prior N(prior_mu, prior_sigma) Normal likelihood N(lik_mu, lik_sigma) Normal posterior, via precision-weighted averaging. Precision inverse variance (1 / sigma^2) - tighter (smaller-sigma) distribution higher precision, .e. represents confident belief. Parameters: prior_mu, prior_sigma - prior’s mean standard deviation. lik_mu, lik_sigma - likelihood’s mean standard deviation, units. four arguments plain numeric scalars equal-length vectors (function fully vectorized, lets raster-fusion.R reuse unchanged across every cell SpatRaster).

title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: hypothetical SSURGO-derived prior belief clay content (%) map unit, hypothetical lab-observed likelihood handful new samples location: Two documented invariants, checked empirically rather just asserted: function symmetric swapping side called “prior” “likelihood” - math doesn’t care labels, (mu, sigma) pairs: Plotting three distributions makes fusion concrete: posterior (green) narrower prior (purple) likelihood (yellow), sits closer likelihood likelihood specified precise (smaller sigma) :
code: prior_clay <- list(mu = 22, sigma = 6)   # SSURGO-derived prior belief lik_clay   <- list(mu = 30, sigma = 3)   # hypothetical lab observation, more precise than the prior  posterior_clay <- bayes_update_normal_normal(   prior_mu = prior_clay$mu, prior_sigma = prior_clay$sigma,   lik_mu = lik_clay$mu, lik_sigma = lik_clay$sigma ) posterior_clay #> $mu #> [1] 28.4 #>  #> $sigma #> [1] 2.683282 # Fusion only sharpens - the posterior can never be more uncertain than either input posterior_clay$sigma <= min(prior_clay$sigma, lik_clay$sigma) #> [1] TRUE  # The posterior mean is pulled between the two inputs, never outside their range posterior_clay$mu >= min(prior_clay$mu, lik_clay$mu) && posterior_clay$mu <= max(prior_clay$mu, lik_clay$mu) #> [1] TRUE swapped <- bayes_update_normal_normal(   prior_mu = lik_clay$mu, prior_sigma = lik_clay$sigma,   lik_mu = prior_clay$mu, lik_sigma = prior_clay$sigma ) identical(posterior_clay, swapped) #> [1] TRUE normal_pdf_df <- function(mu, sigma, label, x) {   data.frame(x = x, density = dnorm(x, mu, sigma), source = label) }  x_grid <- seq(0, 45, length.out = 400) dist_df <- rbind(   normal_pdf_df(prior_clay$mu, prior_clay$sigma, "Prior", x_grid),   normal_pdf_df(lik_clay$mu, lik_clay$sigma, "Likelihood", x_grid),   normal_pdf_df(posterior_clay$mu, posterior_clay$sigma, "Posterior", x_grid) ) dist_df$source <- factor(dist_df$source, levels = c("Prior", "Likelihood", "Posterior"))  ggplot(dist_df, aes(x = x, y = density, color = source, fill = source)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.25, position = "identity") +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Normal-Normal Bayesian fusion: clay content",     subtitle = "Posterior is narrower than both inputs, and pulled toward the more precise (likelihood) side",     x = "Clay content (%)", y = "Density"   )

what: Sensitivity sweep: relative precision drives where the posterior lands
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: core intuition Bayesian fusion posterior mean simple average two inputs - ’s precision-weighted average, whichever side certain (smaller sigma) pulls posterior toward . hold prior_mu/prior_sigma fixed vary lik_sigma across three cases - likelihood much precise, comparably precise, much less precise prior - holding lik_mu fixed , movement posterior mean attributable purely changing relative precision: lik_sigma shrinks (likelihood becomes precise, first row), posterior_mu moves closer lik_mu (30); lik_sigma grows (likelihood becomes less precise, last row), posterior_mu stays closer prior_mu (22). fusion “tug war” made visible:
code: prior_mu <- 22; prior_sigma <- 6 lik_mu <- 30  sweep_cases <- data.frame(   case = c("Likelihood much more precise", "Comparable precision", "Likelihood much less precise"),   lik_sigma = c(1, 6, 18) )  sweep_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sweep_cases)), function(i) {   post <- bayes_update_normal_normal(prior_mu, prior_sigma, lik_mu, sweep_cases$lik_sigma[i])   data.frame(     case = sweep_cases$case[i],     lik_sigma = sweep_cases$lik_sigma[i],     posterior_mu = post$mu,     posterior_sigma = post$sigma   ) })) sweep_results #>                           case lik_sigma posterior_mu posterior_sigma #> 1 Likelihood much more precise         1     29.78378       0.9863939 #> 2         Comparable precision         6     26.00000       4.2426407 #> 3 Likelihood much less precise        18     22.80000       5.6920998 ggplot(sweep_results, aes(x = reorder(case, lik_sigma), y = posterior_mu)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = prior_mu, linetype = "dashed", color = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.15)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = lik_mu, linetype = "dashed", color = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.75)) +   geom_point(aes(color = case), size = 4) +   geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = posterior_mu - posterior_sigma, ymax = posterior_mu + posterior_sigma,                      color = case), width = 0.15) +   scale_color_viridis_d(guide = "none") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Posterior mean shifts toward whichever side is more precise",     subtitle = "Dashed lines mark prior_mu (22, lower) and lik_mu (30, upper); prior_sigma fixed at 6",     x = NULL, y = "Posterior mean (+/- posterior sd)"   )

what: Step 2: fusing a right-skewed property safely - normal_to_lognormal_params() / lognormal_to_normal_params()
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: bayes_update_normal_normal() assumes sides Normal. ’s problem strictly-positive, right-skewed properties like organic matter (OM) CEC: property’s sigma large relative mean, treating Normal fusing directly can place real posterior probability mass zero, physically impossible percentage concentration. normal_to_lognormal_params(mu, sigma) moment-matches raw-space Lognormal’s mean/sd onto mu/ sigma underlying (log-space) Normal, bayes_update_normal_normal() can reused unchanged log-space; lognormal_to_normal_params(mu_log, sigma_log) exact algebraic inverse, converting fused log-space posterior back raw-space mean/sd. hypothetical prior likelihood organic matter (%), property right-skewed sigma large enough, relative mean, real concern: Fusing directly Normal risks posterior mean minus couple sigma dropping zero; importantly, shape raw Normal fit ignores right skew altogether. Converting log-space first: Fusing log-space (still exact Normal-Normal update, just log-transformed parameters), converting posterior back raw space: lognormal_to_normal_params() exact inverse normal_to_lognormal_params() - round-tripping raw-space parameters functions returns original values, floating-point precision: Plotting raw-space prior, likelihood, posterior Lognormal densities (never negative, right skewed, exactly percentage look like) versus naive raw-space Normal fusion produced:
code: prior_om <- list(mu = 3.0, sigma = 2.0)   # SSURGO-derived prior; sigma is 2/3 of the mean lik_om   <- list(mu = 5.5, sigma = 1.0)   # hypothetical lab observation prior_om_log <- normal_to_lognormal_params(prior_om$mu, prior_om$sigma) lik_om_log <- normal_to_lognormal_params(lik_om$mu, lik_om$sigma) prior_om_log #> $mu #> [1] 0.9147499 #>  #> $sigma #> [1] 0.6064031 lik_om_log #> $mu #> [1] 1.688486 #>  #> $sigma #> [1] 0.1803419 posterior_om_log <- bayes_update_normal_normal(   prior_om_log$mu, prior_om_log$sigma, lik_om_log$mu, lik_om_log$sigma ) posterior_om <- lognormal_to_normal_params(posterior_om_log$mu, posterior_om_log$sigma) posterior_om #> $mu #> [1] 5.15803 #>  #> $sigma #> [1] 0.898317 roundtrip <- lognormal_to_normal_params(prior_om_log$mu, prior_om_log$sigma) all.equal(roundtrip, prior_om) #> [1] TRUE x_grid_om <- seq(0.001, 12, length.out = 400)  lognormal_pdf <- function(mu_log, sigma_log, label, x) {   data.frame(x = x, density = dlnorm(x, meanlog = mu_log, sdlog = sigma_log), source = label) }  om_dist_df <- rbind(   lognormal_pdf(prior_om_log$mu, prior_om_log$sigma, "Prior (Lognormal)", x_grid_om),   lognormal_pdf(lik_om_log$mu, lik_om_log$sigma, "Likelihood (Lognormal)", x_grid_om),   lognormal_pdf(posterior_om_log$mu, posterior_om_log$sigma, "Posterior (Lognormal)", x_grid_om) ) om_dist_df$source <- factor(om_dist_df$source,   levels = c("Prior (Lognormal)", "Likelihood (Lognormal)", "Posterior (Lognormal)"))  naive_posterior_om <- bayes_update_normal_normal(prior_om$mu, prior_om$sigma, lik_om$mu, lik_om$sigma)  ggplot(om_dist_df, aes(x = x, y = density, color = source, fill = source)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.25, position = "identity") +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_vline(xintercept = naive_posterior_om$mu - 2 * naive_posterior_om$sigma,              linetype = "dotted", color = "grey40") +   annotate("text", x = naive_posterior_om$mu - 2 * naive_posterior_om$sigma, y = 0, hjust = -0.05,            vjust = -0.5, size = 3, color = "grey40",            label = "naive raw-Normal\nposterior mean - 2sd") +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Log-space fusion keeps organic matter strictly positive",     subtitle = "The naive raw-space Normal posterior's mean-2sd point (dotted line) falls near/below zero",     x = "Organic matter (%)", y = "Density"   ) # The naive raw-space Normal fusion's implied lower tail: naive_posterior_om$mu - 2 * naive_posterior_om$sigma #> [1] 3.211146

what: Step 3: same-family closed-form fusion - fuse_beta() / fuse_gamma()
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: properties naturally bounded (fraction/percentage [0, 1], e.g. saturation) fit better Beta distribution Normal; others strictly positive long right tail fit better Gamma distribution. families exact closed-form conjugate fusion rule, analogous Normal precision-addition family’s shape parameters.

previous_headings: Step 3: same-family closed-form fusion - fuse_beta() / fuse_gamma()
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: Purpose: fuse two Beta beliefs, Beta(prior_alpha, prior_beta) Beta(lik_alpha, lik_beta), via straight addition shape parameters minus one: Beta(a1,b1) x Beta(a2,b2) -> Beta(a1+a2-1, b1+b2-1). Parameters: prior_alpha, prior_beta, lik_alpha, lik_beta - side’s Beta shape parameters (numeric scalar vector). Returns: list(alpha=, beta=, feasible=) - feasible flags whether fused shape parameters stayed positive (prior_alpha + lik_alpha > 1 prior_beta + lik_beta > 1), requirement result remain valid distribution. hypothetical prior likelihood belief water-saturation fraction, expressed Beta parameters (moment-matched via moments_to_beta() assumed mean/variance, shapes concrete interpretable): beta_to_moments() converts fused shape parameters back interpretable mean/variance, also function used (inputs) feasible come back FALSE, fall back fusing Normal-moment space instead:
code: prior_sat_moments <- list(mean = 0.35, var = 0.02^2) lik_sat_moments <- list(mean = 0.50, var = 0.01^2)  prior_sat_beta <- moments_to_beta(prior_sat_moments$mean, prior_sat_moments$var) lik_sat_beta <- moments_to_beta(lik_sat_moments$mean, lik_sat_moments$var) prior_sat_beta #> $alpha #> [1] 198.7125 #>  #> $beta #> [1] 369.0375 lik_sat_beta #> $alpha #> [1] 1249.5 #>  #> $beta #> [1] 1249.5  posterior_sat_beta <- fuse_beta(   prior_sat_beta$alpha, prior_sat_beta$beta, lik_sat_beta$alpha, lik_sat_beta$beta ) posterior_sat_beta #> $alpha #> [1] 1447.212 #>  #> $beta #> [1] 1617.537 #>  #> $feasible #> [1] TRUE beta_to_moments(posterior_sat_beta$alpha, posterior_sat_beta$beta) #> $mean #> [1] 0.4722123 #>  #> $var #> [1] 8.129425e-05 beta_pdf <- function(alpha, beta, label, x) {   data.frame(x = x, density = dbeta(x, alpha, beta), source = label) } x_grid_sat <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 400) sat_dist_df <- rbind(   beta_pdf(prior_sat_beta$alpha, prior_sat_beta$beta, "Prior", x_grid_sat),   beta_pdf(lik_sat_beta$alpha, lik_sat_beta$beta, "Likelihood", x_grid_sat),   beta_pdf(posterior_sat_beta$alpha, posterior_sat_beta$beta, "Posterior", x_grid_sat) ) sat_dist_df$source <- factor(sat_dist_df$source, levels = c("Prior", "Likelihood", "Posterior"))  ggplot(sat_dist_df, aes(x = x, y = density, color = source, fill = source)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.25, position = "identity") +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Beta-Beta conjugate fusion: water-saturation fraction",     x = "Saturation fraction", y = "Density"   )

previous_headings: Step 3: same-family closed-form fusion - fuse_beta() / fuse_gamma()
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: Purpose: fuse two Gamma beliefs, Gamma(prior_shape, prior_rate) Gamma(lik_shape, lik_rate) (shape/rate parameterization), via Gamma(k1,r1) x Gamma(k2,r2) -> Gamma(k1+k2-1, r1+r2) - rates add outright (like Normal precisions), shapes add minus one (like Beta’s alpha/beta). Parameters: prior_shape, prior_rate, lik_shape, lik_rate. Returns: list(shape=, rate=, feasible=), feasible requiring prior_shape + lik_shape > 1. hypothetical prior/likelihood saturated hydraulic conductivity (strictly positive, long right tail), built via Gamma method--moments helper moments_to_gamma():  fuse_beta() fuse_gamma() valid fused shape parameters stay positive - feasible comes back FALSE cell/case, documented fallback re-express sides Normal moments (beta_to_moments()/gamma_to_moments()), fuse bayes_update_normal_normal(), convert result back (moments_to_beta()/moments_to_gamma()). fallback automatic - caller hitting feasible == FALSE must invoke explicitly.
code: prior_ksat_moments <- list(mean = 15, var = 6^2) lik_ksat_moments <- list(mean = 8, var = 2^2)  prior_ksat_gamma <- moments_to_gamma(prior_ksat_moments$mean, prior_ksat_moments$var) lik_ksat_gamma <- moments_to_gamma(lik_ksat_moments$mean, lik_ksat_moments$var) prior_ksat_gamma #> $shape #> [1] 6.25 #>  #> $rate #> [1] 0.4166667 lik_ksat_gamma #> $shape #> [1] 16 #>  #> $rate #> [1] 2  posterior_ksat_gamma <- fuse_gamma(   prior_ksat_gamma$shape, prior_ksat_gamma$rate, lik_ksat_gamma$shape, lik_ksat_gamma$rate ) posterior_ksat_gamma #> $shape #> [1] 21.25 #>  #> $rate #> [1] 2.416667 #>  #> $feasible #> [1] TRUE gamma_to_moments(posterior_ksat_gamma$shape, posterior_ksat_gamma$rate) #> $mean #> [1] 8.793103 #>  #> $var #> [1] 3.638526 gamma_pdf <- function(shape, rate, label, x) {   data.frame(x = x, density = dgamma(x, shape = shape, rate = rate), source = label) } x_grid_ksat <- seq(0.01, 40, length.out = 400) ksat_dist_df <- rbind(   gamma_pdf(prior_ksat_gamma$shape, prior_ksat_gamma$rate, "Prior", x_grid_ksat),   gamma_pdf(lik_ksat_gamma$shape, lik_ksat_gamma$rate, "Likelihood", x_grid_ksat),   gamma_pdf(posterior_ksat_gamma$shape, posterior_ksat_gamma$rate, "Posterior", x_grid_ksat) ) ksat_dist_df$source <- factor(ksat_dist_df$source, levels = c("Prior", "Likelihood", "Posterior"))  ggplot(ksat_dist_df, aes(x = x, y = density, color = source, fill = source)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.25, position = "identity") +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Gamma-Gamma conjugate fusion: saturated hydraulic conductivity",     x = "Ksat (cm/hr)", y = "Density"   )

Parameters: mu1, mu2 - length-2 mean vectors; Sigma1, Sigma2 - 2x2 covariance matrices. Returns: list(mu = fused mean vector, Sigma = fused covariance matrix). small, illustrative example directly ILR-coordinate space (full clay/sand/silt triplets - full workflow fuse_texture_group_from_triplets(), wraps function together distributions.R’s estimate_ilr_moments_mc()/sample_ilr_posterior(); see soilSIM/docs/08_bayesian_updating.md whole chain). fuse two independent bivariate Normal beliefs 2D ILR coordinate pair directly: scalar case, fusion sharpens: posterior variance (diagonal Sigma) larger corresponding diagonal entries either input covariance matrix, posterior mean sits two inputs, pulled toward whichever side smaller (precise) variances - Sigma2 , fused_ilr$mu sits closer mu2: fuse_texture_group_from_triplets(prior_triplets, lik_triplets, z_prior, z_lik, n_mc, n_samples, total) full clay/sand/silt workflow built top : estimates side’s ILR-space (mu, Sigma) low/representative/high triplets via estimate_ilr_moments_mc(), fuses fuse_bivariate_normal() exactly , draws posterior clay/sand/silt samples via sample_ilr_posterior() - guaranteed, construction, sum 100. raster-fusion-ssurgo-solus.Rmd’s “Step 2: Fuse compositional group” demonstrates full chain real SSURGO/SOLUS100 rasters.

what: fuse_property() - top-level entry point, dispatching by input shape
title: Bayesian Updating (Scalar): Fusing Priors with Observed Data
text: Purpose: single entry point inspects shape prior/likelihood (raw-sample vectors vs. named parameter lists) rather requiring caller-supplied method flag, routes accordingly. Parameters: prior, likelihood - raw-sample vectors, named parameter lists matching family; family - required parameter-list route; bounds - unused, kept interface symmetry; method - optional assertion ("general" "closed_form"); errors doesn’t match input shape implies. n_samples, grid_resolution - passed bayesian_update(). two routes deliberately return different shapes (sample vector vs. parameter list) - unified fake-common contract, since caller already knows shape passed therefore shape gets back. Passing method contradicts input shape error rather silent override:
code: # Vector inputs -> routes to bayesian_update() (the general route) fuse_property(prior_samples, lik_samples, n_samples = 500) |> (\(s) c(mean = mean(s), sd = sd(s)))() #>     mean       sd  #> 28.06634  2.80318  # Parameter-list inputs -> routes to bayes_fuse() (the closed-form route) fuse_property(prior_clay, lik_clay, family = "normal") #> $mu #> [1] 28.4 #>  #> $sigma #> [1] 2.683282 fuse_property(prior_clay, lik_clay, family = "normal", method = "general") #> Error in `fuse_property()`: #> ! fuse_property(): method = 'general' was requested but the input shape implies 'closed_form' - pass matching inputs or omit method.

title: Data Acquisition, Cleaning & Infilling: A Function-by-Function Walkthrough
text: infill_soil_property() fills missing _r (representative) values single property using six strategies, tried order, ever using suitable horizons sources: Horizon-name matching (horizon_name_property_infill()) - within group (component), average property horizons whose standardized name similar (similarity > 0.5) target horizon’s name. Depth-weighted averaging (depth_weighted_property_infill()) - within group, inverse-distance-weighted mean horizons within 20 cm depth. Within-component interpolation (within_component_property_interpolation()) - linear (approx()-based) interpolation along depth within component. Cross-component interpolation (cross_component_property_interpolation()) - whole-dataset: borrows components’ suitable horizons within 15 cm depth tolerance. Related-property estimation (related_property_estimation()) - whole-dataset: pedological relationships (e.g. texture sums 100, clay/OM-based CEC). Group-mean fallback (apply_group_fallback_mean()) - last resort: group’s depth-weighted (plain) mean suitable horizons. strategy runs cells prior strategy left unfilled, every filled cell tagged infill_method audit column strategy filled used. infill_soil_property()’s key parameters: df - input data frame (must already unsuitable_horizon computable / present) property_name - single property base name ("rfv" special-cased infill_rfv_property_integrated() instead hierarchy) property_config - optional config get_default_property_config(); auto-looked-NULL max_depth - horizons depth excluded infilled (can still act interpolation/averaging sources shallower horizons profile) verbose - progress logging

text: Alongside fixed hardcoded plausibility bounds apply_basic_range_limits(), soilSIM offers small pluggable rule system callers want additional, custom checks. create_validation_config() returns empty config; add_range_rule() add_relationship_rule() add rules ; apply_validation_rules() evaluates range rules vector values. Applying range rule real clay values shows catching handful unusually clay-rich horizons generic [0, 100] apply_basic_range_limits() bound alone let : Relationship rules like sum--100 texture rule added recorded config currently enforced apply_validation_rules() (evaluates range_rules) - matches legacy reference implementation’s behavior rather oversight introduced , means relationship rule alone won’t flag anything caller writes enforcement config$relationship_rules. Finally, summarize_unsuitable_horizons() (introduced Step 2) worth revisiting reporting counterpart validation layer - tells excluded rather flagged within remained:

See soilSIM/docs/03_distribution_fitting_correlations.md full function-level reference. data vignette small synthetic - hand-constructed numbers, real download - parameter’s effect easy isolate see. Fit percentile triplet five different distribution families compare shapes directly (fit_normal_triplet(), Beta fitting, quantile_linear_cdf(), quantile_triangular(), metalog fitting) resolve_property_family()’s automatic family selection skew, skew_threshold changes decision fit_percentile_triplet() single master dispatcher tying families together fit_beta_mle_newton()’s n_iter parameter - watching Newton-Raphson fit actually converge ILR (isometric log-ratio) compositional transforms: ilr_forward() / ilr_inverse() Correlation-matrix repair: ensure_positive_definite_matrix() validate_correlation_matrix()

text: fit_normal_triplet(p_lo_val, p50_val, p_hi_val, p_lo, p_hi) exact closed-form fit - iteration. mean just median value (p50_val); sd solved directly two-point spread (p_hi_val - p_lo_val) / (qnorm(p_hi) - qnorm(p_lo)), algebraic consequence Normal’s linear quantile function. quantile_normal(fit, q) evaluates mean + sd * qnorm(q) vector probabilities q.
code: normal_fit <- fit_normal_triplet(p_lo_val = l, p50_val = r, p_hi_val = h, p_lo = 0.05, p_hi = 0.95) normal_fit #> $mean #> [1] 25 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 7.59946 quantile_normal(normal_fit, q = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))  # round-trips back to l, r, h #> [1] 12.5 25.0 37.5

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: Every family reproduces l/r/h exactly q = 0.05/0.5/0.95 (’s “fitting triplet” means ) - differs shape connecting three points. Evaluating quantile function fine probability grid differentiating numerically approximates family’s density:  families agree exactly three fitted knots (0.05/0.5/0.95) diverge everywhere else - Triangular angular construction, Normal/Beta/Metalog smooth differently shaped tails, LinearCDF piecewise-straight knots hard clamping beyond (visible flat segments top/bottom curve).
code: q_grid <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)  families <- list(   Normal     = quantile_normal(normal_fit, q_grid),   Beta       = bounds[1] + quantile_beta(beta_fit, q_grid) * diff(bounds),   LinearCDF  = quantile_linear_cdf(c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), c(l, r, h), q_grid),   Triangular = quantile_triangular(triangular_fit, q_grid),   Metalog    = quantile_metalog_linear(metalog_fit, q_grid) )  cdf_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(families), function(fam) {   data.frame(family = fam, q = q_grid, value = families[[fam]]) }))  ggplot(cdf_df, aes(x = value, y = q, color = family)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Family") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Fitted CDFs of the same l/r/h triplet, five families",     subtitle = "l = 15, r = 25, h = 40 at p = 0.05 / 0.50 / 0.95",     x = "Value (clay %)", y = "Cumulative probability"   )

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: resolve_property_family(l, r, h, bounds = NULL, skew_threshold = 0.15) picks family skew proxy ((h - r) - (r - l)) / (h - l) - lopsided high-side spread relative low-side spread around representative value. bounds supplied always resolves "beta"; otherwise "normal" skew proxy within skew_threshold zero, else "lognormal". deliberately never resolves "metalog" - stays explicit, opted-choice. symmetric triplet resolves "normal" (skew proxy exactly 0, well inside default 0.15 threshold); skewed triplets resolve "lognormal". Sliding skew_threshold past triplet’s skew proxy flips decision "lognormal" back "normal": mild-skew triplet’s skew proxy 0.25; skew_threshold rises (0.30, 0.50), triplet resolves "normal" instead "lognormal" - input data, different family, purely threshold drawn. Supplying bounds overrides always resolves "beta":
code: symmetric  <- list(l = 15, r = 25, h = 35)   # (35-25) - (25-15) = 0            -> skew_proxy 0 mild_skew  <- list(l = 15, r = 25, h = 40)   # (40-25) - (25-15) = 5            -> skew_proxy 0.25 strong_skew <- list(l = 20, r = 24, h = 60)  # (60-24) - (24-20) = 32           -> skew_proxy 0.9  triplets <- list(Symmetric = symmetric, `Mild skew` = mild_skew, `Strong skew` = strong_skew)  resolution_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(triplets), function(nm) {   t <- triplets[[nm]]   res <- resolve_property_family(t$l, t$r, t$h)   data.frame(triplet = nm, l = t$l, r = t$r, h = t$h,              skew_proxy = round(res$skew_proxy, 3), family = res$family) })) resolution_df #>       triplet  l  r  h skew_proxy    family #> 1   Symmetric 15 25 35        0.0    normal #> 2   Mild skew 15 25 40        0.2 lognormal #> 3 Strong skew 20 24 60        0.8 lognormal thresholds <- c(0.05, 0.15, 0.30, 0.50) threshold_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(thresholds, function(th) {   res <- resolve_property_family(mild_skew$l, mild_skew$r, mild_skew$h, skew_threshold = th)   data.frame(skew_threshold = th, skew_proxy = round(res$skew_proxy, 3), family = res$family) })) threshold_df #>   skew_threshold skew_proxy    family #> 1           0.05        0.2 lognormal #> 2           0.15        0.2 lognormal #> 3           0.30        0.2    normal #> 4           0.50        0.2    normal resolve_property_family(mild_skew$l, mild_skew$r, mild_skew$h, bounds = c(0, 100))$family #> [1] "beta"

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: fit_percentile_triplet(l, r, h, family, lh_probs = c(0.05, 0.95), bounds = NULL, boundedness = ...) single entry point rest soilSIM calls - wraps every fitter shown Step 1 behind one family argument ("triangular", "uniform", "normal", "lognormal", "beta", "metalog", "linear_cdf", "auto"), plus two degenerate-input guards: non-finite l/r/h returns valid = FALSE, zero-width interval (h == l) always collapses triangular fit min = mode = max = r regardless requested family, since every parametric family divides zero zero-width interval. family = "auto" bounds resolves resolve_property_family() exactly Step 2 (triplet’s skew proxy 0.25 exceeds default 0.15 threshold, resolves "lognormal"). fitted, quantile_from_fit(u, family, fit) matching master quantile dispatcher - round-trip Step 1 built hand family individually: zero-width-interval guard, demonstrated directly:
code: for (fam in c("normal", "beta", "lognormal", "triangular", "metalog", "auto")) {   result <- fit_percentile_triplet(l, r, h, family = fam, bounds = if (fam == "beta") bounds else NULL)   cat(sprintf("%-10s -> resolved family = %-10s valid = %s\n", fam, result$family, result$valid)) } #> normal     -> resolved family = normal     valid = TRUE #> beta       -> resolved family = beta       valid = TRUE #> lognormal  -> resolved family = lognormal  valid = TRUE #> triangular -> resolved family = triangular valid = TRUE #> metalog    -> resolved family = metalog    valid = TRUE #> auto       -> resolved family = lognormal  valid = TRUE auto_fit <- fit_percentile_triplet(l, r, h, family = "auto") quantile_from_fit(u = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), family = auto_fit$family, fit = auto_fit$fit) #> [1] 15.30931 25.00000 40.82483 fit_percentile_triplet(l = 25, r = 25, h = 25, family = "beta", bounds = bounds) #> $family #> [1] "triangular" #>  #> $fit #> $fit$min #> [1] 25 #>  #> $fit$mode #> [1] 25 #>  #> $fit$max #> [1] 25 #>  #>  #> $valid #> [1] TRUE

what: Step 4: fit_beta_mle_newton()’s n_iter parameter - watching convergence
title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: fit_beta_mle_newton(values, bounds, n_iter = 15, eps = 1e-6) runs fixed number Newton-Raphson steps - internal convergence check, n_iter directly controls close fit gets true MLE. Refitting values increasing n_iter shows shape parameters (resulting quantiles) settle steps:  shape1 (shape2, plotted) moves n_iter = 1 n_iter = 3, barely changes n_iter = 5 onward - n_iter = 15 (soilSIM’s default everywhere else) well past point diminishing returns triplet, exactly fixed iteration count without convergence check safe design choice .
code: n_iters <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15) convergence_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(n_iters, function(ni) {   fit_i <- fit_beta_mle_newton(values = c(l, r, h), bounds = bounds, n_iter = ni)   q_i <- bounds[1] + quantile_beta(fit_i, q = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)) * diff(bounds)   data.frame(n_iter = ni, shape1 = fit_i$shape1, shape2 = fit_i$shape2,              q05 = q_i[1], q50 = q_i[2], q95 = q_i[3]) })) convergence_df #>   n_iter   shape1   shape2      q05      q50      q95 #> 1      1 4.876135 13.40713 11.66420 25.80474 44.64633 #> 2      2 4.885615 13.43308 11.67634 25.80661 44.62864 #> 3      3 4.885634 13.43313 11.67637 25.80662 44.62860 #> 4      5 4.885634 13.43313 11.67637 25.80662 44.62860 #> 5     10 4.885634 13.43313 11.67637 25.80662 44.62860 #> 6     15 4.885634 13.43313 11.67637 25.80662 44.62860 ggplot(convergence_df, aes(x = n_iter, y = shape1)) +   geom_line(color = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.2), linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(aes(color = n_iter), size = 3) +   scale_color_viridis_c(guide = "none") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "fit_beta_mle_newton(): shape1 converges within a few Newton-Raphson steps",     x = "n_iter", y = "Fitted shape1"   )

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: Soil texture (clay/sand/silt) 3-part composition must sum fixed total (e.g. 100%) stay non-negative - ordinary independent simulation fraction can’t guarantee . ilr_forward()/ilr_inverse() soilSIM’s isometric log-ratio transform: move composition /2-dimensional unconstrained coordinate system ordinary Normal-distribution machinery applies safely, constraint automatically satisfied way back. Perturbing ILR coordinates inverting always yields valid composition - non-negative summing exactly total - point simulation ILR space rather directly clay/sand/silt:  Every bar stack sums exactly 100 - ilr_inverse()’s softmax-like normalization guarantees construction, finite z1/z2.
code: # A synthetic clay/sand/silt composition example_composition <- c(clay = 24, sand = 40, silt = 36) sum(example_composition) #> [1] 100  z <- ilr_forward(clay = example_composition["clay"], sand = example_composition["sand"],                   silt = example_composition["silt"]) z  # 2 unconstrained coordinates, z1/z2 #>              z1         z2 #> clay -0.3740741 0.07450114 back <- ilr_inverse(z1 = z[, "z1"], z2 = z[, "z2"], total = 100) back  # round-trips back to the original composition #>      clay sand silt #> [1,]   24   40   36 sum(back) #> [1] 100 set.seed(42) z1_perturbed <- z[, "z1"] + seq(-1.5, 1.5, length.out = 9) z2_perturbed <- rep(z[, "z2"], 9) perturbed_compositions <- as.data.frame(ilr_inverse(z1_perturbed, z2_perturbed, total = 100)) perturbed_compositions$step <- seq_len(9)  stack_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("clay", "sand", "silt"), function(part) {   data.frame(step = perturbed_compositions$step, fraction = part,              pct = perturbed_compositions[[part]]) }))  ggplot(stack_df, aes(x = step, y = pct, fill = fraction)) +   geom_col() +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "ilr_inverse(): every reconstructed composition stays valid",     subtitle = "z1 swept across a range at fixed z2 - always sums to 100, always non-negative",     x = "Step (increasing z1)", y = "Percent"   )

title: Distribution Fitting & Correlations: A Function-by-Function Tour
text: Multi-property Monte Carlo simulation needs positive-definite (PD) correlation matrix Cholesky-copula step. Empirically estimated hand-assembled correlation matrices always PD - ensure_positive_definite_matrix() repairs one via eigenvalue flooring, validate_correlation_matrix() checks whether candidate matrix already usable. deliberately broken, non-positive-definite 3x3 correlation matrix (valid-looking diagonal range, internally inconsistent pairwise correlations): ensure_positive_definite_matrix(matrix, min_eigenvalue = 1e-6) eigendecomposes matrix, floors eigenvalue min_eigenvalue, reconstructs, rescales back unit-diagonal correlation matrix (also restoring original dimnames, eigen()$vectors carry): Raising min_eigenvalue pushes repaired matrix (broken) original toward better-conditioned less “confident” correlation structure - visible -diagonal correlations shrinking toward zero floor rises:  validate_correlation_matrix(corr_matrix, properties) cheaper, non-repairing counterpart - checks shape (square, matching length(properties)), unit diagonal, positive definiteness, returning first failing check’s message rather fixing anything. Together two functions shared final guard estimate_correlation_matrix_robust() build_kssl_fallback_matrix() route correlation matrices Cholesky-copula simulation step consumes .
code: broken_matrix <- matrix(   c( 1.0,  0.9, -0.9,      0.9,  1.0,  0.9,     -0.9,  0.9,  1.0),   nrow = 3, dimnames = list(c("clay", "sand", "silt"), c("clay", "sand", "silt")) ) broken_matrix #>      clay sand silt #> clay  1.0  0.9 -0.9 #> sand  0.9  1.0  0.9 #> silt -0.9  0.9  1.0 eigen(broken_matrix, only.values = TRUE)$values  # a negative eigenvalue confirms it's not PD #> [1]  1.9  1.9 -0.8 validate_correlation_matrix(broken_matrix, properties = c("clay", "sand", "silt")) #> $valid #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $message #> [1] "Matrix is not positive definite" repaired_matrix <- ensure_positive_definite_matrix(broken_matrix) repaired_matrix #>            clay      sand       silt #> clay  1.0000000 0.4999996 -0.4999996 #> sand  0.4999996 1.0000000  0.4999996 #> silt -0.4999996 0.4999996  1.0000000 eigen(repaired_matrix, only.values = TRUE)$values  # all positive now #> [1] 1.500000e+00 1.500000e+00 7.894735e-07 validate_correlation_matrix(repaired_matrix, properties = c("clay", "sand", "silt")) #> $valid #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $message #> [1] "" floors <- c(1e-6, 0.01, 0.1, 0.3) floor_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(floors, function(mv) {   r <- ensure_positive_definite_matrix(broken_matrix, min_eigenvalue = mv)   data.frame(min_eigenvalue = mv, clay_sand = r["clay", "sand"], clay_silt = r["clay", "silt"],              sand_silt = r["sand", "silt"]) })) floor_df_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("clay_sand", "clay_silt", "sand_silt"), function(pair) {   data.frame(min_eigenvalue = floor_df$min_eigenvalue, pair = pair, correlation = floor_df[[pair]]) }))  ggplot(floor_df_long, aes(x = factor(min_eigenvalue), y = correlation, color = pair, group = pair)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(size = 2.5) +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Property pair") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "ensure_positive_definite_matrix(): higher min_eigenvalue shrinks correlations",     x = "min_eigenvalue", y = "Repaired correlation"   )

text: vignette walks soilSIM’s core tabular pipeline end end, using real SSURGO data small area interest (AOI) Sierra Nevada foothills Amador County, California: Download clean real SSURGO tabular data AOI Fill missing property values Fit percentile-triplet distributions run correlated Monte Carlo simulation Characterize simulated output statistically Fit Gaussian-process depth-trend models next step toward depth-aware simulation Every number vignette originated real download NRCS Soil Data Access - see “data came ” note . See soilSIM/docs/01_data_acquisition_processing.md, 03_distribution_fitting_correlations.md, 04_monte_carlo_simulation.md, 05_gp_modeling_multivariate_adjustment.md full function-level reference behind step.
code: library(soilSIM) library(ggplot2)

what: Step 1: Acquire and process real SSURGO data
title: Getting Started: Tabular Monte Carlo Simulation from SSURGO
text: AOI small polygon (1 km x 1 km) near Amador County, CA: download_and_prepare_ssurgo() queries NRCS Soil Data Access live AOI, filters maximum depth. call shown reference, vignette loads cached copy real output vignette builds without live network dependency: AOI resolves 66 real map units 116 soil components. process_ssurgo_data() cleans standardizes raw download - flagging unsuitable horizons (bedrock, cemented pans, organic layers) shouldn’t feed property simulation:
code: amador_wkt <- "POLYGON((-120.5 38.5, -120.4 38.5, -120.4 38.6, -120.5 38.6, -120.5 38.5))" # The real call this vignette's cached data came from: ssurgo_amador <- download_and_prepare_ssurgo(   aoi_wkt = amador_wkt,   properties = c("sandtotal", "claytotal", "silttotal", "dbovendry", "ph1to1h2o",                  "cec7", "om", "wthirdbar", "wfifteenbar"),   max_depth = 150 ) ssurgo_amador <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ssurgo_amador.rds", package = "soilSIM")) raw_data <- ssurgo_amador$ssurgo_data dim(raw_data) #> [1] 575  67 length(unique(raw_data$cokey)) #> [1] 116 length(unique(raw_data$mukey)) #> [1] 66 processed <- process_ssurgo_data(raw_data, max_depth = 150, verbose = FALSE) horizon_data <- processed$processed_data sum(horizon_data$unsuitable_horizon) #> [1] 84

what: Step 2: Fill in missing property values
title: Getting Started: Tabular Monte Carlo Simulation from SSURGO
text: Real SSURGO data gaps - process_soil_properties_comprehensive() fills using pedologically informed recovery strategies (horizon-name matching, depth-weighted averaging, related-property estimation) rather blind mean-impute:
code: properties <- c("sandtotal", "claytotal", "silttotal", "dbovendry") infilled <- process_soil_properties_comprehensive(horizon_data, properties = properties, verbose = FALSE) mean(infilled$property_data_complete, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 1

what: Step 3: Fit distributions and run the Monte Carlo simulation
title: Getting Started: Tabular Monte Carlo Simulation from SSURGO
text: soilSIM’s percentile-triplet fitter (fit_percentile_triplet()) turns property’s SSURGO low/representative/high values fitted distribution. clay content first suitable horizon: generate_monte_carlo_realizations() master pipeline: fitting every property/horizon, estimates (falls back KSSL reference) correlation structure across properties, draws correlated realizations: 491 suitable horizons x 4 properties x 200 realizations, 100% success rate. Distribution simulated clay content across realizations, first horizon:  Monte Carlo engine’s whole point preserving cross-property correlation structure, just marginal distributions - ’s worth checking actually happened. mc_result$simulation_data [horizon, property, realization] array; correlation matrix computed across realizations horizon, averaged suitable horizons:
code: first_row <- infilled[!infilled$unsuitable_horizon, ][1, ] clay_fit <- fit_percentile_triplet(   l = first_row$claytotal_l, r = first_row$claytotal_r, h = first_row$claytotal_h,   family = "normal" ) quantile_from_fit(u = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95), family = clay_fit$family, fit = clay_fit$fit) #> [1]  5 10 15 mc_result <- generate_monte_carlo_realizations(   soil_data = infilled,   properties = properties,   n_realizations = 200,   simulation_config = list(     max_depth = 150,     auto_correlation = TRUE,     correlation_fallback = "kssl_global"   ),   parallel = FALSE,   seed = 123 )  dim(mc_result$simulation_data)  # [horizon, property, realization] #> [1] 491   4 200 mc_result$metadata$success_rate #> [1] 1 mc_result$quality_assessment$overall_quality_score #> [1] 1 clay_col <- match("claytotal", properties) clay_realizations <- data.frame(clay = mc_result$simulation_data[1, clay_col, ])  ggplot(clay_realizations, aes(x = clay, fill = after_stat(count))) +   geom_histogram(bins = 20, color = "white") +   scale_fill_viridis_c() +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Simulated clay content, horizon 1",     x = "Clay (%)",     y = "Count of realizations"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "none") prop_names <- dimnames(mc_result$simulation_data)[[2]] n_horizons <- dim(mc_result$simulation_data)[1] n_props <- length(prop_names)  cor_by_horizon <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(n_props, n_props, n_horizons)) for (h in seq_len(n_horizons)) {   realizations_by_property <- t(mc_result$simulation_data[h, , ])   cor_by_horizon[, , h] <- cor(realizations_by_property, use = "pairwise.complete.obs") } mean_cor <- apply(cor_by_horizon, c(1, 2), mean, na.rm = TRUE) dimnames(mean_cor) <- list(prop_names, prop_names)  cor_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(mean_cor)) names(cor_df) <- c("property_1", "property_2", "correlation")  ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = property_1, y = property_2, fill = correlation)) +   geom_tile() +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)), color = "white", size = 3.5) +   scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Cross-property correlation of simulated realizations",     subtitle = "Averaged across all suitable horizons",     x = NULL, y = NULL   ) +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

what: Step 4: Characterize the simulated data statistically
title: Getting Started: Tabular Monte Carlo Simulation from SSURGO
text: analyze_soil_statistics() runs correlation analysis, distribution fitting, outlier detection processed data (real Amador dataset Step 1):
code: stats_result <- analyze_soil_statistics(horizon_data, verbose = FALSE) stats_result$analysis_metadata$properties_analyzed #> [1] 16

what: Step 5: Toward depth-aware simulation - Gaussian process depth trends
title: Getting Started: Tabular Monte Carlo Simulation from SSURGO
text: Monte Carlo simulation treats every suitable horizon independently. soilSIM’s GP modeling group (build_stratified_gp_models()) fits depth-trend models per soil group, simulated properties can follow realistic depth trend rather horizon--horizon independence. prepare_nrcs_training_data() automatically selects grouping strategy - AOI, selects grouping soil series: 26 GP models fit across 7 real soil-series groups AOI. fitted model predicts property’s mean depth trend (uncertainty) soil-series group via predict_gp_depth_trends(). clay content first group:  , integrate_monte_carlo_with_gp() (see soilSIM/docs/05_gp_modeling_multivariate_adjustment.md) combines depth-trend models Monte Carlo simulation like mc_result , nudging realization toward group’s fitted depth trend preserving cross-property correlation structure - natural next step beyond vignette’s scope.
code: gp_train <- prepare_nrcs_training_data(horizon_data, max_depth = 150) table(gp_train$soil_group) #>  #>     Chaix  Cohasset   Holland Josephine  Mariposa  McCarthy     Sites  #>        24       118        21        81        50        60        31 gp_models <- build_stratified_gp_models(   gp_train,   properties = c("clay_pct", "sand_pct", "pH", "organic_matter"),   min_profiles_per_group = 3,   min_observations_per_group = 15,   optimize_hyperparameters = FALSE ) gp_models$model_summary$total_models #> [1] 26 clay_groups <- names(gp_models$clay_pct$models) first_group <- clay_groups[1] clay_gp_model <- gp_models$clay_pct$models[[first_group]]  depth_seq <- seq(0, 150, by = 5) gp_mean <- predict_gp_depth_trends(clay_gp_model, depth_seq)  # predict_gp_depth_trends() returns the fitted mean only; pull the prediction # variance directly from GPfit to draw an uncertainty band around it scaling <- clay_gp_model$depth_scaling scaled_depths <- pmax(0, pmin(1, (depth_seq - scaling$min) / scaling$range)) gp_pred <- GPfit::predict.GP(clay_gp_model$gp_model, xnew = as.matrix(scaled_depths)) gp_se <- sqrt(pmax(gp_pred$MSE, 0))  gp_depth_trend <- data.frame(   depth = depth_seq,   mean = gp_mean,   lower = gp_mean - 1.96 * gp_se,   upper = gp_mean + 1.96 * gp_se )  ggplot(gp_depth_trend, aes(x = depth, y = mean)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.5), alpha = 0.25) +   geom_line(color = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.15), linewidth = 1) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = paste0("GP depth trend: clay content, \"", first_group, "\" soil group"),     subtitle = "Shaded band is a 95% prediction interval",     x = "Depth (cm)",     y = "Clay content (%)"   )
