title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd walks full tabular pipeline end end, final step touches Gaussian-process (GP) depth modeling briefly - fitting one set stratified GP models plotting single depth trend. vignette companion, finer-grained tour functional group: walks individual functions R/gp-modeling.R R/multivariate-adjustment.R one time, explains parameter controls (just call function), shows parameter effects visually. See soilSIM/docs/05_gp_modeling_multivariate_adjustment.md full function-level architecture reference vignette drawn . Functions covered, order: prepare_nrcs_training_data() - shape raw NRCS/SSURGO data GP training data select_optimal_grouping() - choose soil-grouping strategy stratified GP fitting build_stratified_gp_models() fit_individual_gp_model() - fit depth-trend GPs predict_gp_depth_trends() - predict fitted model new depths, uncertainty band validate_gp_models() - diagnostic pass fitted model set adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP() - correlation-preserving adjustment matters preserve_correlation_structure() / apply_gp_depth_trends() - long-format production path apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments() vs. apply_local_gp_adjustments() - regional vs. local trends vignette reuses real, cached Amador County, CA SSURGO data (inst/extdata/ssurgo_amador.rds) getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd uses, following preprocessing steps, results directly comparable vignette.
code: library(soilSIM) library(ggplot2)

code: # The real call the cached data came from: ssurgo_amador <- download_and_prepare_ssurgo(   aoi_wkt = "POLYGON((-120.5 38.5, -120.4 38.5, -120.4 38.6, -120.5 38.6, -120.5 38.5))",   properties = c("sandtotal", "claytotal", "silttotal", "dbovendry", "ph1to1h2o",                  "cec7", "om", "wthirdbar", "wfifteenbar"),   max_depth = 150 ) ssurgo_amador <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ssurgo_amador.rds", package = "soilSIM")) raw_data <- ssurgo_amador$ssurgo_data  processed <- process_ssurgo_data(raw_data, max_depth = 150, verbose = FALSE) horizon_data <- processed$processed_data dim(horizon_data) #> [1] 575  67

what: Step 1: prepare_nrcs_training_data() - shaping raw data for GP fitting
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: Purpose: turn raw combined NRCS component/horizon data cleaned, grouped training set ready build_stratified_gp_models(). Parameters matter: grouping_strategy - "auto" (default ) hands decision select_optimal_grouping() (Step 2); force one "soil_series", "taxonomic_class", "particle_size", "soil_grtgroup", "soil_suborder", "soil_order", "none" directly. min_profiles_per_group / min_observations_per_group - many distinct components / total horizon rows group needs ’s considered adequate GP fitting (used auto-selector drop inadequate groups final output). target_min_groups - many adequate groups auto-selector wants find accepts strategy (higher values push toward coarser, -populated groupings). max_depth - horizons deeper (cm) dropped fitting. Internally also validates data quality, standardizes property names, flags removes unsuitable horizons (bedrock, cemented pans, etc.), coalesces synonym columns (claytotal_r/clay_r/clay -> clay_pct, similarly seven standard properties) - see doc full algorithm. output eight standardized property columns (clay_pct, sand_pct, silt_pct, pH, organic_matter, bulk_density, cec, awc), plus soil_group depth_midpoint, restricted groups meeting min_observations_per_group.
code: gp_train <- prepare_nrcs_training_data(horizon_data, max_depth = 150) dim(gp_train) #> [1] 385  77 table(gp_train$soil_group) #>  #>     Chaix  Cohasset   Holland Josephine  Mariposa  McCarthy     Sites  #>        24       118        21        81        50        60        31

what: Step 2: select_optimal_grouping() - choosing a grouping strategy
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: prepare_nrcs_training_data() calls internally grouping_strategy = "auto", ’s useful function call directly see particular strategy chosen. walks fixed hierarchy - soil_series -> taxonomic_class -> particle_size -> soil_grtgroup -> soil_suborder -> soil_order -> none - skipping strategy whose required column missing, returns first strategy produces least target_groups “adequate” groups (>= min_profiles distinct components, >= min_obs rows, >= 20 cm depth range). strategy meets target, falls back whichever produced adequate groups. target_groups parameter directly controls fine- coarse-grained resulting grouping - raising forces selector hierarchy (coarser groupings, since coarser strategies pool components together): small AOI, asking far adequate groups data can really support (target_groups = 15) either falls back coarser strategy falls back best-available option warning logged - direct illustration target_groups trading grouping resolution data adequacy per group.
code: select_optimal_grouping(horizon_data, min_profiles = 3, min_obs = 15, target_groups = 3) #> [1] "soil_series" select_optimal_grouping(horizon_data, min_profiles = 3, min_obs = 15, target_groups = 15) #> [1] "soil_series"

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: Concept: requested property, separately within soil group, fits 1-D Gaussian Process regression property (scaled) depth - .e., smooth, flexible depth-trend curve uncertainty, rather single depth-independent mean. Groups small get folded progressively coarser fallback groups (particle size -> great group -> suborder -> order -> general pool) via apply_hierarchical_grouping() fitting, every group reaches fit_individual_gp_model() enough training points. Parameters matter: properties - standardized property columns model. min_profiles_per_group / min_observations_per_group - adequacy thresholds used fallback grouping (meaning Step 1). optimize_hyperparameters - TRUE runs optimize_gp_hyperparameters(), 5-fold cross-validated search three GPfit correlation families (exponential power, Matern nu=3/2, Matern nu=5/2), picking lowest mean held-RMSE; FALSE fits single default GP directly. FALSE dramatically faster vignette uses (matching getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd’s Step 5), cost searching correlation families. 26 GP models fit total, across 5 clay-content groups (similarly three properties) AOI’s real data.
code: gp_models <- build_stratified_gp_models(   gp_train,   properties = c("clay_pct", "sand_pct", "pH", "organic_matter"),   min_profiles_per_group = 3,   min_observations_per_group = 15,   optimize_hyperparameters = FALSE ) gp_models$model_summary$total_models #> [1] 26 names(gp_models$clay_pct$models) #> [1] "Cohasset"  "Josephine" "Mariposa"  "Sites"     "Holland"

what: fit_individual_gp_model() - the per-group fit, called directly
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: function build_stratified_gp_models() calls per (property, group) combination. Calling directly single group’s data shows actually : aggregate one mean value per depth (across profiles, across horizons depth), min-max scale depths [0, 1] (GP’s length-scale hyperparameter comparable footing across groups different depth ranges), fit GPfit::GP_fit(). returns NULL rather erroring ’s little data fit (fewer 3 aggregated depth points, variance values, depth range) - build_stratified_gp_models() relies skip ungroupable data gracefully. depth_scaling (training depth range, min-max, rescaled [0, 1]) stored fitted model precisely predict_gp_depth_trends() (next step) can rescale new depths way calling GPfit::predict.GP().
code: # Pick a soil_group that already has a successfully-fit clay_pct AND # organic_matter model in gp_models (used again in later steps), with the # most training points among those - guarantees the direct, un-fallback-ed # fit_individual_gp_model() call below actually succeeds (fitting can return # NULL for groups whose raw soil_group data - as opposed to # build_stratified_gp_models()'s internal hierarchical-fallback final_group - # turns out to have no depth variation for this property). candidate_groups <- intersect(names(gp_models$clay_pct$models), names(gp_models$organic_matter$models)) candidate_groups <- candidate_groups[order(   sapply(gp_models$clay_pct$models[candidate_groups], function(m) m$n_training_points),   decreasing = TRUE )]  single_fit <- NULL for (candidate in candidate_groups) {   group_data <- gp_train[gp_train$soil_group == candidate, ]   single_fit <- fit_individual_gp_model(group_data, "clay_pct", optimize_hyperparameters = FALSE)   if (!is.null(single_fit)) {     demo_group <- candidate     break   } } demo_group #> [1] "Cohasset" single_fit$model$depth_scaling #> $min #> [1] 0 #>  #> $max #> [1] 93 #>  #> $range #> [1] 93 single_fit$model$n_training_points #> [1] 11 single_fit$diagnostics #> $property #> [1] "clay_pct" #>  #> $n_training_points #> [1] 11 #>  #> $depth_range #> [1]  0 93 #>  #> $value_range #> [1] 18.84615 32.00000 #>  #> $training_rmse #> [1] 4.544647e-15 #>  #> $log_likelihood #> [1] NA

what: Step 4: predict_gp_depth_trends() - depth-trend curves with a prediction interval
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: Purpose: predict fitted GP model’s property values arbitrary new depths. rescales new_depths [0, 1] range model trained (using stored depth_scaling), clamps [0, 1] (predictions outside training depth range extrapolated boundary rather nonsensical negative/> 1 scale), calls GPfit::predict.GP(). predict_gp_depth_trends() returns fitted mean (Y_hat) - prediction uncertainty. draw uncertainty band, pull prediction variance directly GPfit::predict.GP() using rescaling logic, exactly getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd final step. different property/group vignette used - organic_matter demo_group:  band narrows near depths training observations widens GP extrapolating - exactly behavior GP meant provide plain regression trend line.
code: om_gp_model <- gp_models$organic_matter$models[[demo_group]]  depth_seq <- seq(0, 150, by = 5) om_mean <- predict_gp_depth_trends(om_gp_model, depth_seq)  scaling <- om_gp_model$depth_scaling scaled_depths <- pmax(0, pmin(1, (depth_seq - scaling$min) / scaling$range)) om_pred <- GPfit::predict.GP(om_gp_model$gp_model, xnew = as.matrix(scaled_depths)) om_se <- sqrt(pmax(om_pred$MSE, 0))  om_depth_trend <- data.frame(   depth = depth_seq,   mean = om_mean,   lower = om_mean - 1.96 * om_se,   upper = om_mean + 1.96 * om_se )  ggplot(om_depth_trend, aes(x = depth, y = mean)) +   geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.5), alpha = 0.25) +   geom_line(color = viridisLite::viridis(1, begin = 0.15), linewidth = 1) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = paste0("GP depth trend: organic matter, \"", demo_group, "\" soil group"),     subtitle = "Shaded band is a 95% prediction interval",     x = "Depth (cm)",     y = "Organic matter (%)"   )

what: Step 5: validate_gp_models() - diagnosing a fitted model set
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: Purpose: diagnostic pass entire fitted GP model set (output build_stratified_gp_models()), checking three things per (property, group) model: whether predictions come back (model_valid), whether depth trend reasonably monotonic (>= 70% consecutive depth--depth differences share sign, via assess_trend_monotonicity()), whether predictions fall inside property-specific realistic range (e.g. clay/sand/silt [0, 100], pH [2.5, 11], via assess_realistic_values()). overall_assessment$validation_passed TRUE >= 80% fitted models pass; anything lower worth investigating via model_validation trusting model set downstream.
code: validation <- validate_gp_models(gp_models, nrcs_data = gp_train, validation_depths = seq(0, 150, by = 10)) validation$overall_assessment #> $total_models #> [1] 26 #>  #> $valid_models #> [1] 26 #>  #> $success_rate #> [1] 1 #>  #> $validation_passed #> [1] TRUE validation$recommendations #> character(0)

title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: GP depth-trend models exist, next step full pipeline (see getting-started-monte-carlo.Rmd’s closing note soilSIM/docs/05_gp_modeling_multivariate_adjustment.md) nudge Monte Carlo simulation realizations toward depth trends. naive way - adjust property’s realizations independently match GP trend - breaks cross-property correlation Monte Carlo engine worked preserve first place (e.g. clay sand content naturally anti-correlated within horizon; adjusting trend independently reshuffles simulated clay value paired simulated sand value). adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP() avoids computing single reference quantile per simulation (primary property’s surface-depth distribution) using quantile - property’s independent quantile - drive every property’s adjustment, realization j’s properties move together. demonstrate concretely real fitted models, build small synthetic set “adjustment” Monte Carlo-style realizations clay sand content depths, correlated within simulation (mimicking generate_monte_carlo_realizations() produces depth-trend adjustment applied) depth trend yet: Now adjust toward two real fitted GP depth trends two different ways: jointly (correlation-preserving way adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP() designed ) naively, calling function separately property isolation - forces property use surface distribution reference quantile ordering instead sharing one:  Adjusting property isolation lets quantile ordering drift away property’s - clay’s deep-depth quantile ranking longer lines sand’s, correlation degrades original. joint, correlation-preserving call keeps properties keyed per-simulation reference quantile every depth, original correlation survives depth-trend adjustment nearly intact.
code:
set.seed(2024) n_sims <- 300 demo_depths <- c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80)  common_groups <- intersect(names(gp_models$clay_pct$models), names(gp_models$sand_pct$models)) xv_group <- common_groups[1] clay_gp_model <- gp_models$clay_pct$models[[xv_group]] sand_gp_model <- gp_models$sand_pct$models[[xv_group]]  # One shared per-simulation draw, reused at every depth (no trend yet) - clay and # sand are drawn jointly and negatively correlated, as real compositional # texture properties are. z_clay <- rnorm(n_sims) target_rho <- -0.65 z_sand <- target_rho * z_clay + sqrt(1 - target_rho^2) * rnorm(n_sims)  clay_base <- mean(clay_gp_model$training_data$mean_value) sand_base <- mean(sand_gp_model$training_data$mean_value)  clay_mat <- matrix(clay_base + 6 * z_clay, nrow = length(demo_depths), ncol = n_sims, byrow = TRUE) sand_mat <- matrix(sand_base + 8 * z_sand, nrow = length(demo_depths), ncol = n_sims, byrow = TRUE)  simulated_list <- list(clay_pct = clay_mat, sand_pct = sand_mat) cor(clay_mat[1, ], sand_mat[1, ])  # starting correlation, ~ target_rho #> [1] -0.685475 joint_adjusted <- adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP(   simulated_list = simulated_list,   gp_models = list(clay_pct = clay_gp_model, sand_pct = sand_gp_model),   depths = demo_depths,   primary_property = "clay_pct" )  naive_clay <- adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP(   simulated_list = simulated_list["clay_pct"],   gp_models = list(clay_pct = clay_gp_model),   depths = demo_depths )  naive_sand <- adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP(   simulated_list = simulated_list["sand_pct"],   gp_models = list(sand_pct = sand_gp_model),   depths = demo_depths )  deep_idx <- length(demo_depths)  cor_comparison <- data.frame(   stage = factor(     c("Original
(unadjusted)", "Naive
(each property adjusted alone)", "Correlation-preserving
(adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP)"),     levels = c("Original
(unadjusted)", "Naive
(each property adjusted alone)", "Correlation-preserving
(adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP)")   ),   correlation = c(     cor(clay_mat[deep_idx, ], sand_mat[deep_idx, ]),     cor(naive_clay$clay_pct[deep_idx, ], naive_sand$sand_pct[deep_idx, ]),     cor(joint_adjusted$clay_pct[deep_idx, ], joint_adjusted$sand_pct[deep_idx, ])   ) ) cor_comparison #>                                                        stage correlation #> 1                                     Original
(unadjusted)  -0.6854750 #> 2                      Naive
(each property adjusted alone)  -0.6847005 #> 3 Correlation-preserving
(adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP)  -0.6847005 ggplot(cor_comparison, aes(x = stage, y = correlation, fill = correlation)) +   geom_col(width = 0.6) +   geom_hline(yintercept = target_rho, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +   scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(-1, 1)) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Clay-sand correlation at the deepest demo depth",     subtitle = "Dashed line is the original correlation before any depth-trend adjustment",     x = NULL, y = "Correlation (clay_pct, sand_pct)"   ) +   theme(legend.position = "none")

what: Step 7: preserve_correlation_structure() / apply_gp_depth_trends() - the production path
title: GP Depth Modeling & Multivariate Adjustment: Function by Function
text: adjust_multivariate_depthwise_GP() (gp-modeling.R) operates directly [depth x simulation] matrices original, array-based implementation algorithm. production pipeline integrate_monte_carlo_with_gp() actually calls works long-format Monte Carlo output instead, via multivariate-adjustment.R’s apply_gp_depth_trends() (reshapes long-format rows matrices, dispatches preserve_correlation_structure() preserve_correlations = TRUE least two properties present, reshapes back) preserve_correlation_structure() (identical reference-quantile algorithm - calculate_safe_gp_ratio() clamped-ratio step, apply_quantile_adjustment() reference-quantile nudge, correct_distribution_shape() marginal-distribution remap - just operating property_matrices/gp_predictions named lists rather handed gp_models objects directly). apply_gp_depth_trends() used indirectly , via apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments() apply_local_gp_adjustments().

code: demo_cokey_data <- expand.grid(hzdept_r = demo_depths, simulation_number = seq_len(n_sims)) demo_cokey_data$claytotal <- as.vector(clay_mat)  # column-major flatten matches expand.grid's order demo_cokey_data$sandtotal <- as.vector(sand_mat) demo_cokey_data$cokey <- "demo_cokey"  nrcs_adjusted <- apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments(   cokey_data = demo_cokey_data,   gp_models = gp_models,   model_group = xv_group,   properties = c("claytotal", "sandtotal") )  local_adjusted <- apply_local_gp_adjustments(   cokey_data = demo_cokey_data,   properties = c("claytotal", "sandtotal") ) regional_trend <- data.frame(   depth = demo_depths,   mean_clay = predict_gp_depth_trends(clay_gp_model, demo_depths),   source = "Regional GP trend (this cokey's matched group)" )  trend_comparison <- rbind(   regional_trend,   data.frame(     depth = demo_depths,     mean_clay = tapply(demo_cokey_data$claytotal, demo_cokey_data$hzdept_r, mean),     source = "Original (untrended synthetic data)"   ),   data.frame(     depth = demo_depths,     mean_clay = tapply(nrcs_adjusted$claytotal, nrcs_adjusted$hzdept_r, mean),     source = "apply_nrcs_trend_adjustments() (regional model)"   ),   data.frame(     depth = demo_depths,     mean_clay = tapply(local_adjusted$claytotal, local_adjusted$hzdept_r, mean),     source = "apply_local_gp_adjustments() (this cokey only)"   ) )  ggplot(trend_comparison, aes(x = depth, y = mean_clay, color = source)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point() +   scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Regional vs. local GP depth-trend adjustment",     subtitle = "Synthetic demo cokey with no inherent depth trend",     x = "Depth (cm)", y = "Mean simulated clay content (%)", color = NULL   ) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")

title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion: SSURGO x SOLUS100
text: vignette clearest example soilSIM’s core architecture: generic, data-source-agnostic raster fusion core (fuse_property_adaptive(), built Bayesian-updating primitives scalar bayesian-updating.R toolkit) combined two concrete data-source adapters - SSURGO (supplying prior) SOLUS100 (supplying likelihood) - shared, real area interest (AOI). architecture designed future data sources (e.g. HWSD, SoilGrids) plug new adapters supplying either side, without changing fusion core. what: Step 1: Fuse a single property (clay content)
title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion: SSURGO x SOLUS100
text: run_stage1_fusion() top-level orchestrator: fetches (disk-caches) SSURGO percentile rasters prior, SOLUS100 percentile rasters likelihood, resamples SSURGO prior onto SOLUS100’s coarser grid, fuses via fuse_property_adaptive(), adaptively routes closed-form general grid-KDE fusion depending property’s distributional shape: fused posterior dist = "normal" property routed bayesian_update_general pair rasters - mu (posterior mean) sigma (posterior standard deviation) - one value per grid cell, SOLUS100’s native 100 m resolution:
code: # The real call this vignette's cached data came from: property_config <- list(id = "clay", solus_variable = "claytotal", dist = "normal") fusion_clay <- run_stage1_fusion(aoi, property_config, top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 5) fusion_clay <- unwrap_nested_rasters(   readRDS(system.file("extdata", "fusion_clay_salinas.rds", package = "soilSIM")) ) fusion_clay$dist #> [1] "normal" fusion_clay$route #> [1] "bayesian_update_general" names(fusion_clay$posterior) #> [1] "mu"    "sigma" fusion_clay$posterior$mu #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 26, 23, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 100, 100  (x, y) #> extent      : -2246800, -2244500, 1810700, 1813300  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070) #> source(s)   : memory #> name        :     lyr.1 #> min value   :  3.218861 #> max value   : 28.167618 terra::plot(fusion_clay$posterior$mu, main = "Fused posterior mean clay content (%)") terra::plot(fusion_clay$posterior$sigma, main = "Fused posterior clay uncertainty (SD)")

what: Comparing the prior, likelihood, and fused posterior
title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion: SSURGO x SOLUS100
text: plots show fusion output. see fusion actually , need look two inputs side side result. fusion_clay$prior$values fusion_clay$likelihood$values list percentile rasters (SSURGO’s SOLUS100’s, respectively) rather single raster - use source’s median (P50) representative value: run_stage1_fusion() already resampled SSURGO prior onto SOLUS100’s grid fusing, three rasters share extent/resolution combine directly c() - separate par(mfrow = ...) panels needed. use one shared color scale (range) across three panels color differences reflect real differences clay content, panel’s auto-rescaling:  SSURGO prior sparse blocky (map-unit polygons rasterized onto grid, NA delineation lines cell) SOLUS100 likelihood smooth, fully-populated 100 m grid - fused posterior inherits prior’s spatial support (cells stay NA unless inputs contribute) clay values pulled toward SOLUS100 pattern. three rasters, viewed distributions rather maps, show Bayesian update numerically:  AOI, SSURGO prior’s mass sits mostly low clay values long thin tail, SOLUS100 likelihood centered much higher (~15-25%). fused posterior sharp, narrow peak near prior’s low end - closed-form normal-normal update (bayesian_update_general) combines sources weighted relative (un)certainty, lands close prior rather likelihood, illustrating “fusion” precision-weighted compromise, simple average two inputs.
code: names(fusion_clay$prior$values)      # SSURGO percentiles #> [1] "P05" "P25" "P50" "P75" "P95" names(fusion_clay$likelihood$values) # SOLUS100 percentiles #> [1] "P025" "P50"  "P975"  prior_r <- fusion_clay$prior$values[["P50"]] likelihood_r <- fusion_clay$likelihood$values[["P50"]] posterior_r <- fusion_clay$posterior$mu shared_range <- range(   terra::minmax(prior_r), terra::minmax(likelihood_r), terra::minmax(posterior_r) )  compare_stack <- c(prior_r, likelihood_r, posterior_r) names(compare_stack) <- c("SSURGO prior", "SOLUS likelihood", "Fused posterior") terra::plot(   compare_stack,   main = c("SSURGO prior (median)", "SOLUS likelihood (median)", "Fused posterior mean"),   col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"),   range = shared_range,   nc = 3 ) prior_vals <- terra::values(prior_r, na.rm = TRUE) likelihood_vals <- terra::values(likelihood_r, na.rm = TRUE) posterior_vals <- terra::values(posterior_r, na.rm = TRUE)  clay_dist_df <- data.frame(   value = c(prior_vals, likelihood_vals, posterior_vals),   source = factor(     c(rep("SSURGO prior", length(prior_vals)),       rep("SOLUS likelihood", length(likelihood_vals)),       rep("Fused posterior", length(posterior_vals))),     levels = c("SSURGO prior", "SOLUS likelihood", "Fused posterior")   ) )  ggplot(clay_dist_df, aes(x = value, fill = source)) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   labs(     title = "Clay content distributions: prior, likelihood, and fused posterior",     x = "Clay content (%)",     y = "Density"   ) +   theme_minimal()

what: Step 2: Fuse a compositional group (clay, sand, silt jointly)
title: Multi-Source Raster Fusion: SSURGO x SOLUS100
text: Fusing clay/sand/silt independently can break sum--100 constraint texture fractions must satisfy. run_stage1_fusion_group() fuses whole compositional group jointly, isometric log-ratio (ILR) space, guaranteeing every cell’s fused clay + sand + silt sums 100: Mean fused clay/sand/silt percentages sum 100 across AOI - joint ILR fusion’s guarantee, verified real fused output rather just asserted.
code: # The real call this vignette's cached data came from: composition_groups <- list(texture = list(members = c("clay", "sand", "silt"))) property_configs <- list(   clay = list(id = "clay", solus_variable = "claytotal", composition_group = "texture"),   sand = list(id = "sand", solus_variable = "sandtotal", composition_group = "texture"),   silt = list(id = "silt", solus_variable = "silttotal", composition_group = "texture") ) fusion_texture <- run_stage1_fusion_group(   aoi, "texture", composition_groups, property_configs, top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 5 ) fusion_texture <- unwrap_nested_rasters(   readRDS(system.file("extdata", "fusion_texture_salinas.rds", package = "soilSIM")) ) names(fusion_texture) #> [1] "clay" "sand" "silt" fusion_texture$clay$dist   # "texture_ilr" for every member - not the per-property normal/beta/gamma dist #> [1] "texture_ilr" means <- sapply(fusion_texture, function(m) terra::global(m$posterior$value, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]) means #>     clay     sand     silt  #> 13.07337 59.86485 27.06177 sum(means) #> [1] 100 terra::plot(c(fusion_texture$clay$posterior$value,               fusion_texture$sand$posterior$value,               fusion_texture$silt$posterior$value),             main = c("Clay", "Sand", "Silt"))

code: # Reference only - not run in this vignette. salinas_wkt <- "POLYGON((-121.66 36.60, -121.64 36.60, -121.64 36.62, -121.66 36.62, -121.66 36.60))" aoi <- terra::project(terra::vect(salinas_wkt, crs = "epsg:4326"), "epsg:5070") property_config <- list(id = "clay", solus_variable = "claytotal", dist = "normal") fusion_clay <- run_stage1_fusion(aoi, property_config, top_depth = 0, bottom_depth = 5) fusion_clay <- unwrap_nested_rasters(   readRDS(system.file("extdata", "fusion_clay_salinas.rds", package = "soilSIM")) )  # The two inputs every function below operates on: named lists of percentile-value # SpatRasters, one list per source, plus the probabilities each percentile represents. prior_values <- fusion_clay$prior$values        # SSURGO, already resampled onto the SOLUS grid prior_probs <- fusion_clay$prior$probs lik_values <- fusion_clay$likelihood$values     # SOLUS100 lik_probs <- fusion_clay$likelihood$probs  names(prior_values); prior_probs #> [1] "P05" "P25" "P50" "P75" "P95" #> [1] 0.05 0.25 0.50 0.75 0.95 names(lik_values); lik_probs #> [1] "P025" "P50"  "P975" #> [1] 0.025 0.500 0.975 bounds <- c(0, 100)  # clay content is a percentage

title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: fit_normal_raster() simplest fit file: closed-form, exact, just three raster arithmetic operations. takes low/median/high percentile-value raster triplet probabilities low/high rasters represent, returns mu (median raster, used directly mean) sigma (back-solved tail spacing): sigma (p_hi_r - p_lo_r) / (qnorm(p_hi) - qnorm(p_lo)) - raw value spread two tail percentiles, divided many standard-normal units apart two probabilities . single elementwise expression, cost doesn’t depend many cells raster . quantile_normal_raster() evaluates fitted distribution target probability q via mu + sigma * qnorm(q):
code: fit_n <- fit_normal_raster(   p_lo_r = prior_values$P25, p50_r = prior_values$P50, p_hi_r = prior_values$P75,   p_lo = 0.25, p_hi = 0.75 ) fit_n$mu #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 26, 23, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 100, 100  (x, y) #> extent      : -2246800, -2244500, 1810700, 1813300  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : NAD83 / Conus Albers (EPSG:5070) #> source(s)   : memory #> varname     : claytotal_0_cm_l #> name        :       P50 #> min value   :  1.721668 #> max value   : 28.000607 q10 <- quantile_normal_raster(fit_n, 0.1) q90 <- quantile_normal_raster(fit_n, 0.9)  normal_stack <- c(q10, fit_n$mu, q90) names(normal_stack) <- c("Q10", "mu (=P50)", "Q90") terra::plot(normal_stack, main = c("Normal Q10", "Normal mean", "Normal Q90"),             col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"), nc = 3)

what: 2. Fitting a Beta distribution: method-of-moments vs. Newton-Raphson MLE
title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: Clay content bounded [0, 100], Normal fit ignores (Q10/Q90 rasters can dip 0 low-clay cells). Beta fit respects bounds. soilSIM ships two Beta fitters: fit_beta_mom_raster(mean_r, var_r) - closed-form method--moments, APPROXIMATE, used seed Newton-Raphson solver (intended standalone fit). takes rescaled--[0,1] mean/variance pair directly, raw percentile rasters. fit_beta_mle_newton_raster(value_rasters, bounds, n_iter = 15, eps = 1e-6) - vectorized Newton-Raphson MLE solver exploits Beta log-likelihood’s closed-form score/Hessian (digamma()/trigamma(), vectorized base-R functions) update every cell’s (alpha, beta) simultaneously per iteration, n_iter times. takes raw percentile-value rasters physical bounds directly, internally seeds fit_beta_mom_raster().  two fits’ shape-parameter rasters differ cell--cell (MoM matches first two moments; Newton MLE fits percentiles supplied ), feed quantile function shape - quantile_beta_mom_raster(fit, q) / quantile_beta_mle_newton_raster(fit, q), implemented via terra::lapp() calling stats::qbeta() per cell, since qbeta() raster-native vectorized form :  Newton-MLE fit’s Q50 tracks raw input P50 raster much closely MoM fit’s , since MLE fit five prior_values’ percentiles rather just mean/variance proxy derived two .
code: # Method-of-moments needs mean/var already rescaled to [0,1]; reuse the Normal fit above as a # cheap mean/variance proxy, rescaled by `bounds`. mean_r <- fit_n$mu / bounds[2] var_r <- (fit_n$sigma / bounds[2])^2 fit_beta_mom <- fit_beta_mom_raster(mean_r, var_r)  # The Newton-Raphson MLE fit takes the raw percentile rasters and bounds directly - it does its # own internal method-of-moments seeding. fit_beta_mle <- fit_beta_mle_newton_raster(prior_values, bounds) beta_params <- c(fit_beta_mom$alpha, fit_beta_mom$beta, fit_beta_mle$alpha, fit_beta_mle$beta) names(beta_params) <- c("alpha (MoM)", "beta (MoM)", "alpha (Newton MLE)", "beta (Newton MLE)") terra::plot(beta_params, col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "plasma"), nc = 2) q_mom <- quantile_beta_mom_raster(fit_beta_mom, 0.5) q_mle <- quantile_beta_mle_newton_raster(fit_beta_mle, 0.5)  median_compare <- c(prior_values$P50, q_mom, q_mle) names(median_compare) <- c("Raw P50 input", "Beta MoM Q50", "Beta Newton-MLE Q50") terra::plot(median_compare, col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"), nc = 3)

what: 3. Fitting a metalog distribution, and its feasibility fallback
title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: metalog family can match arbitrary number percentiles exactly via linear solve rather optimization - fit_metalog_linear_raster(value_rasters, probs, bounds, boundedness) requires number interior percentiles (excluding p = 0/p = 1, metalog’s logit transform undefined) equal number metalog terms, making fit exactly determined. Symmetric percentile sets real, sharp edge : fitting five prior_values’s percentiles (0.05/0.25/0.5/0.75/0.95 - symmetric median) makes underlying basis matrix numerically singular, since two basis columns become linearly dependent symmetric probability grid. asymmetric 4-term subset avoids : every fitted metalog valid one - metalog quantile function must monotonically increasing (equivalent non-negative density everywhere), exact linear solve gives guarantee. check_metalog_feasibility_raster() probes fit grid probabilities flags cells consecutive probes decrease:  substantial fraction cells infeasible - bug, just real consequence fitting 4 5 available percentiles family correction step . quantile_metalog_linear_with_fallback() function every real caller use instead quantile_metalog_linear_raster() directly: evaluates raw metalog quantile function, whichever cells check_metalog_feasibility_raster() flagged, blends quantile_linear_cdf_raster()’s nonparametric interpolation (evaluated full percentile set, just interior ones used fit metalog) instead:
code: ml_probs <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) ml_values <- prior_values[c("P05", "P25", "P50", "P75")] fit_ml <- fit_metalog_linear_raster(ml_values, ml_probs, bounds, boundedness = "b") length(fit_ml$a)   # one coefficient raster per term #> [1] 4 fit_ml$term #> [1] 4 infeasible <- check_metalog_feasibility_raster(fit_ml, bounds, boundedness = "b") n_infeasible <- sum(terra::values(infeasible), na.rm = TRUE) n_total <- terra::ncell(infeasible) cat(sprintf("%d / %d cells (%.0f%%) have an infeasible metalog fit\n",             n_infeasible, n_total, 100 * n_infeasible / n_total)) #> 152 / 598 cells (25%) have an infeasible metalog fit terra::plot(infeasible, main = "Infeasible metalog fit (TRUE = non-monotonic)",             col = c("grey85", "firebrick")) fallback_result <- quantile_metalog_linear_with_fallback(   fit_ml, infeasible, full_value_rasters = prior_values, full_probs = prior_probs,   q = 0.5, bounds = bounds, boundedness = "b" )  raw_metalog_q50 <- quantile_metalog_linear_raster(fit_ml, 0.5, bounds, boundedness = "b") blend_stack <- c(raw_metalog_q50, fallback_result$value, prior_values$P50) names(blend_stack) <- c("Raw metalog Q50 (no fallback)", "With fallback", "Raw input P50") terra::plot(blend_stack, col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"), nc = 3)

title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: SSURGO’s prior percentiles (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95) SOLUS100’s likelihood percentiles (0.025, 0.5, 0.975) aren’t probabilities - every fusion route needs sides share one probs vector, passing mismatched silently mis-fit whichever side’s percentiles don’t match assumed labels. align_percentile_probs() picks whichever side’s probabilities span narrower range shared target (diff(range(prior_probs)) = 0.9 vs. diff(range(lik_probs)) = 0.95, SSURGO side’s probabilities win ) reinterpolates side onto via quantile_linear_cdf_raster() - never reverse, since interpolating requires target probability fall within source’s range, narrower side always safely interpolatable wider one. reinterpolated side comes back plain (unnamed) list aligned$probs’ order, pick layer compare matching position aligned$probs rather name:  shared target happens already include 0.5 sides, P50 layer unchanged realignment - ’s tail percentiles (P05/P95 vs. P025/P975) actually get reinterpolated.
code: aligned <- align_percentile_probs(prior_values, prior_probs, lik_values, lik_probs) aligned$probs #> [1] 0.05 0.25 0.50 0.75 0.95 names(aligned$prior_value_rasters)   # unchanged (SSURGO's probs won - see below) #> [1] "P05" "P25" "P50" "P75" "P95" length(aligned$lik_value_rasters)    # SOLUS reinterpolated onto aligned$probs - unnamed list #> [1] 5 idx50 <- which(aligned$probs == 0.5) lik_compare <- c(lik_values$P50, aligned$lik_value_rasters[[idx50]]) names(lik_compare) <- c("SOLUS raw P50", "SOLUS P50 re-expressed at aligned probs") terra::plot(lik_compare, col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"), nc = 2)

title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: property_config$dist == "auto", resolve_property_dist() picks distribution family AOI’s percentile skew rather fixed per-property label - never overrides explicit (non-"auto") dist. ’s deliberately narrow: ever resolves "beta" (bounds configured), "normal", "lognormal" - never "metalog" "gamma", since distinguishing 3-point proxy isn’t considered reliable. skew proxy ((high - median) - (median - low)) / (high - low), aggregated across whole AOI (default stats::median()) rather per cell - computing per cell create map discontinuities right family boundary. explicit dist always honored untouched:
code: # With bounds configured, "auto" always resolves to "beta" regardless of skew. resolve_property_dist(list(dist = "auto", bounds = c(0, 100)), prior_values, prior_probs) #> $dist #> [1] "beta" #>  #> $dist_source #> [1] "auto" #>  #> $skew_proxy #> [1] 0.1160459  # Without bounds, it falls back to a skew-proxy test: normal if |skew| is small, lognormal if not. resolve_property_dist(list(dist = "auto"), prior_values, prior_probs) #> $dist #> [1] "normal" #>  #> $dist_source #> [1] "auto" #>  #> $skew_proxy #> [1] 0.1160459 resolve_property_dist(list(dist = "normal"), prior_values, prior_probs)$dist_source #> [1] "config"

title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: fuse_adaptive() size-adaptive engine fuse_property_adaptive() (therefore run_stage1_fusion()) delegates "normal"/"beta"/"gamma" families. picks fusion route AOI’s cell count rather requiring caller choose: threshold_cells (default 80,000), uses fully general per-cell KDE route (bayesian_update() samples drawn side’s percentiles); , much faster closed-form route built directly fitting functions Sections 1-4 (e.g. fit_normal_raster() + bayes_update_normal_normal() family = "normal"). AOI small (598 cells), naturally takes general route. Forcing threshold_cells = 0 shows alternate closed-form route exact inputs, verbose = TRUE (pipeline default quiet - deliberate log demo):  routes fuse prior/likelihood mu/sigma posterior output contract, reach differently: general route makes distributional assumption fusion step (requested output family), closed-form route fits sides Normal first (Section 1) fuses via closed-form bayes_update_normal_normal() update - much cheaper per cell, cost Normal assumption.
code: fused_general <- fuse_adaptive(   aligned$prior_value_rasters, aligned$lik_value_rasters, aligned$probs,   family = "normal", verbose = TRUE ) #> [fuse_adaptive] AOI: 598 cells (threshold: 80000) -> route: bayesian_update_general fused_closed_form <- fuse_adaptive(   aligned$prior_value_rasters, aligned$lik_value_rasters, aligned$probs,   family = "normal", threshold_cells = 0, verbose = TRUE ) #> [fuse_adaptive] AOI: 598 cells (threshold: 0) -> route: closed_form_normal route_compare <- c(fused_general$posterior$mu, fused_closed_form$posterior$mu) names(route_compare) <- c(paste0("General route (", fused_general$route, ")"),                            paste0("Closed-form route (", fused_closed_form$route, ")")) terra::plot(route_compare, col = grDevices::hcl.colors(50, "viridis"), nc = 2) route_df <- data.frame(   value = c(terra::values(fused_general$posterior$mu, na.rm = TRUE),             terra::values(fused_closed_form$posterior$mu, na.rm = TRUE)),   route = rep(c("General (KDE)", "Closed-form (Normal-Normal)"),               c(sum(!is.na(terra::values(fused_general$posterior$mu))),                 sum(!is.na(terra::values(fused_closed_form$posterior$mu))))) ) ggplot(route_df, aes(x = value, fill = route)) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   labs(title = "Fused posterior mean clay content: general vs. closed-form route",        x = "Clay content (%)", y = "Density") +   theme_minimal()

what: 8. Did fusion actually update the prior? Comparing prior, likelihood, and posterior distributions
title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: Section 7 compared two fusion routes . basic question whether fusion anything sensible relative two inputs: posterior mean clay distribution actually sit somewhere SSURGO prior SOLUS100 likelihood, sharpened combining ? fusion_clay (loaded back “Reusing real data instead fetching”) already holds real, full-pipeline answer AOI - prior/likelihood/posterior actual objects run_stage1_fusion() produced, toy aligned/fuse_adaptive() example Section 7:  posterior sits almost top prior , barely nudged toward likelihood’s much higher mean (~21%). fusion simply averaging two inputs, posterior land roughly halfway ; clearly doesn’t. exactly precision-weighted Bayesian fusion supposed one side states far uncertainty - sign likelihood ignored. Fitting side’s Normal distribution independently (fit_normal_raster() Section 1, applied whichever low/high percentile pair source actually ) makes reason concrete: SOLUS100’s raw 95% prediction interval (P025-P975) implies mean sigma roughly 5x wider SSURGO’s 5th-95th percentile spread AOI - real, known characteristic SOLUS100’s output (stated prediction intervals often wide), artifact pipeline. Since fusion weights side precision (1/sigma^2, see bayesian-updating.Rmd’s worked scalar examples exact tug--war), 5x wider sigma means roughly 25x lower precision - posterior mean (12.71) landing close prior’s mean (12.5) rather likelihood’s (20.83) fusion math exactly particular inputs, confirmed manually recomputing bayes_update_normal_normal() two independently-fit sides getting (within floating-point/per-cell alignment differences) answer pipeline’s route produced. different AOI/property two sources agree closely uncertainty show posterior pulled toward whichever side sharper, without one side lopsidedly dominating.

what: 9. A per-pixel view: prior, likelihood, and posterior at individual mapunits
title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: Section 8’s density plot pools every cell AOI one distribution per source, useful big picture hides fusion actually single location - precision weighting happens per pixel, using pixel’s prior/likelihood spread, AOI-wide average spread used . section looks handful individual pixels instead. cached object carries percentile-value rasters (prior_values, lik_values), categorical mukey raster fetch_ssurgo_mukey_raster() return - ’s direct mukey lookup pick pixels mapunit membership. proxy, SSURGO’s simulated median (prior_values$P50) close constant within mapunit differs mapunits (mapunit gets Monte Carlo simulation draws), cells sharing repeated P50 value , practice, sitting sizeable mapunit. Picking different repeated values gives handful distinct mapunit areas: four example pixels, pull mu/sigma Normal fits used - fit_prior_normal/fit_lik_normal (Section 8) prior/likelihood, fusion_clay$posterior (pipeline’s real per-cell posterior, carries mu sigma) posterior: evaluate pixel’s three Normal curves (stats::dnorm(), raster machinery needed single cell) shared x-range wide enough show three, facet pixel:  Every pixel tells qualitative story AOI-wide picture Section 8 - posterior curve sits close prior curve, barely shifted toward likelihood - precision weighting happening independently pixel , property/AOI, SOLUS’s per-pixel sigma consistently much larger SSURGO’s regardless mapunit pixel falls (visible directly pixel_df$lik_sigma vs. pixel_df$prior_sigma ). property AOI two sources’ stated uncertainty closer show pixel--pixel variation far posterior moves, including pixels likelihood dominates instead.
code: p50_all <- terra::values(prior_values$P50)[, 1] cell_ids <- which(!is.na(p50_all)) rounded <- round(p50_all[cell_ids], 1)  # Only consider values shared by several cells (a proxy for "a sizeable, distinct mapunit", # rather than a one-off simulation outlier), then spread the picks across the low-to-high clay # range so the examples aren't all pulled from one part of the AOI. freq <- table(rounded) frequent_vals <- sort(as.numeric(names(freq[freq >= 4]))) pick_idx <- round(seq(1, length(frequent_vals), length.out = 4)) picked_vals <- frequent_vals[pick_idx] example_cells <- vapply(picked_vals, function(v) cell_ids[which(rounded == v)[1]], numeric(1))  picked_vals #> [1]  1.7 10.7 14.4 28.0 extract_at <- function(r, cell) terra::values(r)[cell]  pixel_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(example_cells), function(i) {   cell <- example_cells[i]   data.frame(     pixel = sprintf("Pixel %d (mapunit-like cluster, prior P50 ~%.1f%%)", i, picked_vals[i]),     prior_mu = extract_at(fit_prior_normal$mu, cell), prior_sigma = extract_at(fit_prior_normal$sigma, cell),     lik_mu = extract_at(fit_lik_normal$mu, cell), lik_sigma = extract_at(fit_lik_normal$sigma, cell),     post_mu = extract_at(fusion_clay$posterior$mu, cell), post_sigma = extract_at(fusion_clay$posterior$sigma, cell)   ) })) pixel_df #>                                              pixel prior_mu prior_sigma lik_mu #> 1  Pixel 1 (mapunit-like cluster, prior P50 ~1.7%)  1.74080    3.081634     18 #> 2 Pixel 2 (mapunit-like cluster, prior P50 ~10.7%) 10.70449    3.508857     17 #> 3 Pixel 3 (mapunit-like cluster, prior P50 ~14.4%) 14.40415    3.725312     24 #> 4 Pixel 4 (mapunit-like cluster, prior P50 ~28.0%) 28.00061    4.541492     24 #>   lik_sigma   post_mu post_sigma #> 1  12.50023  3.723446   3.338727 #> 2  12.75534 10.353137   3.674820 #> 3  12.75534 13.498238   4.005540 #> 4  12.24512 27.030965   4.630531 curve_at_pixel <- function(row) {   x_lo <- min(row$prior_mu - 4 * row$prior_sigma, row$lik_mu - 4 * row$lik_sigma,               row$post_mu - 4 * row$post_sigma, 0)   x_hi <- max(row$prior_mu + 4 * row$prior_sigma, row$lik_mu + 4 * row$lik_sigma,               row$post_mu + 4 * row$post_sigma, 100)   x <- seq(max(x_lo, 0), min(x_hi, 100), length.out = 300)   rbind(     data.frame(pixel = row$pixel, x = x, density = stats::dnorm(x, row$prior_mu, row$prior_sigma),                source = "Prior (SSURGO)"),     data.frame(pixel = row$pixel, x = x, density = stats::dnorm(x, row$lik_mu, row$lik_sigma),                source = "Likelihood (SOLUS)"),     data.frame(pixel = row$pixel, x = x, density = stats::dnorm(x, row$post_mu, row$post_sigma),                source = "Posterior (fused)")   ) } curve_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pixel_df)), function(i) curve_at_pixel(pixel_df[i, ]))) curve_df$source <- factor(curve_df$source,   levels = c("Prior (SSURGO)", "Likelihood (SOLUS)", "Posterior (fused)"))  ggplot(curve_df, aes(x = x, y = density, color = source, fill = source)) +   geom_area(alpha = 0.3, position = "identity") +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   facet_wrap(~pixel, scales = "free_y") +   scale_color_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   scale_fill_viridis_d(name = NULL) +   labs(title = "Prior, likelihood, and posterior at four individual pixels",        subtitle = "Each panel is one pixel from a different mapunit-like cluster",        x = "Clay content (%)", y = "Density") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

what: Why SpatRasters need terra::wrap() before caching
title: Raster-Native Fitting & Fusion Internals
text: cache_set()’s docs flag real, sharp limitation: terra::SpatRaster holds external pointer -memory/-disk GDAL state, raster’s actual values. plain saveRDS()/readRDS() round-trip serializes pointer, meaningless new R session - read-back object looks like SpatRaster errors moment anything tries touch actual data: terra::wrap() converts SpatRaster PackedSpatRaster - plain, fully self-contained R object holding actual cell values - survive saveRDS()/readRDS(); terra::unwrap() converts back: Since cache_get()/cache_set() don’t wrap/unwrap automatically (every cached value raster - e.g. cached SSURGO Monte Carlo draws plain data frame), every caller caches raster values manually. Two helpers cover two result shapes pipeline actually caches: wrap_percentile_list()/unwrap_percentile_list() - fixed list(values = <SpatRasters>, probs = ) percentile shape fetch_ssurgo_percentiles()/fetch_solus_percentiles() return. wrap_nested_rasters()/unwrap_nested_rasters() - fully generic version result structures whose shape isn’t fixed form, e.g. run_stage1_fusion()’s return value, nests SpatRasters prior$values, likelihood$values, inside posterior (whose shape varies dist). recurses every list element, replacing SpatRaster finds wrapped/unwrapped equivalent leaving everything else untouched - exactly vignette’s fusion_clay object loaded, back Section “Reusing real data instead fetching”:

Sand silt derived sandtotal_r + silttotal_r + claytotal_r == 100 every row - real compositional constraint section 5 (analyze_texture_correlations()) specifically deals . Finally, three deliberate, known outliers injected detect_comprehensive_outliers() section 4 can shown actually catching , rather just asserting works: flat configuration list used throughout sections 2-4, matching run_comprehensive_correlation_analysis(), compute_stratified_correlations(), analyze_texture_correlations(), detect_comprehensive_outliers() read directly config argument (config$stratify_by_horizon, config$minimum_observations, ): Note shape get_statistical_analysis_defaults()’s return value (see section 6) - function nests keys $statistical_analysis element analyze_soil_statistics()’s internal use, standalone functions demonstrated read unnested.
code: set.seed(2026)  n <- 90 genhz <- rep(c("A", "Bt", "C"), each = n / 3)  # Known correlation structure among the latent (standardized) variables mu <- c(clay = 0, om = 0, ph = 0) Sigma <- matrix(   c(1.00,  0.55, -0.45,     0.55,  1.00, -0.30,    -0.45, -0.30,  1.00),   nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(names(mu), names(mu)) ) latent <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu = mu, Sigma = Sigma)  claytotal_r  <- pmin(pmax(25 + 8 * latent[, "clay"], 5), 60) om_r         <- pmin(pmax(2.5 + 1.2 * latent[, "om"], 0.1), 8) ph1to1h2o_r  <- pmin(pmax(6.3 + 0.6 * latent[, "ph"], 4.5), 8.3)  # Close the sand/silt/clay texture triangle to 100 sand_share   <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 0.55, 0.1), 0.15), 0.85) sandtotal_r  <- (100 - claytotal_r) * sand_share silttotal_r  <- 100 - claytotal_r - sandtotal_r  soil_synth <- data.frame(   cokey       = sprintf("synthetic-%03d", seq_len(n)),   genhz       = genhz,   hzdept_r    = rep(c(0, 20, 45), each = n / 3) + round(runif(n, -3, 3)),   claytotal_r = claytotal_r,   sandtotal_r = sandtotal_r,   silttotal_r = silttotal_r,   om_r        = om_r,   ph1to1h2o_r = ph1to1h2o_r ) outlier_idx <- c(5, 40, 85) soil_synth$claytotal_r[outlier_idx[1]]  <- 95   # implausibly high clay soil_synth$ph1to1h2o_r[outlier_idx[2]]  <- 3.0  # implausibly acidic soil_synth$om_r[outlier_idx[3]]         <- 15   # implausibly high organic matter  soil_synth[outlier_idx, c("cokey", "claytotal_r", "om_r", "ph1to1h2o_r")] #>            cokey claytotal_r      om_r ph1to1h2o_r #> 5  synthetic-005    95.00000  1.951439    5.302611 #> 40 synthetic-040    40.11579  2.941149    3.000000 #> 85 synthetic-085    24.94969 15.000000    6.289639 flat_config <- list(   minimum_observations       = 10,   handle_constant_variables  = "warn",   stratify_by_horizon        = TRUE,   include_texture_analysis   = TRUE,   outlier_methods             = c("iqr", "zscore", "modified_zscore"),   outlier_thresholds          = list(iqr = 1.5, zscore = 3, modified_zscore = 3.5),   detect_multivariate_outliers = TRUE,   mahalanobis_alpha           = 0.975 )

text: compute_property_statistics(data, properties, config) Step 7 calls internally, can called directly data frame. property computes n/missing-rate/mean/sd/min/max/ range/CV/median/quartiles/IQR finite values, 95% t-based confidence interval, skewness, kurtosis, (n <= 5000) Shapiro-Wilk normality p-value. injected clay outlier (row 5, clay = 95) good demonstration sensitive plain moment-based statistics single extreme value - compare full-data statistics computation one row excluded: single extreme value moves mean, inflates standard deviation, pushes skewness Shapiro-Wilk p-value toward “normal” - exactly symptom detect_comprehensive_outliers() (section 4) built flag reaches conclusions like one.
code: prop_stats <- compute_property_statistics(   soil_synth,   properties = c("claytotal_r", "om_r", "ph1to1h2o_r"),   config = list() ) prop_stats$claytotal_r[c("mean", "sd", "skewness", "shapiro_p")] #> $mean #> [1] 26.72292 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 10.64954 #>  #> $skewness #> [1] 2.747037 #>  #> $shapiro_p #> [1] 8.392679e-10  prop_stats_no_outlier <- compute_property_statistics(   soil_synth[-outlier_idx[1], ],   properties = "claytotal_r",   config = list() ) prop_stats_no_outlier$claytotal_r[c("mean", "sd", "skewness", "shapiro_p")] #> $mean #> [1] 25.95576 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 7.818675 #>  #> $skewness #> [1] -0.1707517 #>  #> $shapiro_p #> [1] 0.8877306

code: properties <- c("claytotal_r", "om_r", "ph1to1h2o_r")  corr_result <- run_comprehensive_correlation_analysis(   data = soil_synth,   methods = c("pearson", "spearman"),   config = flat_config,   available_properties = properties ) names(corr_result) #> [1] "matrices"   "summary"    "validation" "stratified" corr_result$matrices$pearson$matrix #>             claytotal_r       om_r ph1to1h2o_r #> claytotal_r   1.0000000  0.2416377  -0.5007475 #> om_r          0.2416377  1.0000000  -0.1679191 #> ph1to1h2o_r  -0.5007475 -0.1679191   1.0000000 corr_result$matrices$pearson$condition_number #> [1] 3.314674 cor_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(corr_result$matrices$pearson$matrix)) names(cor_df) <- c("property_1", "property_2", "correlation")  ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = property_1, y = property_2, fill = correlation)) +   geom_tile() +   geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)), color = "white", size = 3.5) +   scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Correlation") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Pearson correlation, synthetic properties", x = NULL, y = NULL) names(corr_result$texture_analysis) #> NULL names(corr_result$stratified) #> [1] "A"  "Bt" "C"

text: detect_comprehensive_outliers(data, properties, config) runs every method config$outlier_methods per property (using matching threshold config$outlier_thresholds), - config$detect_multivariate_outliers TRUE least two properties supplied - real Mahalanobis-distance multivariate check flagging outer 1 - config$mahalanobis_alpha fraction via chi-squared cutoff. univariate methods actually catch three injected outliers known row positions (5, 40, 85)? IQR method’s outliers vector indexed finite values property row order, claytotal_r (missing values) row 5’s flag can read directly: injected outlier caught IQR check property. multivariate check looks across three properties jointly via Mahalanobis distance: config$outlier_thresholds$iqr controls aggressive IQR method (multiplier IQR beyond Q1/Q3) - conventional default 1.5; doubling flag fewer, extreme points: config$mahalanobis_alpha controls multivariate flagging rate directly - chi-squared percentile used cutoff, lower value flags larger fraction points multivariate outliers:

text: Sand, silt, clay compositional data - constrained sum 100 every horizon, construction synthetic dataset (, approximately, real SSURGO data ). constraint alone forces pairwise correlations spuriously negative: clay goes , something else fixed-sum triplet go , whether two properties real relationship. analyze_texture_correlations() reports raw correlations continuity, also computes correlations isometric-log-ratio (ILR) space - transform removes sum--100 constraint - statistically defensible view compositional data: Sand clay particular tend look strongly (spuriously) anti-correlated raw space ILR space - raw view dominated closure constraint, ILR view reflects underlying relationship properties. analyze_texture_correlations() computes ilr_correlations three fractions present 4 complete rows; otherwise stays NULL raw_correlations available.
code: texture_result <- analyze_texture_correlations(   data = soil_synth,   texture_properties = c("sandtotal_r", "silttotal_r", "claytotal_r"),   methods = "pearson",   config = list() ) texture_result$raw_correlations$pearson #>             sandtotal_r silttotal_r claytotal_r #> sandtotal_r   1.0000000  -0.5224611  -0.3046480 #> silttotal_r  -0.5224611   1.0000000  -0.4325944 #> claytotal_r  -0.3046480  -0.4325944   1.0000000 texture_result$ilr_correlations$pearson #>           z1        z2 #> z1 1.0000000 0.1561642 #> z2 0.1561642 1.0000000 texture_result$note #> [1] "Raw Pearson/Spearman correlations among compositional (simplex-constrained) parts like sand/silt/clay percentages are spuriously negative due to the sum-to-100 constraint; ilr_correlations (isometric log-ratio space) avoids that artifact and is the more defensible compositional-data view."

title: Bayesian Updating: Conjugate Fusion and General Grid-KDE Fusion — bayesian_updating
text: Standalone toolkit fusing prior belief distribution likelihood (e.g. SSURGO-derived prior field-measured data), ported code_ref/brdf/bayesian_updating.R validated code_ref/reanalysis-platform/{bayes_fuse.R, reanalysis-platform-fusion.R, texture_ilr_fusion.R} bundle (raster-native; plain-vector/ scalar, since underlying math ordinary base-R arithmetic terra:: stripped ). module intentionally called anywhere monte-carlo.R. standalone, independently-tested set building blocks future "update SSURGO-derived prior observed/field data" feature - wired main Monte Carlo simulation pipeline pass. Three tiers, increasing order generality/cost: bayes_update_normal_normal() - exact, closed-form, Normal-. fuse_beta()/fuse_gamma() - exact, closed-form, -family-(family's kernel parameters simply ADD - principle bayes_update_normal_normal() uses Normal's natural parameters, applied Beta/Gamma), feasible flag documented moment-based fallback route infeasible. bayesian_update() - fully general grid-KDE Bayes' rule (shape, family, even mismatched sides), cost needing raw samples (distributional parameters) sides. fuse_bivariate_normal()/fuse_texture_group_from_triplets() extend tier 1 joint 3-part-composition ILR case (clay/sand/silt texture, whichever role order monte-carlo.R's composition_groups$texture$members configures - see distributions.R's ILR section header), since independent per-fraction fusion (e.g. three separate fuse_beta() calls) measurably breaks sum--100 (documented upstream: 10.5 percentage points realistic synthetic data).

title: Raster-Native Percentile-Based Distribution Fitting — distribution_fitting_raster
text: Fits distribution property's percentile-value rasters (e.g. SSURGO low/rep/high, SOLUS low/pred/high) pure terra::SpatRaster arithmetic /terra::app()/terra::lapp() calls vectorized base-R math functions (qnorm, qbeta, digamma/trigamma) - never per-cell optimizer, makes fast across whole rasters. Ported code_ref/reanalysis-platform/distribution_fitting_raster.R. Reuses R/distributions.R's existing metalog_basis_matrix()/ metalog_to_z()/metalog_from_z() directly rather duplicating : functions pure elementwise arithmetic (log/exp// plus building small, non-spatial coefficient matrix fixed probability grid), already work unchanged whether x/z arguments plain numerics terra::SpatRasters - confirmed dedicated smoke test file written, assumed. Status, original source: fit_normal_raster() / quantile_normal_raster() - EXACT. quantile_linear_cdf_raster() - EXACT (nonparametric fallback target). fit_beta_mom_raster() - method--moments Beta fit, APPROXIMATE relative MLE, used Newton-Raphson seed . fit_beta_mle_newton_raster() / quantile_beta_mle_newton_raster() - vectorized Newton-Raphson Beta MLE, validated (upstream) directly fitdistrplus::fitdist() (~1e-3 1e-5). fit_metalog_linear_raster() / quantile_metalog_linear_raster() / check_metalog_feasibility_raster() / quantile_metalog_linear_with_fallback() - exact linear-solve metalog reformulation (matches rmetalog::metalog() ~1e-12 fit feasible, per upstream validation), validated fallback linear_cdf cells . spline intentionally excluded (per original project's decision - accuracy relative R's splinefun(method="monoH.FC") never confirmed bit-exact).

title: soilSIM 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Data-source-agnostic simulation/fusion core: percentile-triplet arbitrary-percentile distribution fitting (fit_percentile_triplet(), simulate_from_percentiles()), correlated Monte Carlo simulation compositional (ILR) texture handling (generate_monte_carlo_realizations()), Gaussian-process depth-trend modeling (build_stratified_gp_models(), integrate_monte_carlo_with_gp()), Bayesian updating/fusion scalar (bayes_update_normal_normal() family, bayesian_update()) raster-native (fuse_property_adaptive(), fuse_texture_group()) forms. SSURGO data-source adapter: tabular acquisition (download_and_prepare_ssurgo()), cleaning (process_ssurgo_data()), infilling (process_soil_properties_comprehensive()), simulation-ready raster/percentile extraction (simulate_ssurgo_mapunit_draws()). SOLUS100 data-source adapter: raster percentile fetch (fetch_solus_percentiles()) supplying likelihood side raster fusion pipeline. Profile, component, depth simulation: component composition (sim_component_comp(), simulate_cokey_generalized()) horizon depth/thickness simulation (simulate_and_perturb_soil_profiles(), simulate_profile_depths_by_mukey()). Available water storage modeling via Van Genuchten / ROSETTA (van_genuchten(), simulate_vg_aws(), calculate_aws_df()). Statistics workflow validation/diagnostics (analyze_soil_statistics(), validate_complete_workflow(), generate_validation_report()). Four vignettes covering tabular Monte Carlo pipeline, profile/depth simulation, available water storage, multi-source raster fusion (SSURGO x SOLUS100), built real SSURGO data Sierra Nevada foothills Salinas Valley area interest.
